# CLAUDE.md

<!-- td-agent-instructions:start -->
<!-- td-agent-instructions:version=3 -->

## Working with td

td keeps task context durable across sessions. In a new context, run `td usage --new-session -q` to see current work.

Use your judgment about how much tracking a task needs. For substantive work: `td start <id>`, record progress with `td log`, hand off with `td handoff <id>`, then `td review <id>`.

Closing needs a review. Say who did it (default trusted mode; delegated/strict allow only the first):

- independent session: `td approve <id> --reason "..."`
- a sub-agent: `td approve <id> --reviewed-by "<who>"`
- you: `td approve <id> --self-review --reason "..."`

Prefer a reviewer with its own `TD_CONTEXT_ID`; never name one who did not review.

Run `td usage` or `td <command> --help`.

<!-- td-agent-instructions:end -->

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains local canonical skills (`skills/local/`), first-party project skills (`skills/owned/`), and cherry-picked third-party skills (`skills/vendor/`). Owned and vendor copies sync from their canonical upstream repos.

The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`owned/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).

## Commands

```bash
# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
make sync

# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
make sync-check

# Validate and render the repo backlog board
make kanban

# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
make marketplace

# Exercise native Claude Code + Codex marketplace add/list/install in isolated state.
make native-marketplace-smoke

# YAML-parse every skills/**/SKILL.md frontmatter. A file that fails to parse
# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
make lint-frontmatter

# All portable publish gates at once (frontmatter + marketplace + TODO format).
# CI additionally runs `make native-marketplace-smoke` with pinned CLIs.
make validate

# Install scripts/git-hooks/pre-push so `git push` runs `make validate` first.
make install-hooks

# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs

# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
  --title "Title" --description "Description"

# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines

# Start a TODO item as a td issue (td bridge; no-op without td, TODO.md unchanged)
./scripts/start-todo.sh --title "<substring>"

# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"

# Create a new local skill
cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]

# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
uv sync --extra docs
make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
make docs-build     # produces ./site/
```

## Source categories and upstream sync

- `skills/local/` — canonical skills authored in this repository.
- `skills/owned/` — first-party skills maintained in another repository owned by the maintainer. Edit the source project, then sync its distribution copy here.
- `skills/vendor/` — third-party upstream skills; preserve upstream content.

`vendor.yaml` remains the shared sync manifest. `collection: owned` selects
`skills/owned/`; an omitted collection defaults to `vendor`. Both support `series`,
`license_path`, `frozen`, and upstream commit tracking. Add published owned sources
with `scripts/add-vendor.sh --owned <owner/repo/path>`. A cross-repository symlink
cannot serve as a distributable copy.

An unpublished owned skill may use `pending_upstream: true`. Its bootstrap mirror
contains real files but claims no remote SHA; routine sync/check preserves it.
After publishing the canonical source, run `scripts/sync-vendor.sh --activate <name>`.
Only a successful sync clears pending. See [owned workflow](docs/workflows/adding-owned-skills.md).

## Vendor System (also used for owned sources)

- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir

Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.

`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.

Active series in this repo:
- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)

### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed

Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:

- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
  `skills@1.5.24` writes `skills-lock.json`, but a renamed skill is still a
  different install ID; review the lock and explicitly reinstall the new name.
- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.

Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.

## Marketplace Catalog

`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
for the full mechanism.

When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>`, `./owned/<name>`, or
`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).

**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
within-group caveat in
[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).

## SKILL.md Format

Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.

## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)

The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.

`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.

To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:

```bash
# Skip the symlinks at creation time
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>

# …or remove them afterward
rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
```

## Project Memory Workflow

<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance -->
### Issue-driven workflow (GitHub)

This project uses GitHub Issues as the canonical shared backlog, not as a
mandatory record of every change. The `forge-native-dev` skill provides the
scripts below; apply its scope gate before publishing any new record.

| Information | Lives in | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Bounded experiment, small fix, same-session evaluation | Conversation + diff; optional local note | Avoid unnecessary tracking overhead |
| Durable actionable backlog, blockers, shared ownership | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/issues) | Searchable, assignable, cross-linkable |
| Open questions needing ongoing asynchronous input | [Discussions](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/discussions) | Shared deliberation, not a research archive |
| Research docs, trade-off analysis | `backlog/` | Durable, diffable; no Discussion required |
| Past traps, debugging knowledge | `pitfalls/` | Grep-able by symptom, portable |
| Backlog visualization | [Project board](https://github.com/users/daviddwlee84/projects/11) | Built-in to the forge |
| Historical record | `TODO.md` `## Done` section | In git |

**Right-size tracking.** Default to local work for bounded experiments and
small changes. Create an external record only when explicitly requested or when
outstanding work needs durable backlog/ownership/dependency tracking or shared
input. Another session or a long research document alone does not require it;
use td/local notes for execution context where sufficient.

Reuse an existing relevant Issue/Discussion before creating one. "Research",
"maybe later", and "先記下來" do not automatically mean publish a Discussion or
Issue. Do not create both merely because a task includes research and code, or
retrospectively open tickets for completed small work. Local branches/worktrees
and directly requested PRs do not require a synthetic Issue number.

**Tracked work lifecycle (when an Issue is warranted):**
1. Start: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh start <issue-number>`
2. Work in the worktree, commit conventionally
3. Finish: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh finish <issue-number>`
4. After merge: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-cleanup.sh`

**Check for work:** `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-issue.sh list --assignee @me`

**Dashboard:** `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-status.sh`

**PRs are review gates.** Link the existing Issue when there is one; a bounded
change may go directly to a requested PR without a prerequisite ticket. Keep
normal review/publication permissions. Default merge strategy: **squash and merge**.
<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance (end) -->

### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`

`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
own conventions). It has four subareas:

- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
  status / license / last_verified`).

Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |

Status changes trigger existing scripts:
`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).

Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.

### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`

When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:

1. The verbatim symptom or error text
2. The root cause
3. The workaround
4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it

Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
the explanation they do not know yet.

Author: David Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Oct 28 18:45:20 2026 +0800

    feat(skills): add superproject-workspace for submodule superprojects (#34)
    
    * feat(skills): add superproject-workspace for submodule superprojects
    
    A gitlink records a commit, not a branch, so submodule superprojects drift
    by design. Add a skill that makes drift visible and moves pointers by a
    per-child policy stored as extra .gitmodules keys (x-policy track|pin|lazy,
    x-bump pr|direct|manual, x-tier).
    
    - scripts/superproject.py (PEP 723, stdlib): status, init, pull, bump,
      preflight, worktree add|list|remove, audit, adopt, ci-plan
    - bump is atomic: one outer commit with --submodule=log, refusing dirty or
      unpushed children (track: on origin/<branch>; pin: on any origin branch)
    - child worktrees under .worktrees/<child-path>/<branch>; pins branch from
      their recorded gitlink
    - assets: justfile recipes, AGENTS.md block, scheduled bump workflow
      (pr on chore/submodule-bump or direct), child dispatch, pre-commit hook
    - references: decision guide, policies, worktrees, CI bump, agent entry,
      gotchas, case patterns
    - 17 unittest cases against local bare-repo fixtures
    - docs pages (en + zh-TW), marketplace version-control group, cross-links
      from git-workflow and forge-native-dev, adoption backlog note
    
    Closes #33
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * refactor(superproject-workspace): reference the installed CLI instead of vendoring it
    
    Copying superproject.py into every superproject froze it at adoption time,
    so the tool itself would drift across repos exactly like gitlinks do.
    
    - justfile recipes, pre-commit hook, and bump workflow resolve the CLI:
      $SUPERPROJECT_CLI > vendored scripts/superproject.py (opt-in) > project
      skill install > ~/.agents/skills install > GitHub raw at
      $SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF (default main); `just sub-which` shows the winner
    - adopt no longer copies the CLI; --vendor-cli is opt-in for offline use
    - audit flags tool drift: managed-block-stale and vendored-cli-stale
    - new sub-adopt recipe to refresh managed blocks after a skill update
    - docs: `sp` shorthand, CI ref pinning trade-off; CLI version 0.2.0
    
    Refs #33
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./skills/local/superproject-workspace/SKILL.md`

````text
1	---
2	name: superproject-workspace
3	description: Keep a git-submodule superproject (umbrella repo / multi-repo workspace used as one agent entry point) from drifting — per-submodule policy in .gitmodules (track / pin / lazy), lag and drift status, safe fast-forward, preflighted gitlink bumps in one outer commit, scheduled bump PRs, child worktrees, and audit/adopt for existing superprojects. Use when a repo has .gitmodules and the user asks to update/sync submodules, bump pointers, work on a branch inside a submodule, add a repo to the workspace, or asks "monorepo vs submodules", incl. "submodule 落後 / 更新 submodule / 拉到 latest main".
4	---
5	
6	# superproject-workspace
7	
8	A superproject is a repo whose job is to hold other repos as git submodules,
9	so that one agent session gets every repo's context and edit access while each
10	repo keeps its own remote, PRs, and release cycle. The cost: **a gitlink
11	records a commit, not a branch.** Children merge PRs and the superproject
12	silently falls behind; checkouts end up detached, dirty, or on stray branches;
13	pointers reference commits nobody pushed. Drift is the default, not a bug.
14	
15	This skill makes drift **visible** and moves pointers **by policy**, with one
16	CLI (`scripts/superproject.py`, stdlib Python ≥3.10, PEP 723). Every
17	superproject **references** the installed skill's CLI instead of copying it,
18	so `npx skills update` upgrades all of them at once. Otherwise the tool itself
19	would drift the same way the gitlinks do.
20	
21	## When to use
22	
23	- The repo has `.gitmodules` and the user wants to update, sync, or "pull latest" children.
24	- After a child PR merges, to move the superproject pointer.
25	- Starting feature work inside a child repo from the superproject.
26	- Adding a repo to a workspace, or deciding *how* to bring repos together (see `references/decision-guide.md`).
27	- Auditing or upgrading an older superproject that has ad-hoc recipes.
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- Ordinary single-repo git work: use `git-workflow`.
32	- Issue/PR lifecycle inside one child: use that child's own workflow (`forge-native-dev`, etc.).
33	- The repos are not submodules (manifest + gitignored clones, or Project add-dir): only the decision guide applies.
34	
35	## The policy model
36	
37	Each child declares its policy as extra keys in `.gitmodules`. Git ignores keys
38	it does not know, so these keys live next to `path` and `url` and cannot fall
39	out of sync with them.
40	
41	```ini
42	[submodule "app"]
43	    path = app
44	    url = git@github.com:me/app.git
45	    branch = main        # tracking branch (native key; unset -> child's origin/HEAD)
46	    x-policy = track     # track | pin | lazy
47	    x-bump = pr          # pr | direct | manual   (only for track)
48	    x-tier = core        # free-form grouping for --tier selection
49	    update = none        # lazy only: plain `git submodule update --init` skips it
50	```
51	
52	| Policy | Means | Pointer moves | Initialized |
53	|---|---|---|---|
54	| `track` | "Be at the latest `origin/<branch>`" | `pull` (ff-only), then `bump`; may be automated (`x-bump`) | by default |
55	| `pin` | "Be at a known baseline" (production, a release, a reproduction) | only `bump --reason "..."` | by default |
56	| `lazy` | "Reference material; fetch only when a task needs it" | only `bump --reason` | only when named |
57	| unset | treated as `pin`; `audit` warns | | |
58	
59	Bump modes for `track`: `pr` means scheduled CI opens one PR on
60	`chore/submodule-bump`. `direct` means CI commits to the default branch after
61	preflight. `manual` means a human or agent runs `bump`. An umbrella where every
62	child follows main is simply "everything `track`". A workspace hub mixes core
63	`pin`s with `lazy` references. Details and example configs are in
64	`references/policies.md`.
65	
66	## Workflow
67	
68	Below, `sp` means `uv run --script <skill-dir>/scripts/superproject.py`. For a
69	global install, `<skill-dir>` is `~/.agents/skills/superproject-workspace`.
70	After `adopt`, the same commands are available as `just sub-*` recipes. They
71	resolve the CLI in this order, first match wins:
72	
73	1. `$SUPERPROJECT_CLI`
74	2. a vendored `scripts/superproject.py` (opt-in)
75	3. the project skill install `.agents/skills/...`
76	4. the global install `~/.agents/skills/...`
77	5. GitHub raw at `$SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF` (default `main`)
78	
79	`just sub-which` prints which one won. Every command takes `--json`. Mutating
80	commands take `--dry-run`.
81	
82	### 1. Look first
83	
84	```bash
85	sp status --fetch   # policy, lag, drift, dirty, worktrees
86	sp audit            # findings + exact fix commands
87	```
88	
89	Without `--fetch`, lag is computed against stale remote refs. Never report
90	"up to date" without fetching.
91	
92	### 2. Get a child you need
93	
94	```bash
95	sp init                 # all non-lazy, uninitialized children
96	sp init some-reference  # a lazy child, by name/path/basename
97	```
98	
99	`init` never touches an already-initialized checkout and does not recurse
100	unless you pass `--recursive`. Initialization is not a way to update.
101	
102	### 3. Develop inside a child: use a child worktree
103	
104	```bash
105	sp worktree add app feat/login
106	# -> .worktrees/app/feat-login  (gitignored; branch from origin/main for track,
107	#    from the recorded gitlink for pin, so fixes start from the baseline)
108	```
109	
110	Work, commit, push, and open the PR **in the child's own repo and workflow**.
111	The submodule checkout itself stays on its branch or pin. Clean up with
112	`worktree list` (shows merged ones) and `worktree remove app feat/login --delete-branch`.
113	Do not create worktrees of the superproject for this; see `references/worktrees.md`.
114	
115	### 4. Move pointers: inside-out, one outer commit
116	
117	```bash
118	sp pull                 # ff track children (checkout only)
119	sp bump --all-track --commit
120	sp bump lib --reason "prod baseline v2.3" --commit   # pin/lazy
121	```
122	
123	`bump` refuses the whole set if any child is dirty or its commit is not
124	pushed. For a `track` child, "pushed" means on `origin/<branch>`; for a pin, it
125	means on any origin branch. One cross-repo change gets one outer commit. The
126	commit body contains each range and the `--submodule=log` summary. Pass
127	`--partial` only when the user explicitly accepts splitting.
128	
129	### 5. Guard every outer commit
130	
131	```bash
132	sp preflight   # also installed as a pre-commit hook by adopt --with-hook
133	```
134	
135	### 6. Adopt an existing superproject
136	
137	```bash
138	uv run --script <skill>/scripts/superproject.py audit --root ../old-super
139	uv run --script <skill>/scripts/superproject.py adopt --root ../old-super --dry-run \
140	    --policy-default pin --set app=track:pr --set docs-ref=lazy
141	```
142	
143	`adopt` writes policy keys, but only where they are missing or named by
144	`--set`. It also upserts a marker-delimited AGENTS.md block and `sub-*`
145	justfile recipes, adds `.worktrees/` to `.gitignore`, and sets local git
146	config:
147	- `diff.submodule=log`
148	- `status.submoduleSummary=true`
149	- `push.recurseSubmodules=check`
150	
151	Opt in to `--with-ci` and `--with-hook`. It does **not** copy the CLI. Pass
152	`--vendor-cli` only for offline or air-gapped superprojects, and accept that
153	the copy stops receiving fixes. It is idempotent: rerun it (`just sub-adopt`)
154	after a skill update to refresh the managed blocks. `audit` reports
155	`managed-block-stale` and `vendored-cli-stale` when the tool itself has
156	drifted. Review `git diff`
157	before committing, and pick policies with the user. The default
158	`--policy-default pin` is deliberately conservative.
159	
160	## Available scripts
161	
162	- **`scripts/superproject.py`**: `status | init | pull | bump | preflight | worktree add|list|remove | audit | adopt | ci-plan`.
163	  - Common flags: `--root`, `--json`, `--dry-run` (mutating commands).
164	  - Selection: positional names (name, path, or basename), `--tier`, `--policy`, `--mode`.
165	  - Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 refused or check failed, 2 usage error. Diagnostics go to stderr.
166	
167	## Bundled assets
168	
169	- `assets/justfile.snippet`: thin `sub-*` recipes (marker block; `adopt` upserts it).
170	- `assets/agents-block.md.template`: the cross-repo contract for agents (marker block).
171	- `assets/superproject-bump.yml`: scheduled, `workflow_dispatch`, and `repository_dispatch` bump workflow (`pr` and `direct`).
172	- `assets/child-dispatch.yml`: optional; goes in a child repo to request an immediate bump on push to main.
173	- `assets/pre-commit-hook.sh`: runs `preflight`.
174	
175	The recipes, hook, and workflow all use the same CLI resolution. CI pins
176	the version with the `SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF` repository variable (a tag or
177	SHA).
178	
179	## Reference files
180	
181	- `references/decision-guide.md`: read when choosing between a real monorepo, a submodule superproject, a manifest with clones, or Project add-dir.
182	- `references/policies.md`: read when assigning policies, or for umbrella vs hub examples.
183	- `references/worktrees.md`: read before any branch work inside a child.
184	- `references/ci-bump.md`: read when enabling `pr`/`direct` automation, private or GitLab children, or dispatch.
185	- `references/agent-entry.md`: read when setting up the superproject as an agent entry point (AGENTS.md layering, Claude/Codex Projects, root context).
186	- `references/gotchas.md`: read when git prints something surprising about a submodule.
187	- `references/case-patterns.md`: read when adopting; lists lessons from real umbrella and hub superprojects.
188	
189	## Gotchas
190	
191	- **Don't copy the CLI into each superproject.** Copies freeze at adoption
192	  time and silently diverge across repos. Reference the installed skill; vendor
193	  only for offline use, and let `audit` flag stale copies.
194	- **`git pull` in the superproject does not update children.** It moves gitlinks and leaves checkouts behind, which then shows as `modified: app (new commits)`. Run `status`, then decide whether to `bump` (keep the checkout) or `git submodule update -- app` (discard and go back to the gitlink).
195	- **`git submodule update` detaches HEAD** and can strand local commits that are not on a branch. `pull` refuses "detached commit not on origin/<branch>" for this reason; save the commit to a branch first.
196	- **"Latest" never means resetting pins.** A pinned child may legitimately be behind or sit on a release branch. `audit` reports this as info, not an error.
197	- **Never bump to an unpushed child commit.** A fresh clone would then fail with `fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref`. `bump` and `preflight` block this, and `push.recurseSubmodules=check` blocks the outer push.
198	- **A submodule name is not its path.** One example is `[submodule "dotfiles"] path = dotfiles-unix`. Policy keys use the *name*. The CLI accepts either.
199	- **CI PRs opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other workflows.** Run the gates inside the bump job, or use a PAT or GitHub App token (`references/ci-bump.md`).
200	- **After a child's URL changes in `.gitmodules`**, existing clones keep the old URL until `git submodule sync`. `init` syncs, and `audit` flags `url-unsynced`.
201
````

20	=== skills/local/superproject-workspace/references/agent-entry.md
21	     1	# The superproject as an agent entry point
22	     2	
23	     3	## Instruction layering
24	     4	
25	     5	- **Outer `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`** governs *cross-repo* work only. Keep the
26	     6	  `adopt` block in it (commit inside-out, one outer commit, worktrees, pins).
27	     7	  Add a short map of which child owns what.
28	     8	- **Each child's `AGENTS.md`** stays authoritative inside that child. Agents
29	     9	  must read it before editing there; say so explicitly in the outer file.
30	    10	  Claude Code loads nested `CLAUDE.md` files on demand when it touches files
31	    11	  in that directory; Codex reads `AGENTS.md` along the path. Neither harness
32	    12	  guarantees this for files the agent only greps.
33	    13	- Do not copy child instructions upward; link to them. Copies drift exactly
34	    14	  like gitlinks do.
35	    15	
36	    16	## Root context that earns its place
37	    17	
38	    18	What makes a superproject better than "a folder of clones" is content that
39	    19	belongs to *no single child*:
40	    20	
41	    21	- a cross-repo context graph (entities, relations, dated observations)
42	    22	- `pitfalls/` for traps that span repos (version skew, protocol mismatches)
43	    23	- runbooks that orchestrate several children (deploy, parity checks)
44	    24	- agent session history (SpecStory), since cross-repo sessions have no other home
45	    25	
46	    26	Record facts with the gitlink SHA or date they were observed against. A note
47	    27	like "service X does Y" goes stale when the pointer moves.
48	    28	
49	    29	## Claude / Codex Projects and add-dir
50	    30	
51	    31	A Project or `--add-dir` gives similar context breadth without submodules,
52	    32	but provides no versioned snapshot and no home for root content. Use them for
53	    33	one-off reads; use the superproject when the combination itself, or the root
54	    34	knowledge, matters.
55	    35	
56	    36	## Session start checklist (put in AGENTS.md)
57	    37	
58	    38	1. `sp status --fetch`
59	    39	2. Read the target child's AGENTS.md.
60	    40	3. Branch work goes in `worktree add`, never in the submodule checkout.
61	=== skills/local/superproject-workspace/references/case-patterns.md
62	     1	# Case patterns from real superprojects
63	     2	
64	     3	Two production superprojects informed this skill. Their lessons, with private
65	     4	details removed:
66	     5	
67	     6	## Umbrella: parallel platform repos, all following main
68	     7	
69	     8	Five equally owned repos (one per OS or platform), unified by an outer repo
70	     9	whose purpose is UX parity across them. No product is built in the outer repo.
71	    10	
72	    11	What worked:
73	    12	- **Inside-out commits** with a preflight that the inner HEAD is reachable
74	    13	  from `origin/main` before the gitlink is staged. This is the origin of
75	    14	  `bump`/`preflight`.
76	    15	- **ff-only "pull main"** that refuses diverged branches and detached commits
77	    16	  not on main. This is the origin of `pull`'s refusal list.
78	    17	- **"One cross-repo change gets one outer commit"**, reviewed with
79	    18	  `git diff --cached --submodule=log`.
80	    19	- Deploy recipes pin the tool to a specific child checkout, never to an
81	    20	  implicit default.
82	    21	
83	    22	What drifted:
84	    23	- No scheduled bump, so children ran 9+ commits ahead of the recorded pointer
85	    24	  between maintenance sessions. Fix: `x-bump = pr`.
86	    25	- Every child path was hard-coded into a dozen recipes, written twice (POSIX
87	    26	  sh and PowerShell). Adding a sixth child meant editing all of them, and one
88	    27	  pathspec still named a path that no longer existed. Fix: policy-driven
89	    28	  recipes and one cross-platform CLI.
90	    29	
91	    30	## Workspace hub: tiered children, pins, and root knowledge
92	    31	
93	    32	About 20 children across GitHub and GitLab, org and personal, grouped
94	    33	`core / personal / references`. The outer repo holds a structured context
95	    34	graph (entities, relations, dated observations), runbooks, and agent history.
96	    35	
97	    36	What worked:
98	    37	- **Tiers with on-demand init**: references are fetched only when a task
99	    38	  needs them, and never recursively. This is the origin of `lazy` + `update = none`.
100	    39	- **"Latest is not reset-to-main"**: production diagnosis reads the deployed
101	    40	  revision rather than upstream tip. This is the origin of `pin`.
102	    41	- **Root context** that cites the revisions it observed.
103	    42	
104	    43	What drifted:
105	    44	- No rule for when a core pin moves forward, and no lag report. Some
106	    45	  checkouts sat on feature branches, dirty, while their gitlinks pointed at
107	    46	  commits on no origin branch at all. Fix: `status`, `audit`, explicit
108	    47	  `pin`/`track`.
109	    48	- External worktrees outside the entry point. Fix: `.worktrees/<child>/<branch>`.
110	    49	- A bespoke init script (tiers and selection) that the policy keys plus `init --tier` now replace.
111	    50	
112	    51	## Older, less agentic superprojects
113	    52	
114	    53	These typically have `.gitmodules` and nothing else: no policy, no AGENTS.md,
115	    54	and READMEs telling humans to run `git submodule update --remote`. Run `audit`,
116	    55	then `adopt --dry-run --policy-default pin`, agree the policies with the
117	    56	owner, then `adopt` and commit.
118	=== skills/local/superproject-workspace/references/ci-bump.md
119	     1	# Automated bumps in CI
120	     2	
121	     3	`adopt --with-ci` installs `.github/workflows/superproject-bump.yml`:
122	     4	
123	     5	1. `ci-plan --json` lists `track` children with `x-bump` `pr` or `direct`.
124	     6	   Use `--only` to select one child, as `workflow_dispatch` and
125	     7	   `repository_dispatch` do.
126	     8	2. `init` checks out just those children.
127	     9	3. **direct:** `pull` → `bump --commit` → push to the default branch.
128	    10	4. **pr:** switch to the fixed branch `chore/submodule-bump` → `pull` →
129	    11	   `bump --commit` → force-push → open the PR once (later runs update it).
130	    12	
131	    13	The job fails, with a red run, when `pull` or `bump` refuses. Typical causes:
132	    14	a child's history was rewritten (diverged), or the gitlink points at a
133	    15	deleted commit. Fix those by hand.
134	    16	
135	    17	## Which CLI version CI runs
136	    18	
137	    19	The workflow uses `scripts/superproject.py` if the repo vendored one
138	    20	(`adopt --vendor-cli`). Otherwise it runs the skill's CLI straight from GitHub
139	    21	raw at the `SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF` repository variable, defaulting to `main`:
140	    22	
141	    23	- **`main`**: every superproject picks up fixes automatically. You trust the
142	    24	  skill repo's main branch with a job that has `contents: write`.
143	    25	- **tag or SHA**: reproducible and reviewed. Moving it is one variable change
144	    26	  per repo. Use this for superprojects that guard production.
145	    27	
146	    28	## Credentials
147	    29	
148	    30	| Children | Secret | Notes |
149	    31	|---|---|---|
150	    32	| Public | none | `GITHUB_TOKEN` can push the outer repo |
151	    33	| Private on GitHub | `SUBMODULE_TOKEN` | Fine-grained PAT (or GitHub App token) with *Contents: read* on each child. The workflow rewrites `git@github.com:` and `https://github.com/` to use it. |
152	    34	| GitLab | `GITLAB_TOKEN` | Project or group access token with `read_repository`; rewritten the same way |
153	    35	| Other forges | add another `insteadOf` line | |
154	    36	
155	    37	SSH URLs in `.gitmodules` are fine for humans. The `insteadOf` rewrite maps
156	    38	them to HTTPS in CI.
157	    39	
158	    40	## Gotchas
159	    41	
160	    42	- **PRs created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `pull_request` workflows.**
161	    43	  Either run validation in the bump job itself, or create the PR with a PAT or
162	    44	  App token.
163	    45	- **`direct` with branch protection** needs a token that may bypass it, or
164	    46	  else use `pr`.
165	    47	- **Schedule vs dispatch:** a schedule is simple and needs no child changes.
166	    48	  For near-immediate bumps, add `assets/child-dispatch.yml` to each child.
167	    49	  This needs a PAT with *Contents: write* on the superproject, because
168	    50	  `repository_dispatch` requires it.
169	    51	- **GitLab-hosted superprojects:** port the same steps to `.gitlab-ci.yml`
170	    52	  with a scheduled pipeline and `glab mr create`. The CLI is forge-agnostic.
171	=== skills/local/superproject-workspace/references/decision-guide.md
172	     1	# Decision guide: how to bring repos together for an agent
173	     2	
174	     3	Goal: one agent entry point with context (and usually edit access) across
175	     4	several repos, without coupling their histories, CI, or release cycles more
176	     5	than necessary.
177	     6	
178	     7	| Option | What it is | Version snapshot of the set? | Drift problem | Best when |
179	     8	|---|---|---|---|---|
180	     9	| **Real monorepo** | One repo, one history | Yes (every commit) | None | Repos ship together, share CI and owners, and change atomically |
181	    10	| **Submodule superproject** (this skill) | Outer repo pins each child by gitlink | Yes (outer commit = exact set) | Yes, so manage it by policy | Repos are independent but you need reproducible "this set worked together" points, or the outer repo carries shared knowledge (agent history, context, runbooks) |
182	    11	| **Manifest + gitignored clones** | `repos.yaml` + a clone/update script (`mani`, `gita`, `repo`, `meta`, or 20 lines of shell) | No (unless you record SHAs yourself) | None: each clone is just "whatever is checked out" | You only need co-location for context; no one asks "which versions went together?" |
183	    12	| **Project / add-dir** (Claude Code `--add-dir`, Codex or Claude Projects) | Agent session spans several existing checkouts | No | None | Ad-hoc, personal, short-lived cross-repo tasks |
184	    13	
185	    14	## Questions that decide it
186	    15	
187	    16	1. **Do you need to reproduce a combination later?** Examples: "what did prod
188	    17	   run", "the umbrella state that passed parity checks". If yes, choose
189	    18	   submodules, or a monorepo if the repos are tightly coupled.
190	    19	2. **Does the outer repo have content of its own?** Examples: AGENTS.md, a
191	    20	   cross-repo `context/` graph, `pitfalls/`, SpecStory history, deployment
192	    21	   runbooks. If yes, a superproject gives that content a versioned home, and
193	    22	   the gitlinks date each note against concrete child versions.
194	    23	3. **Do children have different owners, visibility, or forges** (GitHub +
195	    24	   GitLab, personal + org)? Then rule out a monorepo; submodules or a manifest
196	    25	   both work.
197	    26	4. **Will you remember to bump?** If not, either automate it (`x-bump = pr` or
198	    27	   `direct`) or choose a manifest. A superproject with no bumping is the worst
199	    28	   option: it pins by accident.
200	    29	
201	    30	## Hybrid that works well
202	    31	
203	    32	Use a superproject for the **core** set (`track` or `pin`), and mark
204	    33	reference material `lazy` so a fresh clone stays small. Truly throwaway reads
205	    34	don't need a submodule at all: use add-dir for those.
206	=== skills/local/superproject-workspace/references/gotchas.md
207	     1	# Submodule gotchas, by symptom
208	     2	
209	     3	### `modified: app (new commits)` after `git pull`
210	     4	The outer pull moved the gitlink; the child checkout stayed where it was (or
211	     5	the reverse: you moved the child). Inspect with `status`. To keep the
212	     6	checkout, run `bump app`. To discard it, run `git submodule update -- app`.
213	     7	Setting `git config submodule.recurse true` makes `pull`/`checkout` update
214	     8	children automatically. That is convenient for consumers, but surprising
215	     9	while you develop in children, so leave it off in maintainer checkouts.
216	    10	
217	    11	### `HEAD detached at 1a2b3c4` inside a child
218	    12	This is normal after `git submodule update`. Commits made in this state belong
219	    13	to no branch and are easily lost. Save them first:
220	    14	`git switch -c rescue/<topic>`. `pull` refuses to move a detached commit that
221	    15	is not on `origin/<branch>`.
222	    16	
223	    17	### `fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref <sha>` / `Fetched in submodule path 'x', but it did not contain <sha>`
224	    18	Someone recorded a gitlink to a commit that was never pushed, or was
225	    19	force-pushed away. Push it if it still exists locally. Otherwise move the
226	    20	pointer to a pushed commit. Prevent it with `preflight` (pre-commit) and
227	    21	`push.recurseSubmodules=check`.
228	    22	
229	    23	### `Submodule 'x' could not be updated` / `update = none` surprises
230	    24	`update = none` in `.gitmodules` makes plain `git submodule update --init`
231	    25	skip the child. That is intended for `lazy` children. `init <name>` passes
232	    26	`--checkout` to override it for that one call.
233	    27	
234	    28	### Clone still uses the old URL after `.gitmodules` changed
235	    29	`.git/config` caches submodule URLs at init time. Run
236	    30	`git submodule sync -- <path>`; `audit` reports `url-unsynced`.
237	    31	
238	    32	### Nested submodules fail to clone (private descendants)
239	    33	`--recursive` pulls in every descendant, including private or unrecoverable
240	    34	ones. The CLI never recurses unless asked. Initialize nested children
241	    35	explicitly, only when the task needs them.
242	    36	
243	    37	### Branch named in `.gitmodules` doesn't exist (`origin/main missing`)
244	    38	The child uses `master`, or a release branch. Set `branch` explicitly. If
245	    39	`branch` is unset, the CLI uses the child's `origin/HEAD`.
246	    40	
247	    41	### `git status` shows `.worktrees/` as untracked
248	    42	Add `.worktrees/` to `.gitignore`. `worktree add` and `adopt` do this
249	    43	automatically.
250	=== skills/local/superproject-workspace/references/policies.md
251	     1	# Policies
252	     2	
253	     3	Keys live in `.gitmodules` under the submodule's **name** (not path):
254	     4	
255	     5	```bash
256	     6	git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.x-policy track   # track | pin | lazy
257	     7	git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.x-bump pr        # pr | direct | manual
258	     8	git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.x-tier core
259	     9	git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.branch main      # native git key
260	    10	git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.update none      # lazy children
261	    11	```
262	    12	
263	    13	## Choosing a policy
264	    14	
265	    15	| Question about the child | Policy |
266	    16	|---|---|
267	    17	| You own it and the superproject should follow its main line | `track` |
268	    18	| A specific version matters (deployed, released, a known-good reproduction) | `pin` |
269	    19	| It's reference reading, a third-party upstream, or rarely used | `lazy` |
270	    20	| You don't know yet | leave unset (treated as `pin`; `audit` reminds you) |
271	    21	
272	    22	## Choosing a bump mode (`track` only)
273	    23	
274	    24	| Mode | Use when | Risk |
275	    25	|---|---|---|
276	    26	| `manual` | Default. Bumps happen deliberately, alongside cross-repo work | Falls behind if nobody looks; `audit` shows `behind` |
277	    27	| `pr` | You want a reviewable stream of updates (umbrellas, docs hubs) | PR noise; needs CI token for private children |
278	    28	| `direct` | The pointer carries no review value (pure aggregation, notes repos) | A broken child lands in the outer default branch without review |
279	    29	
280	    30	`direct` still runs preflight: a commit that is not reachable from
281	    31	`origin/<branch>` is never recorded.
282	    32	
283	    33	## Example: umbrella (every child follows main)
284	    34	
285	    35	Parallel, equally owned repos, such as per-platform dotfiles:
286	    36	
287	    37	```ini
288	    38	[submodule "dotfiles-unix"]
289	    39	    path = dotfiles-unix
290	    40	    url = git@github.com:me/dotfiles.git
291	    41	    branch = main
292	    42	    x-policy = track
293	    43	    x-bump = pr
294	    44	[submodule "dotfiles-windows"]
295	    45	    path = dotfiles-windows
296	    46	    url = git@github.com:me/dotfiles-windows.git

302	    52	## Example: workspace hub (tiers)
303	    53	
304	    54	```ini
305	    55	[submodule "submodules/engine"]
306	    56	    path = submodules/engine
307	    57	    url = https://github.com/org/engine.git
308	    58	    branch = release/2.x       # the baseline the pin follows
309	    59	    x-policy = pin
310	    60	    x-tier = core
311	    61	[submodule "submodules/dashboard"]
312	    62	    path = submodules/dashboard
313	    63	    url = https://github.com/org/dashboard.git
314	    64	    branch = main
315	    65	    x-policy = track
316	    66	    x-bump = manual
317	    67	    x-tier = core
318	    68	[submodule "submodules/references/someone/paper-code"]
319	    69	    path = submodules/references/someone/paper-code
320	    70	    url = https://github.com/someone/paper-code.git
321	    71	    x-policy = lazy
322	    72	    x-tier = reference
323	    73	    update = none
324	    74	```
325	    75	
326	    76	`init --tier reference` fetches all references at once. `status --tier core`
327	    77	narrows the report.
328	    78	
329	    79	## Pins and branches
330	    80	
331	    81	For a pin, `branch` names the line the pin follows, such as a release branch.
332	    82	That is what `status` measures lag against. The safety rule for pins is
333	    83	weaker than for track: the recorded commit must be on **some** origin branch,
334	    84	so a fresh clone can check it out. It does not have to be on `branch`.
335	=== skills/local/superproject-workspace/references/worktrees.md
336	     1	# Worktrees in a superproject
337	     2	
338	     3	## Rule
339	     4	
340	     5	Feature work in a child happens in a **worktree of the child**, placed inside
341	     6	the superproject at `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch-slug>` (gitignored):
342	     7	
343	     8	```bash
344	     9	sp worktree add <child> <branch> [--base REV]
345	    10	sp worktree list
346	    11	sp worktree remove <child> <branch> --delete-branch
347	    12	```
348	    13	
349	    14	The submodule checkout itself stays on its tracked branch, or at its pin.
350	    15	
351	    16	## Why not the alternatives
352	    17	
353	    18	| Approach | Problem |
354	    19	|---|---|
355	    20	| Switch branches in the submodule checkout | Only one branch at a time. The gitlink shows dirty while you work. `pull` and `bump` then operate on your feature branch. Parallel agents collide. |
356	    21	| `git worktree add` of the **superproject** | Submodules in a new superproject worktree start **uninitialized**: each worktree needs a full `submodule update --init`, which is slow and multiplies clones. Git's support for submodules inside multiple superproject worktrees is still marked experimental. |
357	    22	| Worktree outside the superproject (`~/worktrees/...`) | Works, but leaves the agent's entry point. Context such as AGENTS.md, `context/`, and sibling repos is not under the session root, and the agent needs add-dir. Use it only when a task must be isolated from the superproject. |
358	    23	
359	    24	## Base revision
360	    25	
361	    26	- `track` children branch from `origin/<branch>`.
362	    27	- `pin` and `lazy` children branch from the **recorded gitlink**: a fix to a
363	    28	  pinned production baseline should start from that baseline, not from
364	    29	  upstream main.
365	    30	- An existing local or remote branch of the same name is checked out instead
366	    31	  of a new one being created.
367	    32	- Override with `--base`.
368	    33	
369	    34	## Coexistence with superproject issue worktrees
370	    35	
371	    36	`forge-native-dev` places superproject issue worktrees at `.worktrees/issue-<n>`.
372	    37	Child worktrees are nested under the child's path (`.worktrees/app/...`), so
373	    38	the two never collide. Superproject issue worktrees remain fine for changes
374	    39	that touch **only** outer content (docs, context, CI).

377	     2	## Working across submodules

379	     4	This repository is a superproject: each child under a submodule path is its

381	     6	the child's own instructions before editing inside it; they are authoritative
382	     7	there. This file only governs cross-repo work.
383	     8

385	    10	  `.gitmodules` (`x-policy`): `track` follows `origin/<branch>` by
386	    11	  fast-forward, `pin` moves only for a stated reason, `lazy` is not

398	    23	  or pinned commit. Do not create worktrees of this superproject for child

403	    28	  The bump refuses unpushed or unreachable commits.
404	    29	- **One cross-repo change gets one outer commit.** Bump every affected child
405	    30	  together, and leave no unrelated gitlink drift behind.
406	    31	- **Before any outer commit that stages gitlinks**, run
407	    32	  `just sub-preflight`.
408	    33	- Preserve existing child branches, local commits, and dirty work. `pull`
409	    34	  refuses diverged or dirty checkouts; resolve those by hand, don't force.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## What this is
6	
7	An **umbrella superproject** that checks out five standalone dotfiles repos as git submodules so an agent holds all platforms' context in one session:
8	
9	| Submodule | Upstream | Scope | Package layer |
10	|---|---|---|---|
11	| `dotfiles-unix/` | `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` | macOS / Linux / WSL, zsh + bash | ansible + homebrew + mise/uv/cargo/npm |
12	| `dotfiles-windows/` | `daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows` | native Windows, PowerShell 7 (pwsh) | scoop (CLI) + winget (GUI) |
13	| `dotfiles-iSH/` | `daviddwlee84/dotfiles-iSH` | iOS iSH, Alpine x86, ash | apk + chezmoi (experimental) |
14	| `dotfiles-OpenWrt/` | `daviddwlee84/dotfiles-OpenWrt` | OpenWrt / ImmortalWrt, ash | native apk/opkg + chezmoi (default) |
15	| `dotfiles-Termux/` | `daviddwlee84/dotfiles-Termux` | Android native Termux, Bash | pkg + chezmoi; host uv/ADB helper |
16	
17	**Support priority: Unix > Windows >> iSH / OpenWrt / Termux.** The lightweight targets
18	are experimental and do not inherit the complete Unix/Windows parity contract.
19	Read their own `AGENTS.md` before editing. The iSH/OpenWrt shared core, tests and
20	asset lock are byte-identical; Termux has an independent native Bash/pkg core. RPi-ImmortalWrt is an
21	external reference, not a firmware/network surface owned by this repo.
22	
23	The point of this repo is **UX alignment**: the same feature should feel the same on both platforms, even though the implementations are native to each (the pwsh layer is *not* a port of the POSIX shell layer). There is no product or build here — all real work happens inside a submodule. The root `justfile` is an orchestration-only safety layer for those submodules.
24	
25	**Read the submodule's own contract before editing it.** Both are long, binding, and authoritative for their repo; this file only governs *cross-repo* work.
26	
27	- `dotfiles-unix/CLAUDE.md` (`AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md` are symlinks to it) — cross-file maintenance table, chezmoi templating rules, hard invariants.
28	- `dotfiles-windows/AGENTS.md` (`CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it) — same, Windows flavour.
29	
30	## Submodule + working-tree facts that bite
31	
32	- **Commit from the inside out.** First commit and push every affected submodule
33	  to its own remote; only then commit the gitlink pointer bump in this
34	  superproject. `git submodule status` shows drift, and a superproject pointer to
35	  an unpushed commit dangles for every other clone.
36	- **One cross-repo change gets one outer pointer commit.** When work touches both
37	  `dotfiles-unix/` and `dotfiles-windows/`, finish and push both inner commits, then
38	  stage **all affected** gitlinks with `git add dotfiles-unix dotfiles-windows dotfiles-iSH dotfiles-OpenWrt dotfiles-Termux` and record them
39	  together in a single superproject commit. Do not make one outer commit per
40	  submodule or leave the second pointer as unrelated working-tree drift. Include
41	  any matching cross-repo docs/contract edits in that same outer commit. Before
42	  committing, verify the exact selected commits with
43	  `git diff --cached --submodule=log -- dotfiles-unix dotfiles-windows dotfiles-iSH dotfiles-OpenWrt dotfiles-Termux`.
44	- A single-platform change still needs its inner commit plus one outer pointer
45	  commit, but only the affected gitlink should move. Gitlinks record commit IDs,
46	  not branch names; make sure each selected commit is reachable from the intended
47	  upstream branch before the outer push.
48	- **The Unix checkout is NOT the live chezmoi source dir.** On this Mac the live source is `~/.local/share/chezmoi` — a *separate clone* of `daviddwlee84/dotfiles`. Editing `dotfiles-unix/` here changes nothing about the machine until it is pushed and pulled there, or until you pass `--source`:
49	  `chezmoi diff --source=$PWD/dotfiles-unix`. Never assume a bare `chezmoi apply` picks up an edit made in this tree.
50	- **`pre-commit install` does not work here — and is not needed.** These dotfiles set a global `core.hooksPath`, so the dispatcher at `~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit` runs this repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` automatically (redact-agent-secrets → gitleaks → hygiene). The Windows repo deliberately does the opposite; details and the self-test results are in [`docs/git-hooks-and-secret-redaction.md`](docs/git-hooks-and-secret-redaction.md).
51	
52	## Commands
53	
54	From the superproject root, the native chezmoi recipes always pass an absolute
55	`--source` pointing at the matching submodule; they never fall back to the live
56	chezmoi source clone:
57

132	### Init prompts are the main UX-alignment lever
133	
134	Both repos prompt once at `chezmoi init` and gate features on the answers. **Shared keys must keep the same name and the same meaning**: `name`, `email`, `backupMode`, `enableVimMode`, `preferredEditor`, `agentSounds`, `agentLanguagePolicy`, `useChineseMirror`, `installCodingAgents`, `installInputMethod`, `installLlmTools`, `installSummarize`, `installMediaTools`, `installIacTools`, `installTunnelTools`, `installExtraRuntimes`, `installGamingApps`.
135	
136	Deliberate divergences — do not "unify" them: unix `profile` (`macos`/`ubuntu_desktop`/`ubuntu_server`) vs. Windows `role` (`workstation`/`minimal`); each repo also has platform-only keys (`primaryShell`, `noRoot`, `installNiri` … / `installWsl`, `installClink`, `installWindowsApps` …).
137	
138	The two prompt files are maintained in **opposite ways** — a shared new prompt is two different edits:
139	
140	- unix: edit the `PROMPTS` tuple in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`, then `just gen-prompts`. Never hand-edit the generated marker regions in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`.
141	- Windows: hand-author in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, **and** add the matching `--promptBool/--promptChoice "<exact text>=value"` flag to `.github/workflows/windows.yml` in the same commit, or CI's non-interactive init EOFs.

143	## Documentation
144	
145	- Platform-agnostic knowledge (design decisions that span both, cross-repo how-tos, parity notes) → [`docs/`](docs/README.md) **in this repo**, plain Markdown, no site build. Current notes: [parity-matrix](docs/parity-matrix.md), [git-hooks-and-secret-redaction](docs/git-hooks-and-secret-redaction.md), [rime-shared-config](docs/rime-shared-config.md), [multi-machine-compute-plane](docs/multi-machine-compute-plane.md). Add the new file to `docs/README.md`'s index.
146	- Anything a user of one platform needs → that submodule's `docs/`, and it must be **bilingual**: `docs/X.md` + `docs/X.zh-TW.md`, plus `nav` + `nav_translations` in `mkdocs.yml`, with the strict build kept green. A feature landing on both platforms therefore means **four** doc files.
147	- `TODO.md` / `backlog/` / `pitfalls/` exist in *each* submodule (the `project-knowledge-harness` convention). File an item in the repo where the work will land. Do not create `TODO.md`/`ROADMAP.md`/`backlog/`/`pitfalls/` at this level — the submodules have independent upstreams and get cloned standalone, so a note that lives only here is invisible in the repo that has to act on it.
148	- **A cross-cutting item is split, not duplicated.** Decide which submodule will hold the code: **one** `backlog/<slug>.md` goes there, the other submodule gets a `TODO.md` line only, and the platform-agnostic *decision* goes in [`docs/`](docs/README.md) here. Two full backlog docs for one item is the failure mode — the shared reasoning drifts. An item with no code at all (a pure cross-repo contract) is a `docs/` note here and a backlog item nowhere.

45	(or `--plan` / `--wf-id ID --fold Y` / `--aggregate`) · `alpha-compare --experiment E --segment S` ·
46	`alpha-log RUN_DIR` · `alpha-features factors|model` · `--set backtest.standard.enabled=true` (adds the `vectorized` / standard backtest, needs the qdk store) · `data.streaming: true` (XGBoost external memory, ~8.6 GB peak instead of ~32 GB) · Colab: `uv run python scripts/colab/run.py CONFIG --session S --keep`
47	(docs/guides/colab.md). Long queues go to pueue group `alpha` (one job at a time: full runs peak ~32 GB RAM).
48	
49	## Paper research and reusable methods
50	
51	- When asked to research a paper, search existing notes by arXiv ID / DOI first. Read primary sources and record version, date and reading depth; update existing notes rather than duplicating them.
52	- Default to takeaway + key evidence. Save in `docs/papers/<slug>.md` and update the index and MkDocs nav, following [論文筆記](docs/papers/index.md). Ask only about ambiguity that materially changes scope.
53	- Separate author-reported results, our interpretation and local verification. Record dataset, splits, baselines, costs/execution assumptions and source section/table; explicitly mark missing or unchecked details. Abstract-only reading is not a full review.
54	- Search `docs/methods/` before designing related experiments. Index reusable ideas by the problem they solve, linking to papers and experiments. Extend existing method entries before creating pages; update paper/method links together.
55	- Assess factor-dictionary eligibility in each paper note. Only qualifying factor definitions, variants and evidence go to `knowledge/quant-factor-dictionary`; follow its AGENTS.md, contributing guide and schemas, preserve provenance/verification status, and validate/build there. General models, losses and portfolio methods belong in `docs/methods/`.
56	- Deep reading adds derivations, architecture and ablation analysis; reproduction is a separate decision. For hands-on verification, consider [marimo implement-paper](https://github.com/marimo-team/skills/tree/main/skills/implement-paper) and inspect its current instructions before use. Reading alone does not require installing skills or running notebooks.
57	- Scope reproduction separately; link notebooks and experiment reports back to the paper. Local backtests follow backend/fidelity and MLflow rules; quoted external results do not become local MLflow runs.
58	- Only selected follow-up work enters TODO.md/backlog; reading does not automatically create a reproduction task. Use zh-TW prose with English technical terms on first mention.
59	
60	## Project memory
61	
62	- `TODO.md` — priority (P0–P3) × effort (S/M/L) index of future work; link to `backlog/<slug>.md` for anything needing context.
63	- `backlog/` — resume-friendly design / research notes for TODO items.
64	- `pitfalls/` — one file per trap, titled by the **symptom** so it is grep-able; include cause, fix, and how it was found.
65

# Let Claude coordinate ongoing work with Projects

> Hand Claude a stream of related tasks in one conversation and let it run them as parallel cloud sessions that share repositories, instructions, and memory.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Projects are in public beta on Pro, Max, and Ultra plans and rolling out gradually. The rollout started with accounts that have used [cloud sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web.md) and don't have existing projects in claude.ai chat or Cowork. Projects aren't offered on Team or Enterprise plans yet.
>
> If you don't see **Projects** in the sidebar at [claude.ai/code](https://claude.ai/code) or in the Code tab of the [desktop app](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop.md), check under **More** there. If it's missing there too, the rollout hasn't reached your account yet. You can [join the waitlist](https://claude.com/form/projects), and see [Run agents in parallel](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents.md) for what you can use in the meantime.

A project is one ongoing conversation where Claude coordinates a stream of related work for you. You tell it what needs doing and it starts a thread for each task.

Each thread is usually a [cloud session](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web.md): Claude Code running in the cloud rather than on your machine. When a task needs something only your computer has, you can ask Claude to [run that thread on your computer](#run-a-thread-on-your-own-computer) instead of in the cloud, through [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md). Threads run in parallel, and you can check on them and steer them from your phone. Cloud threads keep going after you close your laptop, while a thread on your computer runs only while that computer is awake.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = []
# ///
"""Keep a git-submodule superproject on track.

A gitlink records a commit, not a branch, so a superproject drifts by design.
This CLI makes the drift visible and moves pointers according to a
per-submodule policy stored as extra keys in `.gitmodules`:

    [submodule "app"]
        path = app
        url = git@github.com:me/app.git
        branch = main        # tracking branch (native git key)
        x-policy = track     # track | pin | lazy
        x-bump = pr          # pr | direct | manual   (only meaningful for track)
        x-tier = core        # free-form grouping
        update = none        # set for lazy children (native git key)

Stdlib only. Results go to stdout (text, or JSON with --json); diagnostics go
to stderr. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 refused / check failed, 2 usage error.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

__version__ = "0.2.0"

POLICIES = ("track", "pin", "lazy")
BUMP_MODES = ("pr", "direct", "manual")
