#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Find work that exists only on this machine, or checkouts that drifted from main.

Scans the root repository and every initialized submodule (recursively) and reports:

- local branches whose commits are on no remote (or ahead of / diverged from upstream)
- branches whose upstream was deleted (cleanup candidates)
- uncommitted changes, untracked files and stashes
- extra worktrees (each should end as a pushed branch / PR, then be removed)
- gitlinks that are not the submodule's latest tracked branch (`.gitmodules` `branch`,
  else origin/HEAD), or that
  point at a commit no remote contains

Read-only apart from `git fetch` (skip with --no-fetch). Exit code 1 when anything is
found, so it can gate a session hand-off.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.stdout.rstrip("\n") if out.returncode == 0 else ""


def submodules(repo: Path) -> list[Path]:
    out = git(repo, "submodule", "foreach", "--quiet", "--recursive", "echo $displaypath")
    return [repo / line for line in out.splitlines() if line]


def default_branch(repo: Path) -> str | None:
    ref = git(repo, "symbolic-ref", "-q", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD")
    return ref or ("origin/main" if git(repo, "rev-parse", "-q", "--verify", "origin/main")
                   else None)


def audit(repo: Path, fetch: bool) -> list[str]:
    if fetch:
        git(repo, "fetch", "-q", "--all", "--prune")
    found = []
    fmt = "%(refname:short)|%(upstream:short)|%(upstream:track)"
    for line in git(repo, "for-each-ref", f"--format={fmt}", "refs/heads").splitlines():
        branch, upstream, track = line.split("|")
        if not upstream:
            n = git(repo, "rev-list", "--count", branch, "--not", "--remotes")
            if n and int(n) > 0:
                found.append(f"branch {branch}: {n} commit(s) on no remote")
        elif "gone" in track:
            unmerged = [x for x in git(repo, "cherry", default_branch(repo) or "HEAD",
                                       branch).splitlines() if x.startswith("+")]
            found.append(f"branch {branch}: upstream deleted"
                         + (f", {len(unmerged)} unmerged commit(s)" if unmerged
                            else " (merged; safe to delete)"))
        elif "ahead" in track:
            found.append(f"branch {branch} -> {upstream} {track}")
    dirty = git(repo, "status", "--porcelain", "--ignore-submodules=all").splitlines()
    if dirty:
        found.append(f"uncommitted: {len(dirty)} path(s), e.g. {dirty[0][3:]}")
    stashes = git(repo, "stash", "list").splitlines()
    if stashes:
        found.append(f"stashes: {len(stashes)}")
    worktrees = [x for x in git(repo, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain").split("\n\n") if x]
    for wt in worktrees[1:]:
        fields = dict(line.split(" ", 1) for line in wt.splitlines() if " " in line)
        path = Path(fields.get("worktree", ""))
        branch = fields.get("branch", "detached").removeprefix("refs/heads/")
        state = []
        if not path.exists():
            state.append("missing (prune)")
        else:
            dirty = bool(git(path, "status", "--porcelain", "--ignore-submodules=all"))
            if dirty:
                state.append("UNCOMMITTED CHANGES (back up before removing)")
            unpushed = git(path, "rev-list", "--count", "HEAD", "--not", "--remotes")
            if unpushed and int(unpushed):
                state.append(f"{unpushed} unpushed")
            main = default_branch(repo)
            if main and not git(path, "rev-list", "-1", f"{main}..HEAD"):
                # A fresh branch with no commits also passes this test, so "removable"
                # is only claimed when nothing is uncommitted or unpushed.
                safe = not dirty and not (unpushed and int(unpushed))
                state.append(f"no commits beyond {main}" + ("; removable" if safe else ""))
        found.append(f"worktree {path.name} [{branch}]: " + (", ".join(state) or "clean, pushed"))
    return found


def tracked_branch(parent: Path, rel: str) -> str | None:
    """`branch = ...` from the parent's .gitmodules (git's own tracking setting)."""
    out = git(parent, "config", "-f", ".gitmodules", "--get-regexp", r"^submodule\..*\.path$")
    for line in out.splitlines():
        key, _, value = line.partition(" ")
        if value == rel:
            name = key.removeprefix("submodule.").removesuffix(".path")
            branch = git(parent, "config", "-f", ".gitmodules", f"submodule.{name}.branch")
            return f"origin/{branch}" if branch and branch != "." else None
    return None


def gitlink_drift(parent: Path, sub: Path) -> list[str]:
    rel = str(sub.relative_to(parent))
    pinned = git(parent, "ls-tree", "HEAD", rel).split()
    if len(pinned) < 3:
        return []
    sha = pinned[2]
    found = []
    if not git(sub, "branch", "-r", "--contains", sha):
        found.append(f"gitlink {sha[:7]} is on no remote")
    main = tracked_branch(parent, rel) or default_branch(sub)
    if main:
        tip = git(sub, "rev-parse", main)
        if tip and tip != sha:
            ahead = git(sub, "rev-list", "--count", f"{main}..{sha}")
            behind = git(sub, "rev-list", "--count", f"{sha}..{main}")
            found.append(f"gitlink {sha[:7]} vs {main} {tip[:7]}: "
                         f"{behind} behind, {ahead} not in {main}")
    return found


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--no-fetch", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--no-gitlinks", action="store_true", help="skip gitlink vs main drift")
    ap.add_argument("--include-references", action="store_true",
                    help="also report drift of submodules/references/** (pinned on purpose)")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    repos = [ROOT, *submodules(ROOT)]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as pool:
        results = dict(zip(repos, pool.map(lambda r: audit(r, not args.no_fetch), repos)))
    if not args.no_gitlinks:
        for sub in repos[1:]:
            if not args.include_references and "submodules/references" in str(sub):
                continue
            parent = next(p for p in sorted(repos, key=lambda p: -len(p.parts))
                          if p != sub and sub.is_relative_to(p))
            results[sub] += gitlink_drift(parent, sub)
    report = {str(r.relative_to(ROOT)) or ".": f for r, f in results.items() if f}
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(report, indent=1))
    else:
        for repo, items in report.items():
            print(repo)
            for item in items:
                print(f"  {item}")
        print(f"{len(report)} of {len(repos)} repositories need attention" if report
              else f"all {len(repos)} repositories clean and pushed")
    return 1 if report else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

4	# Worktree-per-issue lifecycle manager.
5	# Subcommands: start, finish, list
6	#
7	# start <issue-number> — create branch + worktree for an issue
8	# finish <issue-number> — push branch, create PR linking to issue
9	# list — show active worktree/issue/PR alignment
10	#
11	# Compatibility: macOS system Bash 3.2+.

13	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
14	
15	# shellcheck source=forge.sh
16	source "$SCRIPT_DIR/forge.sh"
17	
18	# Configurable worktree root (relative to repo root).
19	FORGE_WORKTREE_ROOT="${FORGE_WORKTREE_ROOT:-.worktrees}"
20	
21	usage() {
22	  cat <<'EOF'
23	Usage: forge-worktree.sh <subcommand> [args]
24	
25	Subcommands:
26	  start <issue-number>    Create a branch + worktree for the issue.
27	                          Branch: issue/<number>-<slug>
28	                          Worktree: .worktrees/issue-<number>/
29	  finish <issue-number>   Push the branch and create a PR linking to the issue.
30	  list                    Show active issue worktrees with PR status.
31	
32	Options:
33	  --agent                 Use agent/ prefix for the branch (agent/issue/<n>-<slug>).
34	  --base BRANCH           Base branch to create from (default: auto-detected).
35	  --draft                 Create PR as draft (finish only).
36	  -h, --help              Show this help and exit.
37	
38	Environment:
39	  FORGE_WORKTREE_ROOT     Worktree directory (default: .worktrees).
40	EOF
41	}
42	
43	subcmd=""
44	issue_num=""
45	agent_prefix=0
46	base_branch=""
47	draft=0
48	
49	# Parse global options first, then subcommand
50	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
51	  case "$1" in
52	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
53	    --agent) agent_prefix=1; shift ;;
54	    --base) base_branch="$2"; shift 2 ;;
55	    --draft) draft=1; shift ;;
56	    start|finish|list)
57	      subcmd="$1"; shift

59	      ;;
60	    *)
61	      # Could be a subcommand with args mixed in
62	      echo "Unknown argument: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2
63	      ;;

66

2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	# Auto-cleanup branches and worktrees whose PRs have been merged.

8	# Compatibility: macOS system Bash 3.2+.

10	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

19	Usage: forge-cleanup.sh [OPTIONS]
20	
21	Scan issue branches for merged PRs and clean up branches + worktrees.
22	
23	Options:
24	  --dry-run    Show what would be cleaned without doing it.
25	  --force      Skip confirmation prompts.
26	  --all        Also clean branches with closed (not merged) PRs.
27	  -h, --help   Show this help and exit.
28	EOF
29	}
30	
31	dry_run=0
32	force=0
33	include_closed=0
34	
35	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
36	  case "$1" in
37	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
38	    --dry-run) dry_run=1; shift ;;
39	    --force) force=1; shift ;;
40	    --all) include_closed=1; shift ;;
41	    *) echo "Unknown argument: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
42	  esac
43	done

45	forge_detect
46	_forge_require_cli
47

53	git fetch --prune 2>/dev/null || true
54

57	
58	if [ -z "$branches" ]; then
59	  _forge_log "No issue branches found. Nothing to clean."
60	  exit 0
61	fi
62	
63	# Track what we'll clean
64	to_clean=""
65	clean_count=0
66	
67	_forge_log ""
68	_forge_log "Scanning branches for merged PRs..."
69	_forge_log ""
70	
71	while IFS= read -r branch; do

73

75	  pr_st="$(forge_pr_status "$branch" 2>/dev/null || true)"

84	      reason="PR #${pr_n} merged"
85	      ;;

87	      if [ "$include_closed" -eq 1 ]; then
88	        should_clean=1

163	  fi

167	  git branch -D "$branch" 2>/dev/null || {

169	  }

171	  cleaned=$(( cleaned + 1 ))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Initialize selected, pinned Git submodules without switching existing work."""
import argparse
import configparser
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CORE = {"submodules/tarlin", "submodules/atp-sipui", "submodules/dongwu-tick-downloader",
        "submodules/OfflineAnalysis", "submodules/tarlin-infra", "submodules/trading-journal",
        "submodules/navigation",
        "submodules/lazytarlin", "submodules/Agreements", "submodules/schema",
        "submodules/market-analysis"}
GROUPS = {"personal": "submodules/personal/", "references": "submodules/references/"}


class InitError(Exception):
    pass


def git(root, *args):
    result = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), *args], text=True,
                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    if result.returncode:
        # Avoid echoing authentication helpers, remote URLs, or raw Git stderr.
        raise InitError("Git command failed: {} (exit {})".format(args[0], result.returncode))
    return result.stdout.strip()


def entries(root):
    path = root / ".gitmodules"
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    config = configparser.ConfigParser(interpolation=None)
    config.read(path)
    found = []
    for section in config.sections():
        value = config.get(section, "path").strip('"')
        relative = PurePosixPath(value)
        if relative.is_absolute() or ".." in relative.parts or value.startswith("-"):
            raise InitError("Unsafe submodule path")
        child = (root / value).resolve()
        if not child.is_relative_to(root.resolve()):
            raise InitError("Submodule path escapes its parent")
        stage = git(root, "ls-files", "--stage", "--", value).splitlines()
        if len(stage) != 1:
            raise InitError("Expected one indexed gitlink: " + value)
        mode, revision, slot = stage[0].split("\t", 1)[0].split()
        if mode != "160000" or slot != "0":
            raise InitError("Expected an unconflicted gitlink: " + value)
        found.append((value, revision))
    return found


def selected(root, group, name=None):
    candidates = [(p, sha) for p, sha in entries(root)
                  if (p in CORE if group == "core" else p.startswith(GROUPS[group]))]
    if name:
        prefix = "submodules/" if group == "core" else GROUPS[group]
        candidates = [(p, sha) for p, sha in candidates if p.removeprefix(prefix) == name]
    if not candidates:
        raise InitError("No registered submodules match this group/name")
    return candidates


def initialized(path):
    if not path.exists():
        return False
    if not (path / ".git").exists():
        if any(path.iterdir()):
            raise InitError("Nonempty uninitialized path: " + str(path))
        return False
    return Path(git(path, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")).resolve() == path.resolve()


def preflight(root, modules, recursive):
    for relative, revision in modules:
        path = root / relative
        if initialized(path):
            if git(path, "rev-parse", "HEAD") != revision:
                raise InitError("Existing checkout differs from its gitlink; preserved: " + str(path))
            if recursive:
                preflight(path, entries(path), True)


def warn_case_collisions(path):
    setting = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(path), "config", "--bool", "core.ignorecase"],
                             text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    if setting.stdout.strip() != "true":
        return
    names = {}
    for name in git(path, "ls-files", "-z").split("\0"):
        if name:
            names.setdefault(name.casefold(), []).append(name)
    for collision in names.values():
        if len(collision) > 1:
            print("warning: case-fold collision in {}: {}; use git show for exact files or a "
                  "case-sensitive checkout; no files were repaired".format(path, repr(collision)),
                  file=sys.stderr)


def initialize(root, modules, recursive, dry_run):
    for relative, revision in modules:
        path = root / relative
        if initialized(path):
            print("preserve " + str(path))
        elif dry_run:
            print("initialize {} @ {}".format(path, revision))
            continue
        else:
            try:
                git(root, "submodule", "update", "--init", "--checkout", "--", relative)
            except InitError as exc:
                raise InitError("{}: {}".format(relative, exc)) from None
            if git(path, "rev-parse", "HEAD") != revision:
                raise InitError("Initialized revision does not match gitlink: " + str(path))
            print("initialized {} @ {}".format(path, revision))
        warn_case_collisions(path)
        if recursive:
            children = entries(path)
            preflight(path, children, True)
            initialize(path, children, True, dry_run)


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("group", choices=("core", "personal", "references"))
    parser.add_argument("name", nargs="?", help="Exact original name; references use owner/name")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        modules = selected(ROOT, args.group, args.name)
        recursive = args.group == "core"
        preflight(ROOT, modules, recursive)
        initialize(ROOT, modules, recursive, args.dry_run)
        # Keep the established complete model-source checkout for core development.
        if args.group == "core" and any(p == "submodules/tarlin" for p, _ in modules):
            model = ROOT / "submodules/tarlin/strategy/conbond-model"
            if not args.dry_run and not initialized(model):
                raise InitError("Required nested Tarlin model checkout is missing")
            if initialized(model):
                sparse = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(model), "config", "--bool", "core.sparseCheckout"],
                                        text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
                if sparse.stdout.strip() == "true":
                    if git(model, "status", "--porcelain"):
                        raise InitError("Sparse model checkout has local changes; preserved")
                    if not args.dry_run:
                        git(model, "sparse-checkout", "disable")
                    print("expand model sources " + str(model))
    except (InitError, OSError, configparser.Error, ValueError) as exc:
        print("submodule initialization: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

````text
252	### Run a thread on your own computer
253	
254	When a task needs something only your computer has, such as a local database, a device emulator, or an API behind your VPN, ask Claude to run the thread for that task on your computer instead of in the cloud. When you ask in the project conversation, the thread is a Claude Code session in a folder on your machine, connected through [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md). The project's other threads keep running in the cloud. Compared with a cloud thread, a thread on your computer:
255	
256	* Works with the files, tools, MCP servers, and Claude Code settings on that machine, including its hooks and permission rules, instead of the project's cloud environment
257	* Starts with the project's instructions, but not with its memory files loaded
258	* Runs only while that computer is awake with Remote Control turned on
259	
260	**1. Connect the folder**
261	
262	On the computer that has the folder the task needs, make it available through Remote Control in one of two ways. Both need Claude Code v2.1.280 or later on that computer.
263	
264	* **In the Claude desktop app**: open **Settings > Code** or **Settings > Claude Code** and turn on **Use this computer from your phone and claude.ai**. Add the folder to the list under that switch. Threads can run on this computer while the app is open.
265	* **In a terminal**: run `claude remote-control` in the folder and leave it running. In a git repository, add `--spawn worktree` to give each thread there its own [worktree](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md) instead of the folder itself.
266	
267	**2. Ask for the task with Work locally**
268	
269	In the project conversation, choose **Work locally** from the **+** menu beside the message box, which tags your message **Local**, and write what you want done. Saying in the message that the task should run on your computer works too.
270	
271	**3. Allow it on the card**
272	
273	Claude answers with an **Allow Claude to work in a folder on your device** card. Pick the folder if you connected several. Two threads working in one folder at the same time can overwrite each other's changes, so if the folder is a git repository, you can turn on **Worktree** in the folder's options to give this thread its own worktree instead. Then click **Allow once**.
274	
275	The thread runs in [auto mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode), so Claude runs commands and edits files in that folder without asking you each time. If auto mode is unavailable or turned off in that computer's Claude Code, the thread runs without it, and any permission prompt it raises waits for your answer in the thread, as [Unblock a thread waiting on approval](#unblock-a-thread-waiting-on-approval) describes.
276	
277	To run the thread in another mode, start `claude remote-control` with [`--settings`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session). Then [`permissions.defaultMode`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#start-in-a-different-mode), in that file or in that computer's settings, can pick another mode.
278	
279	While the thread runs, a laptop icon in its header shows whether your computer is connected. Click it to see which folder the thread is using or to turn the connection off. The thread pauses while that computer is asleep, and stops if the desktop app or `claude remote-control` quits.
280	
281	* **To get the thread going again**: see [Lost contact with your folder](#lost-contact-with-your-folder)
282	* **To keep the computer from sleeping on its own**: in the desktop app, turn on **Keep this computer awake for Remote Control** in **Settings > Code** or **Settings > Claude Code**
283	
284	A project can't run a thread on your computer while [**Require trusted devices**](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md#trusted-devices) is on for your account.
285	
286	## Give a project standing context
287	
288	Project memory, project instructions, and the project's repositories, files, and environment carry context across threads. You set each one once.
289	
290	| Context | What it carries | How you set it |
291	| :- | :- | :- |
292	| Project memory | Notes Claude keeps about the project, such as requirements, decisions, and pitfalls, stored as files. Every cloud thread reads the index file `MEMORY.md` when it starts and opens the other files when it needs them | Ask Claude in the project conversation or any cloud thread to remember a requirement, a decision, or a pitfall, or to forget one. Read, edit, and delete the files in **Project settings > Memory** |
293	| Project instructions | Text sent to each new thread and to Claude in the project conversation, up to 16,000 characters. [Write project instructions](#write-project-instructions) covers what to put in it | **Project settings > Memory > Project instructions**, or ask Claude to change the instructions |
294	| Repositories, files, and environment | The repositories every cloud thread clones, the folders and files it can read under `/mnt/project-files`, and the cloud environment it runs in | Repositories and environment in **Project settings > Environment**, or ask Claude in the conversation to add a repository to the project. [Files and folders](#add-files-and-folders) from **Add** in the project's [**Library**](#see-what-needs-you-in-overview) |
295	
296	**Project settings > Memory** lists these files under **Auto memory**, because Claude writes them itself as it works in the project. They're separate from the [auto memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md) Claude Code keeps on your machine, even though both use a `MEMORY.md` index. Project memory is also separate from the `CLAUDE.md` files in the project's repositories. Each cloud thread still reads those `CLAUDE.md` files from its clone when it starts, so put instructions about a repository in its `CLAUDE.md` and notes about the project in project memory.
297	
298	### Write project instructions
299	
300	Project instructions are the brief every new thread starts from. Select **Settings** in the **⋯** menu in the project header to open **Project settings**, then go to **Memory > Project instructions**. A useful brief covers:
301	
302	* What the project is for
303	* Where the work happens: which repositories, which branch to start from, how to name pull requests
304	* How a thread checks its own work before calling it done
305	* What to do when something it needs is missing
306	* What needs your go-ahead first
307	
308	For example:
309	
310	```text theme={null}
311	This project holds p95 latency for the payments API under 200 ms: profiling, query and caching fixes, and the dependency upgrades that come with them, in the payments-api repository.
312	
313	- Branch from main and open one draft pull request per thread.
314	- Before you call work done, run `make test` and `make lint` and paste the summary lines in your final message.
315	- If you can't reach something you need, such as a repository, a secret, an API, or a connector, say exactly what's missing in your first message and stop. Don't substitute, mock, or guess.
316	- Don't merge, force-push, or change CI configuration without asking me in the thread.
317	```
318	
319	Rules about one repository, such as its build commands, belong in that repository's `CLAUDE.md`, which every cloud thread reads when the repository is part of the project. Once work is underway, when you correct a thread, also tell Claude to remember the correction: it goes into [project memory](#give-a-project-standing-context) and later cloud threads start with it.
320	
321	### Decide which repositories to add
322	
323	The repositories you add to a project come with their code and `CLAUDE.md` in every cloud thread, but [not their skills, `.claude/settings.json`, or `.mcp.json`](#what-threads-pick-up-from-your-repositories). Repositories you don't add are still within reach: a cloud thread can add one to itself when its task needs it. Most projects use both:
324	
325	* **Add it to the project**, in the **New project** dialog, in **Project settings > Environment**, or by asking Claude in the conversation to add it to the project. Every cloud thread from then on clones it and starts with its `CLAUDE.md` loaded, whether or not the task touches it.
326	* **Leave it off and let threads add it when needed.** A cloud thread whose task needs a repository the project doesn't have can add it to itself, and a note in the thread says it was added to this thread only. The clone happens partway through the task, so that repository's `CLAUDE.md` wasn't there when the thread started. The next thread starts without it. A repository added this way needs the same [prerequisites](#check-the-prerequisites) as a project repository: the Claude GitHub App installed on it and push access from your GitHub account.
327	
328	A project doesn't need a repository at all. Its cloud threads can still research, write documents, and write and run code in their own sandbox. They deliver files to the project's **Library**. Any of its cloud threads can still add a repository to itself when a task calls for one.
329	
330	Once the project has repositories, Claude can only add repositories from a GitHub owner the project already uses, whether it adds one to the project or a thread adds one to itself. To bring in a repository from a different owner, add it to the project yourself in **Project settings > Environment**.
331	
332	For a project that spans many repositories, such as one feature with server, web, mobile, and desktop code, add the one or two repositories nearly every task touches and name the others in [project instructions](#write-project-instructions) so Claude knows where the rest of the code lives. Cloud threads then start small and pull in the other repositories only for the tasks that need them.
333	
334	### Add files and folders
335	
336	Add the files and folders you want threads to read in the **New project** dialog's **Context** field, or afterward with **Add** in the project's [**Library**](#see-what-needs-you-in-overview). These limits apply to what you add:
337	
338	* **Files you upload at claude.ai/code or in the desktop app**: up to 1,000 files and 2 GB at a time, with a single file up to 480 MB.
339	* **Folders you upload**: hidden files and `node_modules` aren't added. A project holds up to 10 folders and Google Drive folders combined, and single files don't count toward that limit.
340	* **Changes after upload**: uploads are copies, so a change you make on your computer afterward doesn't reach the project until you upload the file again and choose **Replace** when asked about the existing name.
341	
342	### What threads pick up from your repositories
343	
344	Cloud threads load each repository's `CLAUDE.md` instructions but not its skills, `.mcp.json` servers, or `.claude/settings.json`, whether the project has one repository or several.
345	
346	| In each repository | In a cloud thread |
347	| :- | :- |
348	| `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and `.claude/rules/` at the repository root | Loaded from every repository when the thread starts. `CLAUDE.md` files in subdirectories and [path-specific rules](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md#path-specific-rules) aren't loaded |
349	| Skills under `.claude/skills/` | Not loaded. Enable the skill for your claude.ai account instead, as [Get skills, plugins, connectors, and tools into threads](#get-skills-plugins-connectors-and-tools-into-threads) describes |
350	| Agents and commands under `.claude/` | Not loaded. To use them, [run the thread on your own computer](#run-a-thread-on-your-own-computer) |
351	| MCP servers in `.mcp.json` | Not loaded. Use the connectors on your claude.ai account instead, as [Get skills, plugins, connectors, and tools into threads](#get-skills-plugins-connectors-and-tools-into-threads) describes |
352	| Plugins enabled in `.claude/settings.json` | Not loaded. Add the plugin in **Project settings > Plugins** instead |
353	| Permission rules in `.claude/settings.json` | Not applied. Approve tool calls inside the thread, as [Unblock a thread waiting on approval](#unblock-a-thread-waiting-on-approval) describes, or [run the thread on your own computer](#run-a-thread-on-your-own-computer) |
354	| Hooks in `.claude/settings.json` | Not run. To use your hooks, [run the thread on your own computer](#run-a-thread-on-your-own-computer) |
355	| `env` in `.claude/settings.json` | Not applied. Set environment variables in the [cloud environment](#choose-an-environment-for-threads) |
356	
357	### Choose an environment for threads
358	
359	Every new cloud thread starts in the project's [cloud environment](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments.md). The environment sets which domains threads can reach, which environment variables they have, which network secrets are added to their requests, and what the setup script installs before Claude starts. Cloud threads use a default Anthropic-hosted environment until you pick one in **Project settings > Environment**.
360	
361	If cloud threads need to reach an internal API or a private package registry, or need a token your machine normally holds, change the environment rather than the project: see [Network access](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments.md#network-access), [Add network secrets](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments.md#add-network-secrets), and [Setup scripts](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments.md#setup-scripts).
362	
363	### Get skills, plugins, connectors, and tools into threads
364	
365	Cloud threads don't have the skills, MCP servers, plugins, and tools installed only on your machine. A thread that Claude runs on your machine through [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md) uses what's installed there. To make each of these available to cloud threads:
366	
367	* Skills: enable them for your claude.ai account, and cloud threads load the [skills you enable there](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md#skills-in-cowork-and-cloud-sessions), apart from [some threads in a self-hosted environment](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-configuration.md#how-each-session’s-config-is-assembled). Skills committed to a repository's `.claude/skills/` don't load in cloud threads.
368	* Plugins: add them in **Project settings > Plugins**; they load into each new cloud thread. Plugins that a repository declares in its `.claude/settings.json` [don't load in cloud threads](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments.md#what-carries-over-from-your-setup).
369	* MCP servers: cloud threads get their MCP tools from the connectors on your claude.ai account, which are MCP servers you connect once at [claude.ai/customize/connectors](https://claude.ai/customize/connectors). Every cloud thread can use all of them with no per-project setup. The project conversation itself has no connectors, so send work that needs one as a task for a cloud thread. [How connectors reach Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#how-connectors-reach-claude-code) lists the rules for cloud sessions and the settings that turn connectors off.
370	* Command-line tools and packages: install them in the environment's [setup script](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments.md#setup-scripts).
371	
372	To see which connectors a running cloud thread has at claude.ai/code, open the thread and select **Connectors** from the **+** menu beside its message box. Turning a connector off there removes it from that thread and saves that as your account default, so new threads and claude.ai chats start without it until you turn it back on. A cloud thread picks up a connector you add or reconnect after the next message you send it.
373	
374	## Project settings reference
375	
376	You change project settings at claude.ai/code or in the desktop app, not in `settings.json`. Open **Project settings** from **Settings** in the project's sidebar menu or in the project header's **⋯** menu.
377	
378	Settings save as you change them; a text field you're editing, such as the goal or instructions, shows **Save changes** and **Discard** until you leave it. Changes to instructions, repositories, plugins, and environment in **Project settings** reach new threads, not threads already running.
379	
380	| Setting | Section | What it controls |
381	| :- | :- | :- |
382	| Name, icon, and goal | General | The project's name and icon in the sidebar, and its one-line goal |
383	| Coordinator model and effort | General | The model and [effort level](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config.md#adjust-effort-level) for Claude in the project conversation |
384	| Thread model and effort | General | The model and effort level for threads |
385	| Project instructions | Memory | [Standing rules](#give-a-project-standing-context) every new thread receives |
386	| Project repositories | Environment | The repositories new cloud threads clone |
387	| Cloud environment | Environment | The [cloud environment](#choose-an-environment-for-threads) new cloud threads run in |
388	| Plugins | Plugins | The plugins that load into each new cloud thread |
389	| Usage | Usage | [Token use](#usage-and-cost) by thread and by model |
390	| Memory | Memory | The project's [memory files](#give-a-project-standing-context) |
391	| Auto-continue when usage limits reset | General | Whether a thread or the project conversation that [stops at a usage limit](#usage-limit-reached) continues on its own when the limit resets. On by default. |
392	| Restart Claude | General | Restarts the project conversation when [Claude stops responding there](#claude-hasnt-responded) |
393	| Pause, Archive, Delete | General | Stops, hides, or removes the project; see [Pause, archive, or delete a project](#pause-archive-or-delete-a-project) |
394	
395	### Pause, archive, or delete a project
396	
397	All three controls are at the bottom of **Project settings > General**:
398	
399	* **Pause**: stops everything at once. Every running thread and the conversation are interrupted, no new threads start, scheduled tasks don't run, and the project doesn't accept messages until you resume it. Click **Resume** in the same place or on the banner above the project's message box; a paused thread continues when you send it a message after that.
400	* **Archive**: hides the project from the sidebar and archives its threads, which stops any thread that was running or watching a pull request. Scheduled tasks in the project don't run while it's archived. To bring the project back, open it from the Projects page and click **Unarchive**. Its threads stay archived until you unarchive them individually from the session list.
401	* **Delete**: permanently removes the project along with its threads, its memory, and its files, and turns off the project's scheduled tasks. This can't be undone. Branches and pull requests the threads pushed to GitHub aren't affected.
402	
403	## Usage and cost
404	
405	Project usage counts against the same [plan limits](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md#youve-hit-your-session-limit) as your other Claude Code sessions, and a project can't spend past those limits on its own.
406	
407	A thread that stops at your plan's limit waits and by default continues on its own when the limit resets. Its work then counts against your next usage window. To keep threads from continuing, see [A thread hit the usage limit](#usage-limit-reached).
408	
409	Work goes past your plan's limits only if you have turned on [usage credits](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs.md#add-usage-credits-to-your-subscription) for your account. A thread can't turn them on for you.
410	
411	### What draws on your plan
412	
413	A project uses your limits faster than a single session does, and on a Pro plan in particular you should expect to reach your limit sooner on days you run one. These are the parts of a project that use your plan:
414	
415	* **Running threads**: each is a full session, and several can run at once. There's no fixed number; Claude starts as many as the work calls for, and a limit you [ask for](#tune-how-claude-runs-a-project) is a preference rather than a cap. The enforced limit is 500 new threads per day across your projects.
416	* **The conversation**: Claude uses tokens of its own reading what threads report and deciding what to do next.
417	* **Threads watching a pull request**: an idle thread wakes up and uses your plan again when CI fails or a review comment arrives on its pull request. To stop that, ask in the thread for it to stop watching the pull request.
418	
419	A project with no running threads, no watched pull requests, and no new messages doesn't use your plan while it sits idle, and neither does an archived project.
420	
421	### See and reduce a project's usage
422	
423	Open **Usage** in **Project settings** to see token use by thread and by model, and how much went to the project conversation. To bring it down:
424	
425	* On Pro, Max, and Ultra within your plan's limits, the [cache lifetime](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching.md#cache-lifetime) is an hour. A thread that has been idle longer than that re-reads its whole conversation before doing anything when a follow-up reaches it. For new work, ask Claude to start a fresh thread, which can use less than reviving a large old one.
426	* For work that doesn't need the largest model, [choose a smaller model or a lower effort level](#choose-models-and-let-claude-manage-context) for threads, the conversation, or both.
427	* Ask Claude in the project conversation to run fewer threads at a time, or to answer small questions itself instead of starting a thread.
428	
429	## How projects relate to other Claude Code features
430	
431	Several Claude Code features let more than one session work at the same time, so running work in parallel is not by itself what a project is for. In a project, Claude starts and tracks the sessions instead of you, and each one starts from the same instructions. This is how each neighboring feature connects to a project:
432	
433	* **Claude Tag**: [Claude Tag](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/overview) is Claude in your team's Slack channels, on Team and Enterprise plans. Anyone in a channel can give it work, everyone in the channel sees and steers it, and it uses connections an admin set up for that channel.
434	
435	  Projects are on Pro, Max, and Ultra. A project is yours alone: you're the only one who sends it work or sees its threads, and it uses your own GitHub access and connectors. [How Claude Tag differs from Cowork and Claude Code](https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/concepts/how-it-works#how-claude-tag-differs-from-cowork-and-claude-code) has the side-by-side.
436	* **Cloud sessions**: every thread is a [cloud session](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web.md) unless you ask Claude to run it on your machine. Either way, Claude starts and tracks it instead of you. You can also bring the work of a cloud session you started yourself into a project: choose [**Continue in project**](#start-from-an-existing-cloud-session) in that session's sidebar menu.
437	* **Scheduled tasks**: when you ask for scheduled work in a project, Claude creates a [cloud scheduled task](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines.md) that runs as threads in that project and appears in its **Scheduled tasks** view. Scheduled tasks you create outside a project keep working on their own.
438	* **Remote Control**: [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md) connects claude.ai to a Claude Code session running on your machine. When you ask Claude in a project to run a thread on your computer, the project [uses Remote Control to do it](#run-a-thread-on-your-own-computer).
439	* **Local sessions and agent view**: a session you start yourself in your terminal, IDE, or the desktop app's local environment stays outside your projects, though you can [bring its work into one](#start-from-an-existing-cloud-session). [Agent view](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view.md) is a screen for tracking several local sessions side by side, and you still start each one and give it its task yourself.
440	* **Worktrees**: a [worktree](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md) gives each local session its own working copy of a repository. Cloud threads don't need them: each clones its repositories into its own cloud sandbox and works on its own branch.
441	* **Agent teams**: an [agent team](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams.md) is one session that starts teammate sessions for a single task, on your machine or inside a cloud session, and ends with that task.
442	* **Subagents**: a [subagent](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md) runs inside one session, does a side task in its own context window, and returns a summary to that session. A project's threads are whole sessions that Claude starts and that report back to the project conversation, and a thread can still use subagents for its own side tasks.
443	* **Projects in claude.ai chat and Cowork**: the [earlier Projects experience](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects), which groups conversations and reference files without threads or a coordinator. Those projects keep working as they do today until the redesigned experience reaches them.
444	
445	[Run agents in parallel](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents.md) compares these options side by side.
446	
447	## Limitations
448	
449	* Projects are available at claude.ai/code, in the desktop app, and in the Claude mobile app, not in the terminal CLI, the VS Code extension, or the JetBrains plugin, and not through Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry.
450	* Project threads are [cloud sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web.md), or sessions on your own machine through [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md), with Anthropic as the model provider in both cases. [Security](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security.md) and [Data usage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage.md) cover how cloud sessions are isolated and what's retained, and [Connection and security](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md#connection-and-security) covers how a thread on your machine connects and what's stored.
451	* You can't add a session you started yourself on your machine to a project, though you can [bring its work into one](#start-from-an-existing-cloud-session). A project reaches your machine by [running a thread there through Remote Control](#run-a-thread-on-your-own-computer), and that section lists what it needs.
452	* A cloud thread's sandbox pauses between turns and resumes when the thread continues. If the sandbox can't be resumed, the thread continues from a fresh clone, so uncommitted changes can be lost. On long tasks, ask Claude to commit and push work in progress.
453	* A project belongs to one user. You can't share a project or its threads with another user, and thread transcripts don't have the share option other cloud sessions have. There are no organization-level controls for projects during the beta.
454	* A thread belongs to the one project that started it. You can't move or copy a thread to another project, or move it out to stand alone. [**Continue in project**](#start-from-an-existing-cloud-session) goes the other way only: it brings a cloud session's work into a project. You can't merge two projects into one.
455	
456	## Troubleshooting
````

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Inspect direct gitlinks; initialize only missing, empty child checkouts."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import configparser
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def git(root: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
    )
    if result.returncode:
        raise ValueError(result.stderr.strip() or f"git failed: {args[0]}")
    return result.stdout.strip()


def registrations(root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    config = configparser.ConfigParser(interpolation=None)
    if not config.read(root / ".gitmodules"):
        raise ValueError(".gitmodules is missing")
    result = []
    seen = set()
    for section in config.sections():
        path = config[section]["path"]
        parts = PurePosixPath(path).parts
        if len(parts) != 2 or parts[0] != "submodules" or ".." in parts or "\\" in path:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported direct submodule path: {path}")
        if path in seen or (root / path).resolve() != root.resolve() / path:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate or redirected submodule path: {path}")
        seen.add(path)
        entry = git(root, "ls-files", "--stage", "--", path).splitlines()
        if len(entry) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"expected one registered gitlink: {path}")
        metadata, registered_path = entry[0].split("\t", 1)
        mode, sha, stage = metadata.split()
        if mode != "160000" or stage != "0" or registered_path != path:
            raise ValueError(f"not a resolved gitlink: {path}")
        result.append((path, sha))
    if not result:
        raise ValueError("no direct submodules registered")
    return result


def initialized(path: Path) -> bool:
    if not (path / ".git").exists():
        return False
    return Path(git(path, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")).resolve() == path.resolve()


def run(root: Path, initialize: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    errors = []
    for name, expected in registrations(root):
        path = root / name
        if not initialized(path):
            if not initialize:
                errors.append(f"{name}: uninitialized; run just submodules")
                continue
            if path.exists() and (not path.is_dir() or any(path.iterdir())):
                errors.append(f"{name}: nonempty uninitialized path; preserved")
                continue
            git(root, "-c", "protocol.file.allow=never", "submodule", "update",
                "--init", "--checkout", "--", name)
        if not initialized(path):
            errors.append(f"{name}: initialization incomplete")
            continue
        actual = git(path, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
        dirty = git(path, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=normal")
        if actual != expected:
            errors.append(f"{name}: HEAD {actual} differs from gitlink {expected}; preserved")
        elif dirty:
            errors.append(f"{name}: local changes exist; preserved")
        else:
            print(f"OK {name} {actual}")
    return errors


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("action", choices=("check", "init"))
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=ROOT, help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        errors = run(args.root.resolve(), args.action == "init")
    except (OSError, ValueError, configparser.Error) as error:
        errors = [str(error)]
    for error in errors:
        print(error, file=sys.stderr)
    return int(bool(errors))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
-----
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mirror AlphaBaseline's Jingle-internal submodules (originally git@192.168.222.202:...) into the
# private GitLab group gitlab.com/jingle-archive. Run from a machine that can `ssh ts_david_mac`.
# Idempotent: re-running re-pushes the same refs. Never make these projects public.
#
#   scripts/mirror_jingle_submodules.sh [WORKDIR]
#
# Pushes every original remote branch (refs/remotes/origin/*) as a branch on the mirror.
# GitLab.com rejects blobs > 100 MiB; repos with such blobs in history fail here and are
# tracked in pitfalls/gitlab-100mib-blob-limit.md.
set -euo pipefail

SRC_HOST=${SRC_HOST:-ts_david_mac}
SRC_REPO=${SRC_REPO:-/Volumes/Data/Program/JingleAI/AlphaBaseline}
GROUP=${GROUP:-jingle-archive}
WORKDIR=${1:-$(mktemp -d)}

# submodule path in AlphaBaseline <TAB> original internal path
SUBMODULES=$(cat <<'EOF'
factors/alpha_ren	zshank/alpha_ren
factors/FactorGs	shuang/FactorGs
factors/AlphaFactor	shuang/AlphaFactor
factors/AlphaFactor01	shuang/AlphaFactor01
factors/AlphaTail	shuang/AlphaTail
factors/AlphaFactor2	shuang/AlphaFactor2
factors/AlphatailInner	shuang/AlphatailInner
alpha/alpha_baseline	lixuejian/alpha_baseline
alpha/factors	lixuejian/factors
EOF
)

group_id=$(glab api "groups/$GROUP" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])')

while IFS=$'\t' read -r sm orig; do
    name=${sm##*/}
    echo "== $sm -> $GROUP/$name" >&2
    glab api -X POST projects -f name="$name" -f path="$name" -F namespace_id="$group_id" \
        -f visibility=private \
        -f description="Private mirror of internal Jingle repo $orig (AlphaBaseline submodule $sm). Never make public." \
        >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    mirror="$WORKDIR/$name.git"
    [ -d "$mirror" ] || git clone -q --mirror "$SRC_HOST:$SRC_REPO/.git/modules/$sm" "$mirror"
    mapfile -t specs < <(git -C "$mirror" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' refs/remotes/origin \
        | grep -v '/HEAD$' | sed 's#refs/remotes/origin/\(.*\)#refs/remotes/origin/\1:refs/heads/\1#')
    if git -C "$mirror" push -q "git@gitlab.com:$GROUP/$name.git" "${specs[@]}" 'refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'; then
        echo "ok   $name (${#specs[@]} branches)"
    else
        echo "FAIL $name"
    fi
done <<< "$SUBMODULES"

# Root utilities

- `workspace.py`: direct gitlink check/initialization; existing child work is
  preserved. Its tests use disposable local Git fixtures, without remote calls.
- `project_context.py`: adapted from Tadronaut's local JSON context catalog.
  The script and test dependency locks remain independent of child environments;
  source provenance is recorded in the context reference evidence.
- `data_inventory.py`: stdlib-only bounded inventory, duplicate verification and
  explicit cleanup. SSH executes the reviewed script via stdin without installing
  it on the remote host. Reports live under ignored `files/`.
- `todo-kanban.sh`, `add-todo.sh`, `promote-todo.sh`, `sweep-inbox.sh`: copied from

  `assets/`. Changes to this copied tooling are maintained in the root repo.

Use `just` for the public command list and `just check` for focused root checks.
None of the default checks starts a collector, trains a model or queries a cloud
storage service. Actual data maintenance is opt-in through the data commands.

######## Tadronaut-Mono-Repo README (head)
# Tadronaut-Mono-Repo

Monorepo for cross-project [tadronaut](https://github.com/tadronaut) development and agent history.

## Team repository navigation

[Tadronaut navigation](https://github.com/tadronaut/navigation) is the shared
English entrypoint for repository roles, relationship diagrams, issue routing and
team architecture context. This monorepo remains the personal coordination and
investigation workspace. Start with [navigation's README](submodules/navigation/README.md)
and [Agent instructions](submodules/navigation/AGENTS.md) for organization-wide work.

Initialize only that registered checkout with
`python3 scripts/init_submodules.py core navigation`; it is also included in
`just submodules`. Navigation can build its local/container documentation site
independently of the other trading and model repositories.

## Project context and recall

[context/README.md](context/README.md) describes the schema-validated catalog of
customers, machines, projects, SDKs, deployments, and monitoring relationships.
Connection facts and investigations carry dates and evidence; runtime authority
remains with SSH, the running service, and Grafana.

```sh
just context search 竹潤
just context show zr --depth 2
just context show zyc_friend --depth 2
just context show project.tarlin --depth 2 --json
just context validate
just context-test
```

The first run installs lock-pinned Python tooling through uv; catalog operations
then use local files only. See the [2026-09-16 竹潤 TTR investigation](docs/investigations/2026-09-16-zr-ttr-latency.md)
for the latency findings, evidence, and remaining measurement gaps.

The pinned `submodules/libkdc-simple-demo` supplies the `zyc_friend` data pipeline
and server documentation. See its [mihomo/rootless Docker runbook](submodules/libkdc-simple-demo/zyc_friend/docs/mihomo-rootless-docker.md)
for recovery, boot setup and verification. `zyc_server` recalls the same machine
in the catalog; the current OpenSSH alias is `zyc_friend`.

For tools on restricted trading hosts, use the [offline user-space installation
runbook](docs/runbooks/offline-user-tools.md): pinned official downloads on the
controller, verified SSH transfer, and installation under the target user's
`~/.local` with receipts and shell backups.

Offline tick research uses the pinned `submodules/dongwu-tick-downloader`
alongside Tarlin production revisions. See the [tick validation runbook](docs/runbooks/tick-validation.md)
and [executed notebook](docs/investigations/2026-09-16-tick-validation.ipynb).
`just tick-analyze` verifies cached hashes and rebuilds statistics/plots;
`just tick-notebook` executes the companion. Large data transfers are scheduled
outside trading hours; Dongwu's expected zero receive time is never treated as
zero live latency.

## Codex MCP

The project [`.codex/config.toml`](.codex/config.toml) configures Grafana and
Context7 for Codex. Open this checkout as a trusted project and start a new
Codex session after changing MCP configuration. Python 3 and `uvx` must be
######## AlphaResearch README (head)
# AlphaResearch

截面選股 alpha 研究與學習：每期給股票打分排序 → 買前段（可做空時做空尾部）→ 風控 / 組合優化 → 模擬成交 → 評估。
市場順序：A 股 → 台股 → 美股。

- 全貌：[`docs/concepts/pipeline.md`](docs/concepts/pipeline.md)
- 路線圖：[`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md)（目前：**Phase 0 完成 → Phase 1 跑通 AlphaBaseline 閉環**）
- 設計決策：[`docs/design/`](docs/design/)
- 參考資料索引：[`docs/references.md`](docs/references.md)

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/daviddwlee84/AlphaResearch.git   # 不要加 --recursive
cd AlphaResearch
just setup              # 只 init libs/（alpha-risk-kit、quant-data-kit）+ uv sync
cp .env.example .env
just refs factors       # 按需淺拉某一類參考（或 just refs all）
just docs               # Hub 預覽：優先 http://localhost:8121，占用時自動避讓
```

## Layout

```
docs/          筆記站（zh-TW）：concepts / markets / design(ADR) / papers / reports / experiments
src/           alpha_research：data → signals → portfolio → backtest → evaluation
notebooks/     marimo 研究筆記本
libs/          可寫 submodule：alpha-risk-kit（績效分析）、quant-data-kit（資料層）
knowledge/     可寫 submodule：quant-factor-dictionary（因子知識庫）
references/    唯讀 submodule，依研究流程分類（platforms / factors / factor-mining / models /
               evaluation / portfolio / data / learning / legacy）
experiments/   qlib 等獨立環境
```

Agent / 貢獻規則見 [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)。

## 本機與容器預覽

Hub 使用 MkDocs，字典（`knowledge/quant-factor-dictionary`）使用 Zensical。
兩種啟動方式都透過同一個預覽輔助程式（preview helper）選擇連接埠（port），啟動時會印出實際網址。

| 站點 | 優先 port | 本機啟動 | 容器啟動 | 容器停止／日誌 |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Hub | 8121 | `just docs` | `just docs-up` | `just docs-down` / `just docs-logs` |
| 字典 | 8123 | `just dict-serve` | `just dict-up` | `just dict-down` / `just dict-logs` |

本機預覽需先執行 `just setup`；字典另外安裝 Zensical：

```bash
# 僅初始化字典時可單獨執行；不要使用 --recursive
git submodule update --init knowledge/quant-factor-dictionary
just --justfile knowledge/quant-factor-dictionary/justfile install
just docs
# 在另一個終端機執行
just dict-serve
```

預設 `port=auto`、`host=0.0.0.0`，主機及區域網路都可連線。自動模式先試本站優先 port，
占用時向上搜尋，保留另外三站的優先 port（Alpha Hub 8121、HFT Hub 8122、Alpha 字典 8123、HFT 字典 8124），
最多檢查 100 個候選值。明確指定 port 時，占用就報錯，不會偷偷改號：

# Tons-Mono-Repo

臺股量化研究的整合入口。以固定版本的 Git submodules 連接研究、行情收集與揭示檔解析專案，根目錄保存操作指令、資料來源與研究脈絡。整合 repo 歸屬 `daviddwlee84`，可見性為 private；各子專案保留原本 owner。

## 開始使用

根目錄需要 Git、Python 3.10+、[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) 與 [just](https://just.systems/)。初始化子專案需要對各 private repo 的讀取權限；不需要 CUDA 或行情 API 金鑰。

```sh
git clone --no-recurse-submodules https://github.com/daviddwlee84/Tons-Mono-Repo.git
cd Tons-Mono-Repo
just submodules
just check
```

`just` 列出入口。`just submodules` 只初始化缺少的直接子專案，不切換既有分支或覆蓋修改；如果 HEAD 與 gitlink 不同會明確報告。Context 指令只讀本地 JSON，首次使用 uv 可能下載已鎖定的依賴，之後不會因為查 context 而 SSH、存取雲端或執行 evidence 裡的命令。

```sh
just context search aldsp
just context show dataset.twse-202411 --depth 2
just context search idrive_e2
just context search Messenger
just context validate
just todo
```

## 專案分工

| 子專案 | 初始來源／gitlink | 角色 |
|---|---|---|
| [effortless](submodules/effortless) | main · `fb8aa79f` | DVC、GPU features、模型及 Nautilus 研究回測 |
| [nautilus_trader](submodules/nautilus_trader) | main · `138358e4` | Fugle 即時行情與 catalog 落盤應用 |
| [countless](submodules/countless) | feat/architecture · `0d25d36e` | C++23 collector 架構原型 |
| [old-countless](submodules/old-countless) | main · `484a44c6` | 舊 crypto collector 與資料分區歷史 |
| [TWSE-Tick-Data](submodules/TWSE-Tick-Data) | main · `cc8fd37a` | 揭示檔 schema、parser 與整合實驗 |

各子專案沿用自己的 lock 與執行環境。根目錄不提供共同 uv workspace；Linux/CUDA 研究、服務部署與 Nautilus 升版是後續工作。Ubuntu 已有的 `effortless@daweilee` 和其他 checkout 保留為獨立工作環境，來源及資料依賴見 context。

## 資料與歷史入口

- [Context catalog](context/README.md)：來源、主機、dataset、storage、日期、版本及 evidence 的結構化清冊。

- [歷史摘要](docs/history.md)與[Messenger inbox](context/inbox/README.md)：Notion 歷史來源及日後人工整理聊天脈絡的入口。
- [操作手冊](docs/operations.md)：環境要求、盤點、gzip 比對與清理驗證流程。
