````text
1	---
2	name: skill-author
3	description: Author a new agent skill or refactor an existing one to follow agentskills.io best practices — gotchas sections, output templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity (fragility-based), and agentic script design (--help, --dry-run, structured stdout, stderr diagnostics, PEP 723 inline deps, pinned uvx/npx versions). Use whenever the user wants to create a new skill from scratch, scaffold a SKILL.md, write a reference file, design a script meant to be invoked by an agent, lint a draft skill for quality, or convert an ad-hoc workflow into a reusable skill. For evaluating skill output quality with test cases, benchmarking, or optimizing the description trigger rate, defer to the `skill-creator` skill instead — this skill focuses on authoring, not evaluation.
4	---
5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
43	auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
44	symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.
45	
46	```bash
47	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
48	```
49	
50	Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):
51	
52	| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
55	| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
56	| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |
57	
58	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
59	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
60	
61	> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
62	> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
63	> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
64	> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
65	> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
66	> out without further prompting.
67	
68	After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
69	`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
70	follow-up actions deterministically.
71	
72	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
73	
74	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
75	that matter most:
76	
77	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
78	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
79	  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
80	  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
81	  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
82	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
83	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
84	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
85	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
86	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
87	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
88	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
89	  escape hatches.
90	
91	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
92	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
93	happens"), not just that it exists.
94	
95	### 4. Design any scripts
96	
97	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
98	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
99	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
100	requirements:
101	
102	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
103	- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
104	- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
105	- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
106	- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
107	- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
108	
109	For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
110	`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
111	have to set up an environment first.
112	
113	### 5. Lint
114	
115	Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
116	
117	```bash
118	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
119	```
120	
121	It checks three things:
122	
123	1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
124	   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
125	   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
126	2. **Script hygiene** — shell CLI entrypoints in `scripts/*.sh` need a shebang,
127	   executable mode, and a `--help` handler (presence, not execution). Bash libraries
128	   may declare `# skill-lint: sourced-only` in their leading comment header;
129	   they must be non-executable and pass a parse-only Bash syntax check. Missing
130	   CLI requirements alone do not identify a library. See `references/script-design.md`.
131	3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
132	   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
133	
134	Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.
135	
136	### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator
137	
138	Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
139	quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
140	`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
141	right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
142	skill runs test cases and benchmarks."
143	
144	## Available scripts
145	
146	- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
147	  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
148	  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
149	  table in step 2.
150	  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
151	    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
152	    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
153	  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
154	    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
155	    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
156	    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
157	    symlinks).
158	- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
159	  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
160	  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
161	- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
162	  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
163	  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
164	  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
165	  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
166	  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
167	  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
168	  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
169	    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.
170	
171	## Bundled assets
172	
173	Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:
174	
175	- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
176	- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
177	- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
178	  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
179	  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
180	- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
181	  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.
182	
183	## Reference files
184	
185	- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
186	  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
187	  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
188	- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
189	  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
190	  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
191	- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
192	  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
193	  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.
194	
195	## Gotchas
196	
197	- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
198	  symlink with a real file.
199	- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
200	  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
201	  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
202	- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
203	  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
204	  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
205	- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
206	  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
207	  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
208	  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
209	- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
210	  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
211	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
212	  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
213	  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
214	  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
215	  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
216	  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
217	- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
218	  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
219	  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
220	  investing in authoring.
221	- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
222	  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
223	  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
224	  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
225	  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
226	  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
227	  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
228	- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
229	  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
230	  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
231	  if you ever hand-create one, see
232	  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).
233	
234	## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)
235	
236	Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
237	identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
238	weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
239	check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
240	quantitative validation.
241
````

````text
1	# This-repo conventions
2	
3	Conventions specific to the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repository. Skills
4	authored elsewhere may follow different rules; this file is the source of
5	truth for **this** repo.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	skills/
11	├── local/             # skills authored in this repo (committed in full)
12	│   └── <skill-name>/
13	│       ├── SKILL.md
14	│       ├── references/
15	│       ├── scripts/
16	│       └── assets/
17	└── vendor/            # skills cherry-picked from upstream repos
18	    └── <skill-name>/
19	        └── ...        # synced via scripts/sync-vendor.sh
20	```
21	
22	- **Skills maintained in this repo go in `skills/local/`.** For a skill maintained
23	  alongside another first-party project, scaffold with `--project --root <project>`
24	  there and import its distribution copy into `skills/owned/` using the shared
25	  `vendor.yaml` manifest (`collection: owned`). See `docs/workflows/adding-owned-skills.md`
26	  in this repo. Do not maintain two canonical copies.
27	- **Don't manually edit anything in `skills/vendor/`** — it gets overwritten by
28	  the next `make sync`. Upstream changes go through `vendor.yaml` + `make sync`.
29	- **`.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at the repo root are active
30	  discovery-symlink farms**, not legacy. Each entry under them is a relative
31	  symlink (`../../skills/local/<name>` or `../../skills/vendor/<name>`) so
32	  that Cursor / Codex / Warp / OpenCode (`.agents/skills/`) and Claude Code
33	  (`.claude/skills/`) can dogfood the skills authored in this repo. The
34	  `new-skill.sh` scaffolder creates these symlinks automatically in **LOCAL
35	  mode**; never add new *canonical* skill content directly under them here.
36	
37	## `new-skill.sh` placement scopes
38	
39	`scripts/new-skill.sh` supports three placement scopes that mirror the
40	behavior of `npx skills add` (`vercel-labs/skills`). Auto-detection
41	precedence (when no flag given):
42	
43	1. **LOCAL** — publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml`, `skills/local/`, or
44	   `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) found walking up. This is the
45	   default *inside this very repo*. Canonical content lives in
46	   `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with
47	   `--vendor`); the script adds the `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`
48	   discovery symlinks for you.
49	2. **PROJECT** — a git root found walking up. Canonical content goes to
50	   `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents like Cursor / Codex /
51	   OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot read this directly); a relative
52	   symlink `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>` is
53	   added for Claude Code, plus links for any other non-universal agent dir
54	   (e.g. `.windsurf/`, `.continue/`) that already exists at the repo root.
55	3. **GLOBAL** — neither anchor found, or `--global` forced. Same shape as
56	   PROJECT but rooted at `$HOME`: canonical at `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`,
57	   plus `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and any other already-present
58	   `~/.<agent>/skills/` link.
59	
60	The fan-out rule is "claude-code always, others only if their config root
61	already exists at the base dir" — this mirrors `npx skills add`'s
62	"don't create `.windsurf/` unless the project already uses Windsurf"
63	behavior. The script never creates a new top-level agent home dir.
64	
65	Symlinks are always *relative* with a fixed `../../` prefix because both
66	the link's parent (`.../skills/`) and the canonical dir
67	(`.../.agents/skills/` or `.../skills/local/`) are exactly two levels under
68	the base dir. See [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md)
69	for the historical bug this convention prevents.
70	
71	## Skill discovery
72	
73	The `skills` CLI looks for `SKILL.md` files like this:
74	
75	1. **First pass:** one level deep — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
76	2. **Fallback:** recursive up to **5 levels** if first pass found nothing
77	   useful.
78	
79	That's why `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md`
80	both work — they're 2 levels deep, well within the recursive fallback. **Don't
81	nest a skill more than 5 levels deep** or it becomes invisible.
82	
83	## Scripts naming and mirroring
84	
85	Some scripts are bundled into a skill **and** mirrored to `scripts/` at repo
86	root. The pattern:
87	
88	| Canonical location | Mirror |
89	|---|---|
90	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/add-todo.sh` | `scripts/add-todo.sh` |
91	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` | `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` |
92	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/promote-todo.sh` | `scripts/promote-todo.sh` |
93	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/todo-kanban.sh` | `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` |
94	
95	Reason: the canonical copy travels with the skill (downstream consumers get it
96	via `init.sh`). The root-level mirror is for *this* repo's own use so `make`
97	targets and CI don't have to know the skill's path.
98	
99	**Mirrors must stay byte-identical.** If you edit one, run the equivalent
100	`cp` to update the other and verify with `diff`. There is currently no
101	automated check for this — be careful.
102	
103	## Documentation
104	
105	- `README.md` — short repo entrypoint with install snippet.
106	- `docs/` — built into a MkDocs Material site at
107	  `https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/`.
108	- `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` — user-facing docs for each local skill. Link
109	  back to the canonical SKILL.md on GitHub via absolute URL (see linking rules
110	  in `docs/reference/docs-stack-recipe.md`).
111	
112	When you add a new local skill, also add:
113	
114	1. A row to `docs/skills/index.md`.
115	2. A `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` page (can be short; cross-link to SKILL.md).
116	3. A nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`.
117	4. A row to the README's "What's in here" table.
118	
119	## Project memory
120	
121	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` skill on itself. That means:
122	
123	- `TODO.md` is structured (P1/P2/P3/P?/Done sections, validated by
124	  `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`).
125	- `backlog/inbox.md` is the loose-capture inbox.
126	- `backlog/<slug>.md` holds research notes for non-trivial items.
127	- `pitfalls/<slug>.md` holds debugging traps with symptom-first titles.
128	
129	When authoring a skill, if you discover a non-obvious trap, write it to
130	`pitfalls/`. Don't bury it in commit messages or chat history.
131	
132	## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
133	
134	`AGENTS.md` is a **symlink** to `CLAUDE.md`. Edit either one. Don't replace
135	the symlink with a real file or they'll drift.
136	
137	## Bash compatibility
138	
139	All bundled scripts must be **bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). See
140	`script-design.md` § "Bash 3.2 compatibility" for the safe subset and
141	escape hatches.
142	
143	## When this repo's conventions conflict with agentskills.io
144	
145	The agentskills.io best practices are upstream / generic; this file is local /
146	specific. When they conflict, this file wins **for skills authored in this
147	repo**. Notable specifics:
148	
149	- We default to bundling helper scripts in `scripts/` rather than relying on
150	  ad-hoc `uvx` invocations, because we want the helpers to compose with the
151	  repo's `Makefile` and CI.
152	- We use Bash for orchestration scripts (TODO management, vendor sync) so they
153	  run without a Python environment. PEP 723 Python is fine for analytical or
154	  parsing-heavy helpers.
155	- Skill descriptions in this repo lean **even pushier** than the agentskills.io
156	  guidance because we're optimizing for the OpenCode/Claude Code default
157	  triggering behavior, which under-triggers more aggressively than Claude.ai.
158
````
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# lint-skill.sh — Lint a skill directory for quality issues.
3	#
4	# Checks:
5	#   1. Frontmatter & length     — name + description present, description has
6	#                                  "use when" trigger phrasing, portable
7	#                                  name/description lengths, SKILL.md < 500 lines.
8	#   2. Script hygiene           — shell CLIs need shebang, +x, --help; explicitly
9	#                                  sourced-only Bash libraries need syntax and -x off.
10	#   3. Reference reachability   — every references/*.md is mentioned in SKILL.md.
11	#
12	# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS).
13	
14	set -euo pipefail
15	
16	usage() {
17	  cat <<'EOF'
18	Usage: lint-skill.sh [OPTIONS] <skill-dir>
19	
20	Lint a skill directory against agentskills.io best practices.
21	
22	Options:
23	  --strict           Treat warnings as errors.
24	  --quiet            Only print failures (suppress 'ok' lines).
25	  --json             Emit a JSON summary on stdout (in addition to human output).
26	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
27	
28	Examples:
29	  bash lint-skill.sh skills/local/my-skill
30	  bash lint-skill.sh --strict skills/local/my-skill
31	  bash lint-skill.sh --json skills/local/my-skill | jq
32	
33	Exit codes:
34	  0  all checks passed (warnings allowed unless --strict)
35	  1  invalid arguments
36	  2  skill directory not found or missing SKILL.md
37	  3  one or more lint errors
38	EOF
39	}
40	
41	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
42	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
43	
44	STRICT=0
45	QUIET=0
46	JSON=0
47	SKILL_DIR=""
48	
49	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
50	  case "$1" in
51	    --strict)  STRICT=1; shift ;;
52	    --quiet)   QUIET=1; shift ;;
53	    --json)    JSON=1; shift ;;
54	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
55	    -*)        die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
56	    *)
57	      if [ -n "$SKILL_DIR" ]; then
58	        die "only one skill directory allowed (got '$SKILL_DIR' and '$1')" 1
59	      fi
60	      SKILL_DIR="$1"; shift
61	      ;;
62	  esac
63	done
64	
65	[ -n "$SKILL_DIR" ] || die "missing <skill-dir> (try --help)" 1
66	[ -d "$SKILL_DIR" ] || die "not a directory: $SKILL_DIR" 2
67	[ -f "$SKILL_DIR/SKILL.md" ] || die "no SKILL.md in $SKILL_DIR" 2
68	
69	ERRORS=0
70	WARNINGS=0
71	ERROR_MSGS=()
72	WARNING_MSGS=()
73	
74	emit_ok()   { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '  ok    %s\n' "$*"; }
75	emit_note() { [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '  note  %s\n' "$*"; }
76	emit_warn() {
77	  printf '  WARN  %s\n' "$*"
78	  WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1))
79	  WARNING_MSGS+=("$*")
80	}
81	emit_err()  {
82	  printf '  FAIL  %s\n' "$*"
83	  ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1))
84	  ERROR_MSGS+=("$*")
85	}
86	
87	extract_frontmatter_value() {
88	  # Minimal YAML scalar extractor for top-level SKILL.md frontmatter.
89	  # Handles single-line values plus folded/literal blocks (`>-`, `|`).
90	  awk -v key="$1" '
91	    function trim(s) {
92	      gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s)
93	      return s
94	    }
95	    function unquote(s) {
96	      s = trim(s)
97	      if ((s ~ /^".*"$/) || (s ~ /^'\''.*'\''$/)) {
98	        return substr(s, 2, length(s) - 2)
99	      }
100	      return s
101	    }
102	    function flush() {
103	      if (found) {
104	        gsub(/[ \t]+/, " ", value)
105	        print trim(value)
106	        exit
107	      }
108	    }
109	    NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { in_fm = 1; next }
110	    in_fm && $0 == "---" { flush(); exit }
111	    !in_fm { next }
112	    found {
113	      if ($0 ~ /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:[ \t]*/) {
114	        flush()
115	      }
116	      if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]+/) {
117	        line = $0
118	        sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line)
119	        if (value != "") value = value " "
120	        value = value line
121	        next
122	      }
123	      flush()
124	    }
125	    $0 ~ "^" key ":[ \t]*" {
126	      found = 1
127	      value = $0
128	      sub("^" key ":[ \t]*", "", value)
129	      if (value ~ /^[>|][+-]?$/) {
130	        value = ""
131	        next
132	      }
133	      print unquote(value)
134	      exit
135	    }
136	  ' "$SKILL_MD"
137	}
138	
139	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
140	# Check 1: Frontmatter & length
141	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
142	echo "Frontmatter & length:"
143	
144	SKILL_MD="$SKILL_DIR/SKILL.md"
145	
146	# Extract frontmatter (between first two `---` lines).
147	FM_START=$(awk '/^---$/{print NR; exit}' "$SKILL_MD" || true)
148	FM_END=$(awk -v start="${FM_START:-0}" 'NR>start && /^---$/{print NR; exit}' "$SKILL_MD" || true)
149	
150	if [ -z "$FM_START" ] || [ -z "$FM_END" ] || [ "$FM_START" != "1" ]; then
151	  emit_err "SKILL.md missing YAML frontmatter (must start with '---' on line 1)"
152	else
153	  emit_ok "frontmatter delimiters present"
154	
155	  FM=$(sed -n "${FM_START},${FM_END}p" "$SKILL_MD")
156	
157	  # Real-parser gate. The awk extractor below is permissive; harnesses
158	  # (`npx skills`, Claude Code, Cursor) are not — they skip a skill whose
159	  # frontmatter fails to parse. Delegate to the sibling batch linter.
160	  FM_LINTER="$(dirname "$0")/lint-frontmatter.sh"
161	  if [ -f "$FM_LINTER" ]; then
162	    if FM_OUT=$(bash "$FM_LINTER" --quiet "$SKILL_MD" 2>&1); then
163	      emit_ok "frontmatter parses as YAML"
164	    else
165	      while IFS= read -r fm_line; do
166	        case "$fm_line" in
167	          FAIL*|checked*|'') continue ;;
168	          *) emit_err "frontmatter: $(printf '%s' "$fm_line" | sed 's/^ *//')" ;;
169	        esac
170	      done <<EOF
171	$FM_OUT
172	EOF
173	    fi
174	  else
175	    emit_note "lint-frontmatter.sh not found next to this script; skipping the YAML parse check"
176	  fi
177	
178	  NAME=$(extract_frontmatter_value name)
179	  if [ -n "$NAME" ]; then
180	    emit_ok "name field present: $NAME"
181	    NAME_LEN=${#NAME}
182	    if [ "$NAME_LEN" -gt 64 ]; then
183	      emit_err "name is too long (${NAME_LEN} chars); portable maximum is 64"
184	    else
185	      emit_ok "name length is ${NAME_LEN} chars (<=64)"
186	    fi
187	    if printf '%s\n' "$NAME" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$'; then
188	      emit_ok "name is portable hyphen-case"
189	    else
190	      emit_err "name must be lowercase hyphen-case: letters, digits, single hyphens; no leading/trailing hyphen"
191	    fi
192	    # Compare against directory basename.
193	    BASENAME=$(basename "$SKILL_DIR")
194	    if [ "$NAME" != "$BASENAME" ]; then
195	      emit_warn "name '$NAME' does not match directory '$BASENAME'"
196	    fi
197	    # Reject placeholder.
198	    case "$NAME" in
199	      *PLACEHOLDER*) emit_err "name still contains PLACEHOLDER text" ;;
200	    esac
201	  else
202	    emit_err "frontmatter missing 'name:' field"
203	  fi
204	
205	  DESC=$(extract_frontmatter_value description)
206	  if [ -n "$DESC" ]; then
207	    DESC_LEN=${#DESC}
208	    emit_ok "description field present (${DESC_LEN} chars)"
209	    case "$DESC" in
210	      *PLACEHOLDER*) emit_err "description still contains PLACEHOLDER text" ;;
211	    esac
212	    # Check for trigger-phrase signal.
213	    if printf '%s\n' "$DESC" | grep -qiE '\b(use when|use whenever|use this|trigger|invoke when)\b'; then
214	      emit_ok "description includes trigger phrase ('use when' or similar)"
215	    else
216	      emit_warn "description lacks an explicit trigger phrase like 'Use when...'; this hurts triggering"
217	    fi
218	    # Length sanity.
219	    if [ "$DESC_LEN" -lt 80 ]; then
220	      emit_warn "description is short (${DESC_LEN} chars); consider naming more concrete trigger contexts"
221	    elif [ "$DESC_LEN" -lt 120 ]; then
222	      emit_note "description is ${DESC_LEN} chars; 120-500 chars is the preferred trigger budget"
223	    elif [ "$DESC_LEN" -le 500 ]; then
224	      emit_ok "description is in the preferred 120-500 char budget"
225	    elif [ "$DESC_LEN" -le 900 ]; then
226	      emit_note "description is ${DESC_LEN} chars: valid but context-heavy (yellow tier)"
227	    elif [ "$DESC_LEN" -le 1024 ]; then
228	      emit_note "description is ${DESC_LEN} chars: valid but close to the 1024-char hard limit (orange tier)"
229	    else
230	      emit_err "description is too long (${DESC_LEN} chars); Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned maximum is 1024"
231	    fi
232	  else
233	    emit_err "frontmatter missing 'description:' field"
234	  fi
235	fi
236	
237	# Length check.
238	LINES=$(wc -l < "$SKILL_MD" | tr -d ' ')
239	if [ "$LINES" -lt 500 ]; then

241	elif [ "$LINES" -lt 700 ]; then
242	  emit_warn "SKILL.md is ${LINES} lines (recommended <500; move detail to references/)"
243	else
244	  emit_err "SKILL.md is ${LINES} lines (>700 is hurting context budget; split into references/)"
245	fi
246	
247	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
248	# Check 2: Script hygiene
249	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
250	echo
251	echo "Script hygiene:"
252	
253	if [ -d "$SKILL_DIR/scripts" ]; then
254	  HAS_SCRIPTS=0
255	  for script in "$SKILL_DIR"/scripts/*.sh; do
256	    [ -e "$script" ] || continue

261	    # library. Never infer this from a missing shebang/+x or source the file.

263	      /^[[:space:]]*$/ { next }

265	      /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
266	      { exit }

304	  # Also lint .py scripts for shebang/+x/argparse-help.

307	    HAS_SCRIPTS=1

309	
310	    FIRST_LINE=$(head -n1 "$script")
311	    case "$FIRST_LINE" in
312	      "#!"*) emit_ok "$NAME has shebang" ;;
313	      *)     emit_warn "$NAME missing shebang (less critical for .py if invoked via 'python …' / 'uv run …')" ;;
314	    esac
315	
316	    if [ -x "$script" ]; then
317	      emit_ok "$NAME is executable"
318	    else
319	      emit_warn "$NAME is not executable"
320	    fi
321	
322	    if grep -qE 'argparse|click|typer|--help' "$script"; then
323	      emit_ok "$NAME appears to expose --help"
324	    else
325	      emit_warn "$NAME has no obvious --help mechanism"
326	    fi
327	  done

```text
# `.gitmodules` keys (verbatim from the gitmodules page)

**`submodule.<name>.path`**
> Defines the path, relative to the top-level directory of the Git working tree, where the submodule is expected to be checked out. The path name must not end with a `/`. All submodule paths must be unique within the `.gitmodules` file.

**`submodule.<name>.url`**
> Defines a URL from which the submodule repository can be cloned. This may be either an absolute URL ready to be passed to git-clone[1] or (if it begins with `./` or `../`) a location relative to the superproject's origin repository.

**`submodule.<name>.update`**
> Defines the default update procedure for the named submodule, i.e. how the submodule is updated by the `git submodule update` command in the superproject. This is only used by `git submodule init` to initialize the configuration variable of the same name. Allowed values here are _checkout_, _rebase_, _merge_ or _none_, but not _!command_ (for security reasons). See the description of the _update_ command in git-submodule[1] for more details.

**`submodule.<name>.branch`**
> A remote branch name for tracking updates in the upstream submodule. If the option is not specified, it defaults to the remote `HEAD`. A special value of `.` is used to indicate that the name of the branch in the submodule should be the same name as the current branch in the current repository. See the `--remote` documentation in git-submodule[1] for details.

**`submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules`**
> This option can be used to control recursive fetching of this submodule. If this option is also present in the submodule's entry in `.git/config` of the superproject, the setting there will override the one found in `.gitmodules`. Both settings can be overridden on the command line by using the `--[no-]recurse-submodules` option to `git fetch` and `git pull`.

**`submodule.<name>.ignore`**
> Defines under what circumstances `git status` and the diff family show a submodule as modified. The following values are supported:
>
> - **all**: The submodule will never be considered modified (but will nonetheless show up in the output of status and commit when it has been staged). Adding a submodule with (`new commits`) can be overridden using _git add --force <submodule.path>_. This setting affects `status`, `update-index`, `diff` and `log` (due to underlying `diff`).
> - **dirty**: All changes to the submodule's work tree will be ignored, only committed differences between the `HEAD` of the submodule and its recorded state in the superproject are taken into account.
> - **untracked**: Only untracked files in submodules will be ignored. Committed differences and modifications to tracked files will show up.
> - **none**: No modifications to submodules are ignored, all of committed differences, and modifications to tracked and untracked files are shown. This is the default option.
>
> If this option is also present in the submodule's entry in `.git/config` of the superproject, the setting there will override the one found in `.gitmodules`. Both settings can be overridden on the command line by using the `--ignore-submodules` option. The `git submodule` commands are not affected by this setting.

**`submodule.<name>.shallow`**
> When set to true, a clone of this submodule will be performed as a shallow clone (with a history depth of 1) unless the user explicitly asks for a non-shallow clone.

# Where each key is honored

| Key | Set in `.gitmodules` | Page-documented `.git/config` behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | Yes | Not addressed on this page |
| `url` | Yes | Not addressed on this page |
| `update` | Yes (`checkout`, `rebase`, `merge`, `none` only) | Only used by `git submodule init` to seed the `.git/config` variable. `!command` is rejected in `.gitmodules`. |
| `branch` | Yes | Not addressed on this page |
| `fetchRecurseSubmodules` | Yes | `.git/config` entry **overrides** `.gitmodules` |
| `ignore` | Yes | `.git/config` entry **overrides** `.gitmodules` |
| `shallow` | Yes | Not addressed on this page |

Notes:
- The page documents only two keys where `.git/config` takes precedence over `.gitmodules`: `fetchRecurseSubmodules` and `ignore`. Both can also be overridden on the command line.
- For `update`, the value is copied into `.git/config` by `git submodule init`, so the effective setting comes from there. The `!command` form is only accepted in `.git/config`, not in `.gitmodules`.
- The page does not say whether `path`, `url`, `branch`, or `shallow` can be overridden in `.git/config`. Check git-submodule[1] or git-config[1] before relying on that.
- `.gitmodules` cannot be a symbolic link in a working tree. Git refuses to check out such an entry.
```

```text
The content you pasted is cut off at "[Content truncated due to length...]" right where the `pushRepoLooksLikeRef` advice entry begins. The `submodule.*`, `status.submoduleSummary`, `diff.submodule`, `push.recurseSubmodules`, `fetch.recurseSubmodules`, and `extensions.worktreeConfig` definitions aren't in the text I received, so I can't quote them verbatim.

You can get the exact text from the full page at https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config (search for "submodule.recurse" or "extensions.worktreeConfig"), or from `git help config` on a machine with Git installed.

From my general knowledge of Git, these are summaries, not quotes, and may differ in wording or detail from the current manual:

- **`submodule.recurse`**: Boolean (default `false`). If true, commands that support `--recurse-submodules` (such as `checkout`, `fetch`, `grep`, `pull`, `push`, `read-tree`, `reset`, `restore`, `switch`) recurse into submodules by default.
- **`submodule.<name>.update`**: How `git submodule update` integrates the superproject's recorded commit. Values are `checkout` (default), `rebase`, `merge`, `none`, or `!command`.
- **`submodule.<name>.branch`**: The remote branch that `git submodule update --remote` tracks for this submodule. Defaults to the remote's HEAD.
- **`submodule.<name>.ignore`**: Controls which submodule changes are reported by `status` and `diff`. Values are `all`, `dirty`, `untracked`, or `none` (default).
- **`submodule.<name>.active`**: Boolean that marks whether the submodule is active. Inactive submodules are skipped by most submodule commands.
- **`submodule.propagateBranches`**: Experimental. When true, branch operations with `--recurse-submodules` also create or update matching branches in submodules. Default `false`.
- **`status.submoduleSummary`**: Boolean or integer. When enabled, `status` and the commit message editor show a summary of commits in changed submodules. An integer sets a maximum number of lines.
- **`diff.submodule`**: Format for submodule diffs. Values are `short` (default, shows only the commit range), `log` (shows the commit log), or `diff` (shows the inline diff).
- **`push.recurseSubmodules`**: Behavior when pushing a superproject with changed submodules. Values are `check` (refuse to push if submodule commits haven't been pushed), `on-demand` (push changed submodules first), `only` (push submodules but not the superproject), or `no` (default, ignore submodules).
- **`fetch.recurseSubmodules`**: Whether `fetch` recurses into submodules. Values are `on-demand` (default, fetch only submodules whose recorded commits are missing), `true` (always fetch), or `false` (never fetch).
- **`extensions.worktreeConfig`**: A repository extension that, when enabled, lets each linked worktree keep its own config in `$GIT_DIR/config.worktree`, which is read and written with `git config --worktree`.

# Superproject justfile workflow

The root `justfile` is an orchestration layer for the five sibling submodules. It
keeps each repository's own task runner. Its main job is to ensure
that a chezmoi command launched from `dotfiles-all` uses the checkout being
edited instead of the separate live source clone.

Run `just --list` from the superproject root to see the available recipes.

## Native chezmoi source

The native recipes choose one source from the host OS:

| Host | Source |
|---|---|
| macOS | `dotfiles-unix/` |
| Linux | `dotfiles-unix/` |
| WSL | `dotfiles-unix/` |
| native Windows | `dotfiles-windows/` |

The source path is derived from the justfile's own directory, so the recipes
remain correct even when `just` discovers the file from a child directory.

```bash
just apply
just diff
just status
just dry-run
```

`apply`, `diff`, `status`, and `dry-run` pass extra targets or flags after the
recipe name through to chezmoi:

```bash
just apply ~/.config/tmux
just dry-run --exclude=scripts
```

`apply-unix` and `apply-windows` make the selected checkout explicit, but each
recipe is available only on its native OS. There is intentionally no override
that applies Windows templates to a Unix home, or Unix templates to native
Windows. Windows apply keeps the submodule's existing `--init` behaviour.

## Validation without cross-OS deployment

`just check` selects the native suite:

- Unix: the `dotfiles` lint and Bats recipes, followed by a source-pinned
  chezmoi dry-run.
- Windows: PSScriptAnalyzer, Pester, and the strict MkDocs build from
  `dotfiles-windows`.

On macOS or Linux, `just check-windows` runs the same static Windows checks when
`pwsh` and `uv` are installed. It never runs chezmoi apply or Windows run-scripts;
`windows-latest` CI remains the real deployment gate.

Other platform-specific recipes still belong to the submodule task runners.
Run them from inside that submodule. In particular, do not substitute an inner
bare `just apply` for the root recipe: the inner recipes assume their checkout
is the live chezmoi source directory.
just gitlink-review
```

The staging recipes fail unless every selected inner worktree and index is
clean, including untracked files, and its HEAD is reachable from the local
`origin/main`. `gitlink-review` repeats those checks against the commits staged
in the outer index and prints:

```bash
git diff --cached --submodule=log -- dotfiles-unix dotfiles-windows dotfiles-iSH dotfiles-OpenWrt dotfiles-Termux
```

These helpers never pull, commit, or push, and never stage outer documentation
or unrelated files. Review and commit the remaining outer changes manually.

## Lightweight targets and renamed gitlinks

`dotfiles-unix/` is only a local path change; GitHub remains `daviddwlee84/dotfiles`.
All submodule status/fetch/pull/diff helpers include iSH, OpenWrt and Termux. `gitlink-stage-all`
requires all five inner repos clean and reachable from origin/main. Individual
recipes also include `gitlink-stage-ish`, `gitlink-stage-openwrt`, and `gitlink-stage-termux`.
The review handles newly added or renamed gitlinks absent from the old HEAD tree;
its diff includes the deleted legacy `dotfiles` path during this migration.

`just check` retains the primary native gate. `just check-ish` and
`just check-openwrt` run independent host validation on macOS/Linux; they do not
apply to those devices. `just check-superproject` uses disposable local Git repos.
Full Unix apply/diff/status/dry-run reject iSH/OpenWrt/Android markers rather than treating
those targets as supported general Linux. Use each target's standalone bootstrap.

## Android provisioning

The macOS/Linux host entrypoints forward to the public Termux repository:

```sh
just termux-host-deps --install
just termux-devices
just termux-setup --serial DEVICE_SERIAL
just termux-ssh --serial DEVICE_SERIAL
just termux-doctor --serial DEVICE_SERIAL
just check-termux
````

[project]
name = "alpha-research"
version = "0.0.1"
description = "Cross-sectional equity alpha research: ranking, portfolio construction, backtest, evaluation"
readme = "README.md"
authors = [{ name = "Da-Wei Lee", email = "daviddwlee84@gmail.com" }]
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "alpha-risk-kit[plots]",
    "quant-data-kit",
    "pandas>=2.2",
    "numpy>=1.26",
    "scipy>=1.11",
    "pyarrow>=16",
    "duckdb>=1.1",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "matplotlib>=3.8",
    "tabulate>=0.9",
]

[project.scripts]
alpha-run = "alpha_research.workflow:main"
alpha-compare = "alpha_research.compare:main"
alpha-log = "alpha_research.workflow:log_main"
alpha-walk = "alpha_research.walkforward:main"
alpha-features = "alpha_research.feature_report:main"

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["pytest>=8.0", "ruff>=0.6"]
research = ["marimo>=0.9", "mlflow>=2.16"]
# rankers (plug-and-play models in alpha_research.models)
ml = [
    "catboost>=1.2",
    "lightgbm>=4.3",
    "xgboost>=3.0",
    "scikit-learn>=1.5",
    "torch>=2.4",
    # imported by XGBoost when GPU external memory (data.streaming) gets device arrays
    "cupy-cuda12x>=13; sys_platform == 'linux'",
]
# feature store (featurelab panel profile, ADR 0007); featurelab needs Python >= 3.13 (Colab stays 3.12)
features = ["featurelab; python_version >= '3.13'"]  # quant-data-kit comes from the main deps (featurelab[qdk] would pull its git URL)
# portfolio optimization beyond the scipy LP (alpha_research.portfolio, ADR 0005): power-cone impact
opt = ["cvxpy>=1.5", "clarabel>=0.9", "mosek>=11"]
docs = [
    # Cap below the next major: MkDocs 2.0 removes the plugin system
    # (see mkdocs-site-bootstrap skill references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md).
    "mkdocs>=1.6,<2",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10",
    "mkdocs-llmstxt>=0.2",
    "mkdocs-copy-to-llm>=0.1",
    "pymdown-extensions>=10.7",
]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = ["dev", "research", "docs", "ml", "opt", "features"]

[tool.uv.sources]
alpha-risk-kit = { path = "libs/alpha-risk-kit", editable = true }
quant-data-kit = { path = "libs/quant-data-kit", editable = true }
featurelab = { path = "libs/featurelab", editable = true }

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/alpha_research"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = ["libs", "knowledge", "references", "experiments", "docs", ".specstory", ".claude"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "W"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# marimo notebooks: long zh-TW markdown / labels
"notebooks/*.py" = ["E501"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["alpha_research", "alpha_risk_kit", "quant_data_kit"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = "-m 'not network'"
markers = ["network: hits live data providers (run with -m network)"]
-----

services:

----- precommit
# Pre-commit hooks. Private repo: no secret scanning / redaction for now (2026-10-31);
# credentials still live only in `.env` (gitignored). Re-add gitleaks before making anything public.
#
# See https://pre-commit.com

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v5.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-added-large-files
        args: ['--maxkb=4096']
      - id: check-merge-conflict
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
        exclude: ^\.specstory/
      - id: trailing-whitespace
        args: [--markdown-linebreak-ext=md]
        exclude: ^\.specstory/
# Pre-commit hooks for the dotfiles-all superproject.
#
# Scope: only files tracked at THIS level (CLAUDE.md, docs/, .specstory/,
# .claude/plans/). The submodules run their own, richer stacks — commits made
# inside dotfiles/ or dotfiles-windows/ are covered there, not here.
#
# The redaction hook is pulled from the published agent-skills repo (same as
# dotfiles-windows) rather than vendoring scripts/redact_secrets.py, so there
# is no local copy to drift. Bump with `pre-commit autoupdate`.
#
# Install: pre-commit install    Run over everything: pre-commit run --all-files

repos:
  # Auto-redact leaked secrets in agent artifacts BEFORE gitleaks runs. If a
  # file is rewritten, pre-commit reports "files were modified by this hook"
  # and you must `git add` + re-commit — same UX as trailing-whitespace.
  - repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
    rev: ahh-v1.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: redact-agent-secrets

  # Gitleaks — block the commit when an unallowlisted secret is detected.
  # Config: .gitleaks.toml (agent-history-hygiene portable subset).
  - repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
    rev: v8.22.1
    hooks:
      # System-installed gitleaks; avoids the Go toolchain build.
      - id: gitleaks-system
        pass_filenames: false

  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v5.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-private-key
      # 8 MB, matching the dotfiles repo: the binding constraint is SpecStory
      # transcripts, which are plain markdown and grow with session length.
      # The cap still catches what it is for — a binary or dataset landing
      # here by accident.
      - id: check-added-large-files
        args: ['--maxkb=20000']
      - id: check-merge-conflict
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
        exclude: ^\.specstory/
      - id: trailing-whitespace
        args: [--markdown-linebreak-ext=md]
        exclude: ^\.specstory/
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-json

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# new-skill.sh — Scaffold a new agent skill in the npx-skills-compatible layout.
#
# Three placement scopes (auto-detected by default, override with --local /
# --project / --global):
#
#   LOCAL    Publishing-repo workflow (this very repo). Canonical content lives
#            under <repo>/skills/local/<name>/ (or skills/vendor/<name>/ with
#            --vendor), and discovery symlinks are added at
#            <repo>/.agents/skills/<name> and <repo>/.claude/skills/<name>
#            -> ../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>.
#
#   PROJECT  Generic per-project install. Canonical content at
#            <repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/ (universal agents like Cursor /
#            Codex / OpenCode / Warp pick this up directly), plus a relative
#            symlink at <repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>
#            (and other already-present non-universal agent dirs).
#
#   GLOBAL   System-wide install. Canonical content at ~/.agents/skills/<name>/
#            plus a relative symlink at ~/.claude/skills/<name> ->
#            ../../.agents/skills/<name> (and any other detected agent dir).
#
# Auto-detection precedence (when no scope flag given):
#   1. publishing repo (vendor.yaml, skills/local/, or
#      skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json found walking up) -> LOCAL
#   2. inside a git repo (.git found walking up)                 -> PROJECT
#   3. otherwise                                                 -> GLOBAL
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS — no mapfile, no ${var,,},
# no [[ -v var ]]).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
ASSETS_DIR="$SKILL_DIR/assets"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: new-skill.sh [OPTIONS] <skill-name>

Scaffold a new agent skill with the standard layout (SKILL.md, references/,
scripts/, assets/) seeded from skill-author's templates, then place it where
the active scope says it belongs and add discovery symlinks for non-universal
agents.

Scope (mutually exclusive — auto-detected if omitted):
  --local            Force LOCAL mode (this publishing repo's skills/local/).
                     Requires a vendor.yaml / skills/local/ / skills/.claude-plugin
                     anchor walking up from --root or CWD.
  --project          Force PROJECT mode (<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/).
                     Requires a git repo root (.git) walking up.
  --global           Force GLOBAL mode (~/.agents/skills/<name>/).

Other options:
  --vendor           In LOCAL mode, place under skills/vendor/<name>/ instead of
                     skills/local/. (Rare — vendored skills normally come via
                     vendor.yaml + scripts/sync-vendor.sh.)
  --root DIR         Override repo / project root discovery.
  --no-symlinks      Skip the agent-dir discovery symlinks (just write the
                     canonical dir). Useful for CI / packaging tests.
  --dry-run          Print what would be created without writing.
  --force            Overwrite if the target canonical directory already exists.
                     Existing symlinks are always replaced.
  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.

Examples:
  bash new-skill.sh my-skill                # auto-detect scope
  bash new-skill.sh --project my-skill      # force project (.agents/skills)
  bash new-skill.sh --global my-skill       # force user-wide (~/.agents/skills)
  bash new-skill.sh --local my-skill        # force skills/local/ (publish repo)
  bash new-skill.sh --dry-run my-skill      # see what would happen
  bash new-skill.sh --root /path/to/repo my-skill

Output:
  Single JSON object on stdout (parseable by an agent), prose on stderr.
  Keys: skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[].

Exit codes:
  0  success

````text
# Scaffold the canonical directory
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Mode:      $MODE"
log "Base:      $BASE_DIR"
log "Canonical: $CANONICAL_DIR"

create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR"
create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/references"
create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/scripts"
create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/assets"

write_template "$ASSETS_DIR/SKILL.md.template" "$CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md"
substitute "$CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md"

# .gitkeep so empty subdirs survive `git add`.
if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "0" ]; then
  for sub in references scripts assets; do
    if [ -z "$(ls -A "$CANONICAL_DIR/$sub" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
      : > "$CANONICAL_DIR/$sub/.gitkeep"
    fi
  done
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fan-out symlinks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
SYMLINKS_CREATED=""
TARGET_SUFFIX="$(target_suffix_for_mode)"

if [ "$NO_SYMLINKS" = "1" ]; then
  log "Symlinks:  skipped (--no-symlinks)"
else
  if [ "$MODE" = "local" ]; then
    # In LOCAL mode also add the .agents/skills convenience link in addition to
    # .claude/skills, because this repo dogfoods .agents/skills as a discovery
    # farm even though it isn't a "consumer install".
    link_into "$BASE_DIR/.agents/skills" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"
  fi

  # claude-code: always fanned out (most-used non-universal agent).
  link_into "$BASE_DIR/.claude/skills" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"

  # Other non-universal agents: only if their config root already exists at
  # $BASE_DIR (mirrors upstream's "don't create .windsurf/ unless present"
  # rule). Use a heredoc rather than a pipe so the while-loop runs in the
  # parent shell — preserves SYMLINKS_CREATED mutations and lets `die` exit
  # the script.
  while IFS='|' read -r root_dir sub; do
    [ -n "$root_dir" ] || continue
    case "$root_dir" in \#*) continue ;; esac
    if [ -d "$BASE_DIR/$root_dir" ]; then
      link_into "$BASE_DIR/$root_dir/$sub" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"
    fi
  done <<EOF
$NONUNIVERSAL_AGENTS_IF_PRESENT
EOF
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structured success output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
  log "Dry run complete. Re-run without --dry-run to actually create files."
  exit 0
fi

# Build a JSON array of symlinks for the structured output. bash 3.2 safe.
json_symlinks() {
  printf '['
  local first=1 line
  # Read from a temp string; the while-loop body runs in the parent shell
  # because we use here-string, so we can mutate `first`.
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
    if [ "$first" = "1" ]; then first=0; else printf ','; fi
    # line is "<link> -> <target>" — keep that as a single string.
    printf '"%s"' "$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')"
  done <<EOF
$SYMLINKS_CREATED
EOF
  printf ']'
}

NEXT_STEPS="\"Edit $CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md to fill in description and workflow\",\"Run lint-skill.sh $CANONICAL_DIR to verify\""

printf '{"skill":"%s","mode":"%s","canonical":"%s","symlinks":%s,"next_steps":[%s]}\n' \
  "$NAME" "$MODE" "$CANONICAL_DIR" "$(json_symlinks)" "$NEXT_STEPS"
     1	# Creating local skills
     2	
     3	A local skill is a custom-authored skill maintained in this repo under
     4	[`skills/local/<skill-name>/`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local).
     5	
     6	## Scaffold a new skill
     7	
     8	Use the bundled scaffolder (recommended — seeds the full agentskills.io
     9	best-practice layout and fans out the discovery symlinks for non-universal
    10	agents):
    11	
    12	```bash
    13	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
    14	```
    15	
    16	The script picks one of three **placement scopes** by walking up from your
    17	CWD; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global` when intent isn't
    18	obvious:
    19	
    20	| Scope | Trigger | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
    21	|---|---|---|---|
    22	| **LOCAL** | `vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` / `skills/.claude-plugin/` found | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
    23	| **PROJECT** | `.git` found | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor/Codex/OpenCode/Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any non-universal agent dir already present at the repo root) |
    24	| **GLOBAL** | neither anchor, or `--global` | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any non-universal agent dir already present under `$HOME`) |
    25	
    26	This mirrors the placement contract of `npx skills add` (canonical content
    27	in `.agents/skills/` + relative symlinks into each non-universal agent's
    28	home), so a skill scaffolded here will be picked up by Claude Code,
    29	Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Warp, etc. without any extra wiring. See
    30	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](../reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
    31	for the upstream mechanism.
    32	
    33	Alternative (just the SKILL.md skeleton, no symlinks, no `references/` /
    34	`scripts/` / `assets/`):
    35	
    36	```bash
    37	cd skills/local
    38	npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
    39	```
    40	
    41	This creates only `skills/local/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` with the required
    42	YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`).
    43	
    44	Before writing the description, check the repo's
    45	[Agent skill compatibility](../reference/agent-skill-compatibility.md) policy.
    46	Local skills should target portable coding-agent limits: hyphen-case names
    47	under 64 chars, descriptions under 1024 chars, and 120-500 chars preferred.
    48	
    49	## Required structure
    50	
    51	See [Conventions](../conventions.md) for the full layout rules. In short:
    52	
    53	- `SKILL.md` — required, lean (under ~500 lines).
    54	- `assets/` — templates the skill copies into target projects.
    55	- `scripts/` — executable helpers (Bash 3.2 compatible).
    56	- `references/` — long-form material loaded on demand.
    57	
    58	## Author the SKILL.md following agentskills.io best practices
    59	
    60	The two highest-leverage rules from the
    61	[agentskills.io best practices](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices):
    62	
    63	1. **Procedures over declarations.** Tell the agent what to *do*, not what
    64	   to *be*. A SKILL.md that says "follow these three steps" is much more
    65	   reliable than one that says "be a careful and methodical helper".
    66	2. **Defaults over menus.** Pick one workflow as the default; offer
    67	   alternatives via flags or in `references/`. Letting the agent choose
    68	   between three equivalent options at every step is a debugging nightmare.
    69	
    70	A third rule we apply in this repo:
    71	
    72	- **Bundle the workflow as a script if you can.** If the skill keeps asking
    73	  the agent to perform the same multi-step procedure, write it as a shell
    74	  script in `scripts/` and make the SKILL.md call the script. The
    75	  [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
    76	  skill is the reference for this pattern.
    77	
    78	## Add a docs page
    79	
    80	Every local skill should also have a page under `docs/skills/<skill>.md`
    81	that explains, for a human reader, what the skill is for, when it
    82	triggers, and what it costs to use. The `SKILL.md` is the agent-facing
    83	contract; the docs page is the human-facing pitch. Both are valuable.
    84	
    85	When you create the docs page, also link it from
    86	[`docs/skills/index.md`](../skills/index.md) and from `mkdocs.yml`'s `nav:`
    87	block at the repo root.
    88	
    89	## Test by installing into a scratch project
    90	
    91	```bash
    92	mkdir /tmp/scratch && cd /tmp/scratch
    93	git init
    94	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
    95	```
    96	
    97	This pulls the new skill into `.agents/skills/` of a clean project so you
    98	can verify the SKILL.md activates as you expect.
---

+## forge-native-dev in a submodule superproject
+
+If the repo is a superproject (`.gitmodules` present), use the two skills at
+different levels:
+
+- **forge-native-dev** handles issues and PRs in each child, in that child's
+  own forge. Superproject issue worktrees (`.worktrees/issue-<n>`) are only for
+  changes to outer content.
+- **superproject-workspace** handles pointer policy, child worktrees under
+  `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch>`, and the preflighted bump commit that
+  records merged child work in the superproject.
+
--- a/skills/local/git-workflow/references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md
+++ b/skills/local/git-workflow/references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md
+
+## Worktrees in a submodule superproject
+
+A worktree of a **superproject** starts with every submodule uninitialized, so
+it is the wrong tool for work inside a child repo. Create a worktree of the
+**child** instead, under `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch>`. The
+`superproject-workspace` skill's
+`superproject.py worktree add <child> <branch>` does this, including the
+`.gitignore` entry and branching pins from their recorded gitlink. See its
+`references/worktrees.md`.

```text
dev () {
	case "${1:-}" in
		(__complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|retire|prepare|artifact|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|shell-init|cache|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap|activity) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev "$@" || return $?
			return 0 ;;
	esac
	local __dev_cd_file __dev_action_file __dev_dir __dev_status
	local __dev_action __dev_task __dev_delete __dev_unknown
	if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" 
	then
		__dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"  || {
			printf 'dev: cannot create the shell directory side channel\n' >&2
			return 1
		}
	fi
	if ! __dev_action_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-action.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" 
	then
		__dev_action_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-action.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"  || {
			rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
			printf 'dev: cannot create the shell action side channel\n' >&2
			return 1
		}
	fi
	__dev_status=0 
	DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 DEV_SHELL_ACTION_FD=4 command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev "$@" 3> "$__dev_cd_file" 4> "$__dev_action_file" || __dev_status=$? 
	if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]
	then
		if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
		then
			if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]
			then
				builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$? 
			fi
		else
			__dev_status=1 
		fi
	fi
	if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_action_file" ]
	then
		exec 4< "$__dev_action_file"
		if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_action <&4 && IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_task <&4 && IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_delete <&4 && IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_unknown <&4 && {
				[ "$__dev_action" = retire ] || [ "$__dev_action" = retire-recursive ]
			}
		then
			if [ "$__dev_action" = retire-recursive ]
			then
				case "$__dev_delete:$__dev_unknown" in
					(false:false) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --recursive -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(true:false) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --recursive --delete-branch -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(false:true) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --recursive --close-unknown -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(true:true) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --recursive --delete-branch --close-unknown -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(*) __dev_status=1  ;;
				esac
			else
				case "$__dev_delete:$__dev_unknown" in
					(false:false) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(true:false) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --delete-branch -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(false:true) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --close-unknown -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(true:true) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --delete-branch --close-unknown -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(*) __dev_status=1  ;;
				esac
			fi
		else
			__dev_status=1 
		fi
		exec 4<&-
	fi
	rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" "$__dev_action_file" || :
	return $__dev_status
}
dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.

It exists to keep four things separate that otherwise collapse into one:

  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
  herdr / tmux / zellij
                  a per-host live runtime
  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next

Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
human intent Git cannot answer — task state/owner/next action and asset identity,
tags, notes and experiment lifecycle — so closing a runtime session or moving a
Try never means losing the thread. Transient pane data is not persisted.

TL;DR: default managed-task loop

  dev work start --> HOT: work / commit / test
  HOT  -- dev work park --next "..." --> WARM
  WARM -- dev work resume           --> HOT

  direct:          dev work done      --> DONE
  branch/worktree: dev work done --ff  --> DONE
  branch/worktree: dev work done --pr  --> push / review handoff
                                          |
            feedback --> resume if parked --> work

  DONE --> dev work sweep (report) --> dev work sweep --apply (reap) --> next task
  Remote merge detection and cleanup are not automatic; verify integration first.

Usage:
  dev [flags]
  dev [command]

Available Commands:
  activity             Review development history and recorded activity
  agent                Manage agent skills, MCP, instructions, prompts and history
  dotfile              Inspect and manage local dotfiles through native chezmoi
  fleet                Inspect and safely synchronize dev repositories across machines
  git                  Manage Git worktrees, submodules, ignore rules and guarded transactions
  help                 Guides to repository workflows, policies, and tradeoffs
  pr                   Inspect, try and merge pull requests with explicit actions
  repo                 List, clone, create and sync repositories
  self                 Configure, diagnose and maintain dev itself
  snippet              Find and share GitHub Gists and GitLab snippets
  ssh                  Manage SSH hosts, fleet registrations, and Herdr machines
  status               Show the full context of the current directory
  summary              Generate an agent-ready snapshot of this machine's projects
  triage               Find forgotten local work and preview batches of safe actions
  tries                Manage experiment lifecycle and metadata

Manage the linked worktrees dev owns.

Who owns which worktree — the rule dev encodes, so nobody has to improvise:

  dev            anything you might come back to tomorrow: features, fixes,
                 experiments, cross-machine handoffs. Placed at
                 paths.worktree_path, outside the repo.
  Claude Code    harness-owned turn-scoped subagent isolation in
                 .claude/worktrees/ (keep that gitignored); not a history
                 relocation guarantee.
  herdr          dev does not call "herdr worktree create". It creates the
                 worktree with git and asks herdr to open it, so the path
                 policy holds on machines without herdr too.

A new worktree is a clean checkout: no node_modules, no .venv, none of the
gitignored env files the project needs. dev provisions it — see the config's
[worktree] section, or a repo's own .dev-cli/config.toml.

TL;DR: the checkout is disposable, the branch is not

  dev work start --> paths.worktree_path/<repo>/<branch>  (default mode)
                                  |
                                  +-- dev git worktree list       what exists, and how dirty
                                  +-- dev git worktree open       attach a runtime to one
                                  +-- dev git worktree provision  re-run installs after a pull
                                  |
  dev work done --ff --> MERGED --> dev work retire --> checkout gone, branch kept

  dev git worktree rm removes a checkout. It never removes a branch or its commits.

----
TL;DR: default managed-task loop

  dev work start --> HOT: work / commit / test
  HOT  -- dev work park --next "..." --> WARM
  WARM -- dev work resume           --> HOT

  direct:          dev work done      --> DONE
  branch/worktree: dev work done --ff  --> DONE
  branch/worktree: dev work done --pr  --> push / review handoff
                                          |
            feedback --> resume if parked --> work

  DONE --> dev work sweep (report) --> dev work sweep --apply (reap) --> next task
  Remote merge detection and cleanup are not automatic; verify integration first.

```text
Exit code 1
---
description: One repo that holds your skills, AGENTS.md and shared docs, and points at your other repos. You run your agent from it.
---

A repository that holds your [skills](./Skill.md), your [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md.md) and your shared docs, and points at your other repos. You run your [agent](./Agent.md) in the Home Repo, and it opens or clones the other repos as the task needs them.

When a project spans several repos, an agent started in one of them sees only that repo. Each repo ends up with its own copy of the skills and the agent setup, the copies drift apart, and [grilling](./Grilling.md) a feature that crosses repos happens without the whole overview. A Home Repo keeps one copy of the shared material, and [sessions](./Session.md) start there rather than inside a single repo.

| Lives in the Home Repo                                              | Stays in each repo                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Skills used across repos                                            | The repo's code                            |
| AGENTS.md, with a pointer to each repo                              | Its own AGENTS.md, build and test commands |
| Shared docs: coding standards, a glossary, system-wide decisions    | Docs about that repo alone                 |
| Tooling, such as a CLI that connects the agent to external services |                                            |

Each pointer is a [context pointer](./Context%20pointer.md): one line naming the repo, where it lives on disk, and where to clone it from if it's missing. About 20 repos works fine this way. At a few hundred, one pointer per repo is too many for the agent to choose between, so point at one file per area of the business and list that area's repos in it ([progressive disclosure](./Progressive%20disclosure.md)). At thousands of repos, the skills have enough consumers that a skills marketplace fits better.

A Home Repo replaces a monorepo when you can't have one: when you mix public and private repos, or when a team won't adopt a monorepo. For a team, the Home Repo is the thing you share. In a [software factory](./Software%20factory.md), the Home Repo goes in the [sandbox](./Sandbox.md) and clones the other repos as it needs them.

_Avoid:_ "agent repo" and "meta-repo", older names for the same thing.

_Usage:_

"I keep copying the same skills into every repo, and the copies have drifted."

"Move them into a Home Repo. One copy of the skills, AGENTS.md points at each repo, and you start your sessions there."

# Plan: `superproject-workspace` skill

## Context

In AI-assisted development an agent often needs one entry point with context and edit access across many repos. A real monorepo couples the repos too tightly. A **superproject of git submodules** keeps them decoupled, but it drifts over time:

- child PRs merge and the gitlink silently falls behind
- children sit detached or dirty
- a pointer can reference an unpushed commit
- worktrees get messy
- each superproject grows its own ad-hoc justfile

The user has two working examples, which follow two different patterns:

- **dotfiles-all** is an *umbrella*. All 5 children are owned by the user and track `main`. Strong points: the `gitlink-preflight` check that a commit is reachable from `origin/main`, the ff-only `submodule-pull-main`, and inside-out commits. Weak points: no scheduled bump, 5 hard-coded paths, and every recipe duplicated for sh and pwsh.
- **Tadronaut-Mono-Repo** is a *workspace hub*. Children are tiered core/personal/references. Lazy init happens through `scripts/init_submodules.py`, and gitlinks are reproducible pins ("latest ≠ reset to main"). Experiments run in external worktrees, and a `context/` knowledge graph lives at the root. Weak points: no rule for when a pin moves forward, and no report of how far behind each child is.

The user has more, older and less agentic superprojects. The goal is one skill that encodes best practice for both patterns, and that can audit and upgrade the existing repos.

## Decisions (agreed with the user)

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Scope | Cover both patterns with one **per-submodule policy**. An umbrella is the special case where every child is `track`. |
| Policy storage | Custom keys in `.gitmodules`, read and written with `git config -f .gitmodules` |
| Bump mode | Each submodule chooses: `pr` (scheduled CI opens a PR), `direct` (CI commits to main after preflight), or `manual` |
| Worktrees | Child feature branches go in `.worktrees/<sub>/<branch>`, created from the child's own gitdir and gitignored. They stay inside the agent's entry point. Never use superproject worktrees. |
| No-submodule alternative | Covered by the decision guide only: manifest + gitignored clones, or Claude/Codex Project add-dir |
| Tooling | One PEP 723 Python CLI run via `uv run`. It works cross-platform, which removes the duplicate sh/pwsh recipes. Thin justfile wrapper, `--json` and `--dry-run` on every subcommand. |
| Adoption | `audit` (read-only) plus `adopt` (writes policy keys, AGENTS.md block, recipes, optional CI) |
```
