````text
# Worktrees

Submodule workspaces initialize recursively at committed gitlinks by default.
Use `--submodules=none` to skip, or `start --submodule PATH` to select children
for task branches. `dev git submodule status/init/develop/recover` inspects, prepares
and restores child checkouts. Explicit `--recursive` cleanup verifies initialized
child clones' remote recovery before removing them and the outer linked worktree;
canonical repositories and the outer branch are retained.

A worktree is a second working directory for the same repository: its own
files, its own checked-out branch, sharing one history and one remote.

## What they are actually for

**Preventing two writers from editing the same files at once.** Not feature
management — that is what branches are for.

So the question is never "how many agents am I running?" It is:

> Could these two writers touch the same file?

- Different files, one goal → one checkout is fine. Several agents, several
  panes, one branch.
- Different *approaches* to the same problem → one worktree each, so they can
  be compared and the loser discarded.
- Anything where the file ranges are unknown → worktrees.

## Who owns which worktree

| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feature, fix, experiment, handoff | `dev` | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until external retirement |
| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | owned by that harness; no transcript-relocation guarantee |

Use `dev` for its configured placement, provisioning, and guarded cleanup.
Choose task registration separately, when recorded park/resume and retirement help.

Never put a long-lived worktree inside the repository. Every file watcher,
language server, indexer and `rg` run in the outer repo then sees a second copy
of the whole tree.

## Commands

```bash
dev work start --task auth --branch feat/auth --base main  # new managed work
dev git worktree create feat/auth --base main   # create/provision; no task record
dev git worktree list                           # every worktree of this repo
dev git worktree open feat/auth                 # open and activate an existing one
dev git worktree open feat/auth --no-focus      # make it visible without navigation
dev git worktree rm feat/auth                   # remove the checkout; branch survives
dev git worktree provision                      # re-run setup on an existing checkout
```

When choosing a managed task, use `dev work start` with an explicit base. For an existing
external worktree that only needs runtime visibility, use
`dev git worktree open <branch> --repo <repo> --runtime herdr --no-focus`. It reports the
branch, actual path and backend/handle immediately, then the runtime surface
opened/reused, without switching focus or attaching. No task adoption,
provisioning, agent launch, or Git/index/dirty-file mutation occurs. Runtime
`none` reports no runtime and emits no shell `cd` handoff. Errors remain errors;
without the flag, normal activation and shell navigation are unchanged.

Report the repository, branch, actual path and runtime handle/result when handing
work back. Making an external checkout visible does not make it a managed task.

## Always pass a base

```bash
dev git worktree create fix/orderbook --base main
```

Without `--base`, dev uses the repository's default branch. Passing it
explicitly is still preferred for scripts and agent-driven creation because
the intended committed starting point stays reviewable in the command.

## Worktrees created directly in Herdr

Herdr's **New worktree** action is allowed. Git registers that checkout with
the canonical repository, so dev can display it as an external worktree as
long as the canonical repo is discoverable through `paths.scan_roots` or
`paths.repo_paths`—even
when the checkout lives under `~/.herdr/worktrees` and that directory is not a
scan root.

It remains deliberately unmanaged: dev does not silently create a task, move
the checkout, or run provisioning. If the work becomes durable, opt in:

```bash
dev git worktree provision /path/to/worktree  # optional: env files + dependencies
dev work adopt                           # report candidates; changes nothing
----
# Parallel agents

How to run several coding agents without them stepping on each other.

## The one rule

> **Worktree per change stream. Exact pane per agent.**

Not one worktree per agent. Isolation follows the *git mutation boundary*, not
who is typing.

```
one independent change stream
        → one worktree
        → one Herdr workspace
        → one exact launch pane
        → one or more coordinated agents
```

## Choose the operation

| Intent | Action |
|---|---|
| Observe existing work | `herdr agent get/read/wait`; do not send probe keys or focus it |
| Spawn independent work | `dev work start <repo> --task <name> --base <committed-ref> --json`, validate the exact new pane, then launch there |
| Handoff the same task | Settle the old session, checkpoint dirty code, get explicit user agreement, then resume with a new forked session ID |

A new independent task does not need to wait for an unrelated agent. It does
need a committed base: dirty state in another checkout is not inherited.

## Shared-checkout collision guard

Herdr-aware writer claims (`start --direct`, `start --branch-only`, and
`resume`) compare recognized agents by canonical Git worktree root and reject a
checkout occupied by another pane. `idle`, `done`, `blocked`, `working`, and
`unknown` are all occupied states. Herdr resolves the current pane before
excluding it, so an inherited ID made stale by a pane move is not trusted.

Pure `repo open`, `wt open`, and TUI Enter/focus navigate to the live owner and
do not authorize another writer. `--allow-shared-checkout` is an explicit
````

```text
mattpocock/skills:docs/engineering/implement-spec.md: `implement-spec` takes a [spec](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/spec) and its [tickets](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/ticket) and lands the whole thing in one run. The orchestrating [agent](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/agent) hands each ticket to an implementer [subagent](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/subagent) working in its own git worktree, merges each finished branch into a single **integration branch**, runs [code-review](https://aihero.dev/skills-code-review) over the result, and resolves the tickets.
mattpocock/skills:docs/engineering/implement-spec.md: - **A [harness](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/harness) that runs subagents in the background and gives each one a git worktree.** The skill exists to run tickets at the same time, so on a harness that runs subagents one at a time, it is only a slower `implement`.
mattpocock/skills:docs/engineering/implement.md: Not with `/implement`: one invocation, one ticket. For a whole spec in one run, use [implement-spec](https://aihero.dev/skills-implement-spec), which gives each ticket on the ready frontier to a [subagent](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/subagent) in its own worktree, then merges the results onto one integration branch. Running several `/implement` sessions side by side in one checkout is worse than unsupported. One field report describes a `git commit --amend` in one session landing on another session's commit, a stash vanishing from `refs/stash`, and commits landing on the wrong branch, all in a single afternoon across three issues. The sessions share one working directory, one index, and one HEAD. Users work around this with git worktrees, but `refs/stash` is shared across worktrees too, so worktrees alone do not fix the stash case.
mattpocock/skills:skills/engineering/implement-spec/SKILL.md: 4. Use a fresh **implementer subagent** for each ticket, each in its own worktree on its own branch. Each implementer subagent:
mattpocock/skills:skills/engineering/implement-spec/SKILL.md: - confirms its worktree is based on the integration branch before starting, and resets onto it if not;
mattpocock/skills:CHANGELOG.md: `implement-spec` (user-invoked) implements a whole spec in one run. It reads the tickets as a **task graph**, runs implementer subagents in their own worktrees across the ready **frontier**, and lands everything on one **integration branch**, closing out with `code-review`. Ahead of graduating:
mattpocock/skills:CHANGELOG.md: - Each implementer confirms its worktree is based on the integration branch, builds its ticket with `tdd`, and merges the integration tip into its own branch before reporting done, so each merge is a fast-forward.
mattpocock/skills:docs/engineering/resolving-merge-conflicts.md: One caveat from a user report on parallel worktrees: when sibling [sessions](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/session) each build a ticket in their own tree, the merge back is best done by the session that wrote the change, because it is the one that already knows the intent. If one agent resolves everybody's conflicts at the end, it loses the [context](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/context) that step 2 of this skill must then rebuild.
```

````text
以下是將 Git Submodules 架構與 `uv` Workspace、跨模組測試及型別檢查（Pyright / Mypy / Basedpyright）無縫整合的完整配置：

### 3. 最棘手的問題：外置 Worktree 如何共用環境與型別檢查？

這是在結合「外置 Worktree（`../.worktrees/<task-name>/`）」與「Python 虛擬環境」時最核心的工程細節。

當你在 `modules/core-engine` 建立了一個外置 Worktree 到 `../.worktrees/feat-x/core-engine` 時，根目錄 `.venv` 裡的 Editable 連結（`.pth` 檔）預設還是指向原本的 `modules/core-engine` 主目錄！如果在 Worktree 裡改了程式碼並直接跑測試，Python 會讀到舊目錄的程式碼。

有兩種極簡的解法可以寫進先前的 `sub-ops.sh` 與 `CLAUDE.md` 中：

#### 解法 A：使用 `PYTHONPATH` 動態覆寫（最快、完全隔離，推薦給 Agent）
不需要重新安裝 `.venv`，也不用擔心多個平行任務的 Worktree 互相搶占根目錄的 `.venv`。只要在 `sub-ops.sh` 或 Agent 測試指令中，將當前任務的 Worktree 路徑掛在 `PYTHONPATH` 最前面，Python 就會優先載入 Worktree 裡修改的程式碼，其餘未修改的套件則繼續回退使用根目錄的 `.venv`：

---
name: workspace-assembler
description: 將多個既有的獨立 Git 儲存庫組裝成單一 Context 容器（支援 Git Submodules 鎖定模式或 Home Repo 忽略模式），並提供跨儲存庫的 Worktree 建立、狀態巡檢與收尾清理。當使用者要求「組裝多個 repo」、「建立虛擬 Monorepo」、「跨 repo 開分支」或「清理跨專案 worktrees」時觸發。

# Workspace Assembler & Multi-Repo Lifecycle Skill

你負責協助使用者將分散的多個獨立 Git 儲存庫（Multi-repos）組裝到同一個父專案（Context Container）中，並管理日常的跨專案開發與收尾。

## 階段一：初始化與組裝既有 Repos (Setup / Assemble Mode)

當使用者希望把多個既有 Repo 組裝在一起時，請依序執行以下步驟：

1. **詢問與盤點（若使用者尚未提供完整資訊）**：
   * **目標儲存庫清單**：請使用者提供要組裝的 Git URLs，或是本地端已存在的 Repo 資料夾路徑。
   * **整合模式選擇**：
     * **模式 A（Git Submodules - 嚴格版本鎖定）**：適合需要確保各模組版本相容性（如策略引擎搭配特定版本資料管線）的專案。
     * **模式 B（Home Repo / Gitignore - 靈活無狀態）**：將子專案放進 `modules/` 並加入父專案的 `.gitignore`，適合純粹共享 Context 與統一操作、不想管父專案 Commit 指標的場景。

2. **執行組裝動作**：
   * 確保目前目錄已執行 `git init`，並建立 `modules/` 與 `scripts/` 目錄。
   * 將本技能附帶的 `scripts/sub-ops.sh` 複製到專案的 `./scripts/sub-ops.sh` 並設定 `chmod +x`。
   * **若為模式 A (Submodules)**：
     對每個 Repo 執行 `./scripts/sub-ops.sh add-submodule <git-url> <module-name> [default-branch]`（此腳本會自動設定 `branch = main` 與 `ignore = dirty`，避免日常髒狀態干擾）。
   * **若為模式 B (Home Repo)**：
     將 `modules/` 加入 `.gitignore`，並將各個 Repo clone 或移動至 `modules/<module-name>`。
   * 根據組裝結果，讀取 `templates/CLAUDE.template.md` 並在父專案根目錄生成專屬的 `CLAUDE.md`，填入實際的模組清單與角色描述。

---

## 階段二：日常跨專案開發與收尾 (Daily Operations Mode)

當專案已組裝完成，請一律透過 `./scripts/sub-ops.sh` 執行跨專案操作，**嚴禁在父專案根目錄直接執行 `git worktree add`**：

1. **全局狀態檢查**：
   執行 `./scripts/sub-ops.sh status`，向使用者回報哪些模組處於游離狀態（Detached HEAD）、有未提交修改或外置 Worktrees。
2. **啟動跨專案任務（隔離環境）**：
   當需要同時修改多個模組時，執行：
   `./scripts/sub-ops.sh start-task <task-name> <module-1> <module-2> ...`
   （這會在父專案外的 `../.worktrees/<task-name>/` 下為指定模組建立同名分支 `feat/<task-name>` 的獨立 Worktree）。
3. **由下而上提交（Bottom-Up Commit）**：
   先在各個模組（或其 Worktree）內完成測試、Commit 與 Push；確認遠端已有該 Commit 後，若為 Submodule 模式且使用者要求鎖定新版本，才更新父專案指標。
4. **任務收尾與清理**：
   當 PR 合併或任務結束，執行 `./scripts/sub-ops.sh cleanup <task-name>` 一鍵清除外置目錄並 prune 所有子模組。
```

---

## 2. Git Submodule 與 Worktree 鐵律 (Strict Git Rules)

### 規則 A：嚴禁在 Detached HEAD 下直接 Commit
進入任何 `modules/<repo>` 修改程式碼前，必須先檢查分支狀態：
1. 執行 `git -C modules/<repo> status`。
2. 若處於 `HEAD detached`，**必須**先切換至目標分支（如 `git checkout main && git pull`）或建立新功能分支（`git checkout -b feat/<name>`），才允許寫入修改。

### 規則 B：Worktree 外置原則（平行開發或多處修改時）
* **絕對禁止**在父專案根目錄執行 `git worktree add`（Git 對巢狀 Submodule Worktree 支援不穩定）。
* 當任務需要隔離環境、或子模組主目錄已有未提交變更時，請進入**目標子模組**，將 Worktree 建立於外置暫存區：
  ```bash
  # 格式：../.worktrees/<task-name>/<submodule-name>
  git -C modules/<repo> worktree add ../../../.worktrees/<task-name>/<repo> -b feat/<task-name>
  ```
* 所有程式碼修改、測試與推送，皆在該外置 Worktree 目錄內完成。

### 規則 C：由下而上提交協議 (Bottom-Up Commit Protocol)
禁止在父專案根目錄盲目執行 `git commit -a`。提交變更時必須嚴格遵守以下順序：
1. **Step 1 (Submodules First)**：在各個有修改的 Submodule（或其外置 Worktree）內完成測試、`git commit` 與 `git push`（或建立 PR）。
2. **Step 2 (Verify Remote)**：確認子模組的 Commit 已存在於遠端儲存庫（避免父專案紀錄了本地獨有的孤兒 Commit Hash）。
3. **Step 3 (Update Superproject)**：只有在明確需要推進父專案版本鎖定時，才回到父專案根目錄，將子模組切至最新目標 Commit，執行 `git add modules/<repo>` 並提交父專案。

---

## 3. 標準巡檢與收尾指令 (Standard Commands)

請優先呼叫內建腳本管理跨專案狀態，不要手動逐一進入資料夾檢查：

* **全局狀態健檢**：`./scripts/sub-ops.sh status`
### 3. 建議的 `.gitmodules` 搭配設定

為了讓這套工作流最順暢，建議在父專案的 `.gitmodules` 中為每個子模組補上 `branch` 與 `ignore` 屬性：

```ini
[submodule "modules/core-engine"]
	path = modules/core-engine
	url = git@github.com:your-org/core-engine.git
	branch = main
	ignore = dirty
```

* **`branch = main`**：讓 `./scripts/sub-ops.sh checkout-default` 知道每個子模組該回到哪個主分支（有些可能是 `main`，有些可能是 `master` 或 `develop`）。
* **`ignore = dirty`**：當你在子模組裡測試或修改檔案時，父專案的 `git status` 會自動忽略這些未提交變更，不會干擾父專案的視線；但只要子模組的 **Commit Hash 改變**（亦即正式提交了新版本），父專案依然會偵測到並提示你是否要更新版本鎖定。

你可以根據目前的目錄結構（例如你的子模組是放在根目錄還是 `modules/` 下），微調 `CLAUDE.md` 第一段的路徑描述即可直接套用。需要針對你的特定開發語言或測試流程（例如跨 Submodule 的 `pytest` 或環境變數共享）做進一步調整嗎？

這種情況有沒有什麼best practice？（雖然複雜度極高 但有沒有可能work？）

_**Assistant (2026-11-13 08:45:33Z)**_

完全可行。用 Git Submodules 打造「父專案（Superproject）作為 Context 容器」的架構，最大的優勢是**版本鎖定（Version Pinning）**——這在需要嚴格確保「某版策略引擎必須搭配某版資料管線」的場景中，是純路徑指標（Home Repo）做不到的。

要讓 AI Agent 在 Submodule 架構下順暢運作、且不在多處編輯與 Worktree 收尾時崩潰，核心原則是：**「對 Git 保持嚴格邊界，對 Agent 隱藏底層複雜度」**。以下是實戰中最穩健的 4 個 Best Practices：

**1. 調整 `.gitmodules` 與全域 Git 配置，消除預設痛點**
Submodule 最煩人的是動不動就進入 `detached HEAD`（游離狀態），以及父專案 `git status` 永遠顯示一堆髒狀態。請先在父專案設定：
* **追蹤分支而非死鎖 Commit（開發期）**：在 `.gitmodules` 中為常改動的子模組加上 `branch = main`，搭配 `git submodule update --remote --merge`，讓子模組保持在分支上，避免 Agent 在游離狀態下直接 Commit 導致程式碼遺失。
````

```text
---
description: A mention in one document that points to another, so the agent can pull it into context only when the task calls for it.
---

A mention in one document that points to another, so the [agent](./Agent.md) can pull it into the [context window](./Context%20window.md) only when the task calls for it. The unit [progressive disclosure](./Progressive%20disclosure.md) is built from.

The reason to use a pointer (instead of inlining the content) is cost. A pointer is one line in the context window. The document behind it might be thousands of [tokens](./Token.md), but those tokens cost nothing until the agent actually follows the pointer. Inline a 2,000-token runbook in [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md.md) and every [session](./Session.md) pays for it; replace it with "deploy process: see `internal/deploy.md`" and only the sessions that deploy ever load it. The agent follows the pointer with a [tool call](./Tool%20call.md) when the task matches.

A pointer needs two parts to work: a stable path, and enough description for the agent to know when following it is worth it. A bare path is a pointer the agent has no reason to follow; "see `internal/deploy.md`" with no hint of what's inside gets skipped by a session that needed it. Write the line so it matches how tasks present: "release, deploy, or rollback — read `internal/deploy.md` first".

Pointers are everywhere once you look: lines in AGENTS.md, [skill](./Skill.md) descriptions (the harness loads the description; the skill body waits behind it), filenames in a directory listing, links between docs, the lines in a [Home Repo](./Home%20Repo.md)'s AGENTS.md that name each of your other repos.

A pointer can also tie a [secondary source](./Secondary%20source.md) back to the [primary source](./Primary%20source.md) it was derived from — the compaction summary that names the original transcript, the doc that names the source file it describes. This makes the secondary source's lossiness recoverable: when the summary turns out not to be enough, the agent follows the pointer and reads the original, instead of working from whatever the summary kept.

_Avoid:_ "reference" — too dry; doesn't convey that following it pulls more context in. "Portal" — too florid.

_Usage:_

"AGENTS.md is getting huge."

"Most of it should be context pointers, not content. Keep the always-on rules inline; turn the deploy runbook and the style guide into skills and leave a context pointer behind."
----
```

```text
description: 'Right-sized GitHub/GitLab workflow for durable backlog, collaboration, PR review, and issue-linked worktrees. # forge-native-dev

Use GitHub/GitLab as the canonical **shared backlog**, not a mandatory record
of every action an agent takes. Creating a ticket is cheap; maintaining,
reading, and receiving notifications from unnecessary tickets is not.

**Core thesis**: Right-size tracking before choosing a forge surface. Issues
hold durable work commitments; PRs are review gates. A small experiment can
finish in the conversation and diff without either an Issue or a Discussion.

Lightweight lifecycle: **work -> validate -> report**, with an optional local
note and the repository's normal commit/review policy.
Tracked lifecycle: **Issue -> branch/worktree -> work -> PR -> review -> merge
-> cleanup**. A Discussion is optional, not a prerequisite to either lifecycle.

Surfaces, separated by the question they answer:

| Surface | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `references/issue-driven-workflow.md` | "Why issues over local TODO.md?" |
| `references/forge-abstraction.md` | "What `gh` command maps to what `glab` command?" |
| `references/agent-patterns.md` | "How do I wire agents to work from issues?" |
| `references/coexistence.md` | "I have git-workflow / PKH installed too — which wins?" |
| `references/github-features.md` | "How do I use Discussions, Projects, Wiki?" |
| `references/gitlab-features.md` | "How do I use Boards, Threads, CI/CD?" |
| `references/conventions.md` | "What commit/branch/merge conventions should I follow?" |
| `scripts/forge.sh` | The sourced library — all other scripts depend on it. |
| `scripts/forge-init.sh` | One-shot repo setup. |
| `scripts/forge-worktree.sh` | Issue-to-worktree-to-PR lifecycle. |
| `scripts/forge-cleanup.sh` | Auto-cleanup merged branches + worktrees. |
| `scripts/forge-status.sh` | Alignment dashboard. |
| `scripts/forge-issue.sh` | Standalone issue operations. |
| `scripts/forge-pr.sh` | Standalone PR/MR operations. |

## When to use this skill

- The user explicitly requests an Issue, Discussion, or shared backlog item.
- Actionable work will remain deferred or blocked, needs ownership/dependency
  tracking, or benefits from asynchronous coordination. Apply the scope gate below;
  "maybe later", "先記下來", or "research" alone does not select an external surface.
- The user asks "should I open a PR?", "幫我開 PR", or finishes work on
  a branch and needs to ship it.
- The user says "clean up branches", "清理 branch", "which branches are
  done?", or has stale worktrees.
- The user wants to see the state of their issues/branches/PRs at a glance.
- A new project needs to be set up for issue-driven development.
- The user asks about configuring agents to work from GitHub/GitLab issues.

## When NOT to use this skill

- The project has no GitHub/GitLab remote — use `git-workflow` instead.
- The user explicitly prefers `project-knowledge-harness` (local TODO.md).
- Bounded experiments, quick fixes, or same-session research with no remaining
  coordination need — work locally; an online remote does not change this.
- Git-only operations with no requested forge interaction.
```

```text
forge_detect() {
  git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || _forge_die "not inside a git repository" 2

  FORGE_REMOTE_URL="$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$FORGE_REMOTE_URL" ]; then
    _forge_warn "no 'origin' remote found"
    FORGE_TYPE="unknown"
    FORGE_CLI=""
    return 0
  fi

  case "$FORGE_REMOTE_URL" in
    *github.com*|*github.com:*)
      FORGE_TYPE="github"
      if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        FORGE_CLI="gh"
      else
        _forge_warn "GitHub remote detected but 'gh' CLI not found — install: brew install gh"
        FORGE_CLI=""
      fi
      ;;
    *gitlab.com*|*gitlab.com:*|*gitlab.*)
      FORGE_TYPE="gitlab"
      if command -v glab >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        FORGE_CLI="glab"
      else
        _forge_warn "GitLab remote detected but 'glab' CLI not found — install: brew install glab"
        FORGE_CLI=""
      fi
_forge_issue_from_branch() {
  local branch="$1"
  case "$branch" in
    issue/[0-9]*)
      printf '%s' "$branch" | sed 's#^issue/\([0-9]*\).*#\1#'
      ;;
    agent/issue/[0-9]*)
      printf '%s' "$branch" | sed 's#^agent/issue/\([0-9]*\).*#\1#'
      ;;
    *)
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pull Requests / Merge Requests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

forge_slugify() {
  printf '%s' "$1" \
    | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' \
    | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]/-/g; s/--*/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' \
    | cut -c1-50
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Utility: get current user login
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

forge_whoami() {
  _forge_require_cli
  case "$FORGE_TYPE" in
    github) gh api user -q '.login' 2>/dev/null || printf '@me' ;;
    gitlab) glab api user -q '.username' 2>/dev/null || printf '@me' ;;
  esac
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Utility: get the default branch name
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

forge_default_branch() {
  local branch
  branch="$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's#^origin/##' || true)"
  if [ -z "$branch" ]; then
    branch="$(git remote show origin 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*HEAD branch: //p' || true)"
  fi
  if [ -z "$branch" ]; then
    branch="main"
  fi
  printf '%s' "$branch"
}
```

````text
# Worktrees for parallel agents

Read this before setting up parallel Claude Code sessions/agents, or when
debugging a worktree that's missing a gitignored file (like `.env`) or won't
clean up. Based on the official
[Claude Code worktrees docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees) and
[`git worktree`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree).

## Table of contents

1. [Why worktrees](#why-worktrees)
2. [Starting a worktree](#starting-a-worktree)
3. [Choosing the base branch](#choosing-the-base-branch)
4. [Copying gitignored files (`.worktreeinclude`)](#copying-gitignored-files-worktreeinclude)
5. [Isolating subagents](#isolating-subagents)
6. [SpecStory separation bonus](#specstory-separation-bonus)
7. [Cleanup](#cleanup)
8. [Manual worktrees & non-git VCS](#manual-worktrees--non-git-vcs)

---

## Why worktrees

A git worktree is a separate working directory with its own files and branch,
sharing the same repo history and remote. Running each parallel agent/session
in its own worktree means edits in one never touch another — one terminal
builds a feature while a second fixes a bug, with zero file collisions.

## Starting a worktree

```bash
claude --worktree feature-auth   # or -w
# → creates .claude/worktrees/worktree-feature-auth/ on branch worktree-feature-auth
claude --worktree                # omit the name → generates e.g. bright-running-fox
```

You can also ask Claude to "work in a worktree" mid-session (it uses the
`EnterWorktree` tool). **Add `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore`** so worktree
contents don't appear as untracked files in your main checkout.

# .worktreeinclude — copy gitignored files into new git worktrees.
#
# Uses .gitignore syntax. Only files that are BOTH matched by a pattern here
# AND gitignored get copied into a fresh worktree. Tracked files (e.g. a
# committed .vscode/settings.json) are already present in the checkout, so
# listing them here does NOTHING — put only genuinely-ignored files below.
#
# Not processed when a custom WorktreeCreate hook replaces git (non-git VCS);
# copy local files inside that hook script instead.
#
# Place this file at the repository root and commit it.

.env
.env.local
.env.*.local
config/secrets.json
````

````text
A lot of folks ask me "how do you work with agents in multiple repos at once?"

I have a very simple solution - the Home Repo

I have a single repo (the home) where all of my skills, steering files, wiki etc live.

I run my agent in the home repo, and then inside AGENTS.md I have pointers to the other repos:

```
For skills, clone mattpocock/skills to ~/repos/skills.
For Sandcastle, clone mattpocock/sandcastle to ~/repos/sandcastle
```

This is extremely simple and incredibly effective. The home repo lets you:

1. Put all your steering files and tooling in one place
2. Have a single spot to run all your agents in
3. Make sweeping changes over multiple repos

Talked about this in the course yesterday and folks are loving it (see below).

I'm sure you will too. Enjoy!
````

````text
## Categories in the install UI

The grouped picker UI of `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`
is driven by [`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`](skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json).
Each plugin entry defines one category and explicitly lists its member skills;
anything not listed there falls under **Other** automatically. The manifest is
the source of truth for the current category set rather than a duplicated list
in this README.

```bash
# Validate the manifest (paths exist, no duplicates, name not reserved,
# on-disk skills covered).
make marketplace

# Exercise Claude Code + Codex native add/list/install in isolated state.
make native-marketplace-smoke
```

The manifest lives under `skills/`, **not** at the repo root, because the
install command's `/skills` subpath makes the CLI read
`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. See
[npx skills metadata model](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/reference/npx-skills-metadata/)
for the full mechanism, the `kebabToTitle` group naming rule, reserved
marketplace names, and the `marketplace.json` vs `plugin.json` distinction.
````

````text
## Workspaces

For a monorepo of related packages, one lockfile and one venv for all of them:

```toml
[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["packages/*"]

[tool.uv.sources]
my-core = { workspace = true }
```

Members share the resolution, so a version conflict between two members is a
hard error rather than two silently different environments. If the packages
genuinely need different dependency versions, they are not a workspace.

On exiting a worktree session:

- **No changes/commits**: worktree + branch removed automatically (named
  sessions prompt so you can keep them).
- **Uncommitted changes / untracked / new commits**: Claude prompts to keep or
  remove.
- **Non-interactive `-p` runs**: not cleaned up automatically — remove with
  `git worktree remove` (add `--force` if it has uncommitted work).

Subagent/background worktrees are swept once older than `cleanupPeriodDays`,
provided they have no uncommitted changes/untracked files/unpushed commits.

## Manual worktrees & non-git VCS

Full manual control:

```bash
git worktree add ../proj-feature-a -b feature-a   # new branch
git worktree add ../proj-bugfix bugfix-123        # existing branch
git worktree list
git worktree remove ../proj-feature-a
```

Remember to reinitialize the dev environment in each new worktree (install
deps, create venvs). For **non-git VCS** (SVN/Perforce/hg), configure
`WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks — note that `.worktreeinclude` is **not
processed** when a custom hook replaces the default git logic, so copy local
config files inside the hook script instead.

## Worktrees in a submodule superproject

A worktree of a **superproject** starts with every submodule uninitialized, so
it is the wrong tool for work inside a child repo. Create a worktree of the
**child** instead, under `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch>`. The
`superproject-workspace` skill's
`superproject.py worktree add <child> <branch>` does this, including the
`.gitignore` entry and branching pins from their recorded gitlink. See its
`references/worktrees.md`.
````

    10	
    11	Use the dry-run to verify the exact parent checkout, portable network source,
    12	relative path and mode. Only apply the approved request. `--parent PATH` selects
    13	an exact checkout; the default is the nearest repo containing cwd, not its
    14	canonical or outermost checkout. Source selection combines known local remotes
    15	and cached forge repositories without refreshing. Ambiguous names need an exact
    16	URL or interactive selection. Local-only sources and existing targets/stores are
    17	not adopted. REPOS/REMOTE `y u` copies the selected network clone URL locally.
    18	
    19	The wizard offers pinned/default-branch. Non-interactive default is pinned;
    20	`--ref` is pinned-only, and a missing ref resolves the fresh clone's default
    21	branch commit. Default-branch mode tracks the real default, not an assumed main.
    22	Both stage a fixed gitlink; neither enables remote-following updates or creates
    23	task-member intent. `--submodules=recursive|none` controls only new descendants.
    24	Only `.gitmodules` and the new gitlink are staged; unrelated staged/dirty work
    25	and other checkouts are preserved. No commit, push, task branch or runtime is
    26	created. Use `develop` separately for managed task membership.
    27	
    28	**Gotchas:** `.gitmodules` must be absent or unchanged, including hidden index
    29	edits; filters/encodings, conflicts, active Git operations, detached/unborn
    30	parents and unsafe paths block addition. `--yes` is required for non-interactive
    31	mutation; `--json` never prompts. A local `planned` result has no resolved HEAD.
    32	An error may still return a partial result (`phase`, `git_dir`, `head`, `staged`,
    33	`warnings`). Inspect retained paths and finish metadata/staging manually; for
    34	`initialization-incomplete`, run `dev git submodule init` inside the new child.
    35	Never force-delete partial clones or replay add over them. The retirement
    36	`recover` journal format does not apply to addition.
    37	
    38	## Initialize and develop existing gitlinks
    39	
    40	`dev repo clone`, clone-style `repo new`, and new linked worktrees initialize
    41	recursively at committed gitlinks by default. Use `--submodules=none` to opt out;
    42	`--no-provision` only skips environment provisioning. Global and project
    43	`[submodules] init = "recursive"|"none"` control the default.
    44	
    45	Detached HEAD at a gitlink is intentional. Select development members with
    46	repeatable `dev work start --submodule PATH`; they get the task branch at the same
    47	commit. `--submodule-base PATH=REF` records their integration target. Project
    48	`submodules.develop` supplies optional default paths. Direct/branch-only modes
    49	do not switch child branches. Later use `dev git submodule develop PATH...` from
    50	the managed worktree. Never infer permission to reset an existing child branch.
    51	
    52	`dev git submodule init` fills missing checkouts, preserves existing ones and refuses
    53	nonempty uninitialized directories. Initialization failure is not ready: retain
    54	partial results, retry init, and do not launch an agent. `status --json` reports

    57

    64	
    65	`park --cold --recursive`, `retire --recursive`, `wt rm --recursive` and
    66	`sweep --recursive` retain full recovery requirements for initialized child
    67	clones. Cold permits unmerged published work; Retire additionally verifies

    80	local/ignored files, unexpected `.git`, symlinks/reparse points, external ownership
# Worktree ownership

For ordinary clone/worktree acquisition, submodule initialization is core Git acquisition, before provisioning/runtime, and defaults to recursive pinned checkouts. `--no-provision` does not skip it; `--submodules=none` does. Gitlink children are independent submodule clones, not nested managed linked worktrees. Read `submodules.md` for selection and explicit disposal rules.

Read this before creating a worktree, sharing a checkout between agents, or when
a new checkout lacks dependencies, env files, or launcher backend state.

## The rule

| Change boundary | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|
| Durable feature/fix/experiment/handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until external `dev work retire` |
| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | managed by that harness; do not assume artifact relocation |
| Runtime workspace/panes | Herdr | per-host runtime | until explicitly closed |
| Rendered agent history | SpecStory | process launch checkout | until committed/removed with that checkout |

Use a `dev` worktree for independent approaches or any change stream whose code,
history, or plan must remain reviewable. Agents with explicitly disjoint file
ownership may share one checkout, but `--allow-shared-checkout` is a deliberate
coordination override—not a default.

`EnterWorktree` changes an agent's working location; it does not prove an
existing SpecStory wrapper/watcher rebound its source/output paths. Start the
new process from the target worktree root.

## Create managed work or surface an existing checkout

Task tracking is optional. `dev git worktree create <branch> --base <ref>`
creates/provisions/opens a checkout without a task record. Existing Git work
survives closing its runtime without adoption. Use `dev work start` only when
the recorded start/park/resume lifecycle is wanted.

For task-free merged cleanup, run from the canonical checkout and outside the
target runtime: `dev work sweep --merged-worktrees --base main --delete-branches`
reports the exact contained candidates; after review, add `--apply` to confirm
each removal. An open PR, agent `done`, or td issue closure is not containment.
Dirty products and unsettled artifacts remain blockers. A transcript path is
not a discard allowlist; inspect its exact final changes after the writer exits.
Squash integration may require a separate manual decision.

Prefer `dev work start <repo> --task '<task>' --base '<committed-ref>'` for new
managed work: it creates/selects the checkout, provisions it, opens the runtime,
and records task intent. For an already registered external worktree that only
needs runtime visibility:

```bash
dev git worktree open <branch> --repo <repo> --runtime herdr --no-focus
```

This opens or reuses the exact checkout without switching/attaching, launching an

## 1. Claude Code: Projects, multiple directories, worktrees

### What a "Claude project" is (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects)
- It is a cloud and web feature, not a CLI one. "A project is one ongoing conversation where Claude coordinates a stream of related work." Claude starts a thread for each task, usually as a cloud session. You can ask for a thread to run on your own machine through Remote Control.
- **Availability:** public beta on Pro, Max and Ultra only, not Team or Enterprise. It runs at claude.ai/code, in the desktop app and in the mobile app. The docs say it is "not in the terminal CLI, the VS Code extension, or the JetBrains plugin", and not on Bedrock, Google's platform or Foundry.
- **Configuration:** done in the UI under Project settings, "not in `settings.json`". Settings cover name and goal, coordinator and thread model/effort, project instructions, repositories, cloud environment, plugins and memory.
- **Multiple repos:** you add GitHub repos (github.com only, with the Claude GitHub App installed). Every cloud thread clones all of them.
  - The docs advise: "add the one or two repositories nearly every task touches and name the others in project instructions." A thread can add another repo to itself partway through a task.
  - Claude can only add repos from a GitHub owner the project already uses.
- **What is shared across threads:**
  - Project instructions, up to 16,000 characters.
  - Project memory: a `MEMORY.md` index plus files. This is separate from local auto memory.
  - Repositories and uploaded files, which appear under `/mnt/project-files`.
  - The cloud environment.
  - Plugins set in Project settings.
  - The connectors on your claude.ai account.
- **What cloud threads load from each repo:**
  - Loaded: root `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/`.
  - Not loaded: subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` files, path-specific rules, `.claude/skills/`, agents and commands, `.mcp.json`, and the plugins, permissions, hooks and env in `.claude/settings.json`.
  - Skills must be enabled on your claude.ai account instead.
  - A thread run on your own machine uses that machine's setup and gets the project instructions, but "not with its memory files loaded".
- **Limits:**
  - 500 new threads per day.
  - Uploads: 1,000 files or 2 GB at a time, 480 MB per file, at most 10 folders.
  - A project belongs to one user and can't be shared.
  - A sandbox that can't be resumed restarts from a fresh clone, so uncommitted work can be lost.
- **For your design [inference]:** Projects are a hosted alternative to a home repo, not a way to configure one. They don't read a repo's skills, so a home repo's `.claude/skills` would not reach cloud threads.

### CLAUDE.md discovery (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)
- **Ancestors:** CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files in directories above the working directory load at launch.
- **Subdirectories:** they load on demand, "once Claude reads, writes, or edits another file in that subdirectory".
- **`--add-dir`:** "By default, CLAUDE.md files from these directories are not loaded." Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1` loads the added directory's `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.claude/rules/*.md` (except rules with `paths`).
  - An added directory's **`AGENTS.md` does not load** even with that variable set.
- **AGENTS.md:** read only when there is no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or above it (needs v2.1.277 or later).
  - A subdirectory's AGENTS.md loads when Claude reads a file there, if that subdirectory has no CLAUDE.md of its own.
  - You can switch to `claude-md-and-agents-md` to load both.
- **`@imports`:** relative to the importing file, at most four hops deep. Imports pointing outside the working directory trigger a one-time approval dialog.
- **Auto memory:** "Per repository, shared across worktrees". The first 200 lines or 25KB load.
- **`claudeMdExcludes`:** skips ancestor CLAUDE.md files by glob pattern.

### Skills discovery (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)
- **Parents:** project skills load from `.claude/skills/` in the start directory and every parent directory up to the repo root.
- **Nested:** `<subdir>/.claude/skills/` loads "the first time Claude reads or edits a file in that subdirectory". `/add-dir <subdir>` loads it sooner (v2.1.257 or later).
  - If names clash, the nested skill is invoked as `/apps/web:deploy`.
- **`--add-dir` / `/add-dir` / SDK `additionalDirectories`:** loads `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/commands/` and `.claude/agents/`. Clashing names get a prefix such as `/cli:verify` (v2.1.309 or later).
  - Only `skills/` is watched for changes; restart after editing an added directory's commands or agents.
- **Settings `permissions.additionalDirectories`:** "grants file access only and loads none of these."
- **Worktrees:** the parent search stops at the worktree root. If the worktree has no `.claude/skills`, the main checkout's skills load instead (v2.1.277 or later).

### Worktrees (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows)
- **Creating one:**
  - `claude --worktree <name>` (or `-w`) creates `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` at the repo root on branch `worktree-<name>`. Without a name you get a generated one.
  - The docs recommend adding `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore`.
  - The base is `worktree.baseRef`: `"fresh"` (the remote default branch, the default) or `"head"`. You can't set it to a branch name.
  - `--worktree "#1234"` or a PR/MR URL starts from that pull request.
  - Interactive runs need workspace trust; `-p` skips the trust check.
- **EnterWorktree:** Claude creates or switches worktrees mid-session. Entering a path outside `.claude/worktrees/` always asks for approval, and only `bypassPermissions` skips that.
  - `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in hooks stays at the original root, while the hook's `cwd` field follows the worktree.
  - The EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree tools are removed when `permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories` is on.
- **Isolation:** Claude Code blocks edits, command working directories and git redirects (`-C`, `GIT_DIR` and similar) aimed at the main checkout.
- **Subagents with `isolation: worktree`:**
  - Each gets a temporary worktree, removed automatically when the subagent made no changes. Worktrees with changes wait for the periodic sweep.
  - It uses the same base branch as `--worktree`.
  - The subagent takes its instruction files from the main conversation, not from its worktree, and doesn't load the worktree root's CLAUDE.md or rules.
- **Cleanup when you exit an interactive session:**
  - Claude checks for changed or untracked files, "uncommitted work inside checked-out submodules", and new commits.
  - A clean, unnamed worktree is removed together with its branch. A named session prompts first.
  - Worktrees with work in them prompt you. If Claude can't inspect the submodule checkouts, it prompts rather than removing.
  - `-p` runs are never cleaned up and stay locked; remove them with `git worktree unlock` then `git worktree remove`.
- **Periodic sweep (`cleanupPeriodDays`):** applies to subagent and backgrounded-session worktrees. It keeps a worktree if:
  - it holds work;
  - "a checked-out submodule in the worktree holds changed or untracked files, or Claude Code can't inspect the worktree's submodules" (v2.1.274 or later);
  - it was created by hand with `git worktree add`;
  - it has no Claude marker in its git metadata.
  - Running agents hold a `git worktree lock`.
- **Shared with the main checkout:** the `.git` directory, project-scope plugins, "don't ask again" approvals (saved to the main checkout's `settings.local.json`), and untracked skills, agents and commands (the read-through described above).
- **`.worktreeinclude`:** copies gitignored files that match its patterns into new worktrees.
- **`WorktreeCreate` / `WorktreeRemove` hooks:** replace the git logic entirely, including where worktrees are placed.
- **Submodules:** the only documented behavior is the submodule-dirtiness checks in cleanup and the sweep. Nothing documents whether submodules get initialized in a new worktree.
  - **[inference]** The page lists everything that is copied (`.worktreeinclude`) and is silent on submodules, so expect submodules to be uninitialized in new worktrees. A setup step or a WorktreeCreate hook would need to run `git submodule update --init`.

## 2. Matt Pocock's Home Repo Pattern

- **Video:** the title is "The Home Repo Pattern: Run agents across ALL your repos" (YouTube oEmbed). I could not get the description or transcript.
- **Tweet (Nov 10, 2026), full text via https://api.fxtwitter.com/mattpocockuk/status/2120260969750540327:**
  - He keeps one repo "where all of my skills, steering files, wiki etc live", runs his agent there, and "inside AGENTS.md I have pointers to the other repos":
    ```
    For skills, clone mattpocock/skills to ~/repos/skills.
    For Sandcastle, clone mattpocock/sandcastle to ~/repos/sandcastle
    ```
  - Listed benefits: steering files and tooling in one place, a single spot to run agents, and sweeping changes across repos.
- **Most detailed primary source:** his dictionary entry at https://github.com/mattpocock/dictionary-of-ai-coding/blob/main/dictionary/Home%20Repo.md, added 2026-11-12.
  - **What lives in the home repo:** cross-repo skills, AGENTS.md with a pointer to each repo, shared docs (standards, glossary, system-wide decisions) and tooling such as a CLI.
  - **What stays in each repo:** its code, its own AGENTS.md with build and test commands, and docs about that repo alone.
  - **Pointers:** each is "one line naming the repo, where it lives on disk, and where to clone it from if it's missing". The agent "opens or clones the other repos as the task needs them". This is clone-if-missing, done by the agent following the instruction.
  - **Scale and progressive disclosure:** "About 20 repos works fine". At a few hundred, "point at one file per area of the business and list that area's repos in it". At thousands, use a skills marketplace.
  - **When it fits:** it replaces a monorepo when you can't have one, for example with mixed public and private repos or a team that won't adopt a monorepo. It also goes into a sandbox for a "software factory".
  - **Avoid** the older names "agent repo" and "meta-repo".
  - A related entry on context pointers says each pointer needs "a stable path, and enough description for the agent to know when following it is worth it".
- **Not in any source I could read:** submodules, gitignored clones, worktrees in the home-repo context, or an auto-clone script. His pointers use absolute paths outside the home repo (`~/repos/...`). **[inference]** That means sibling clones, not nested checkouts or submodules.
- **No published skill:** the mattpocock/skills file tree has no home-repo skill. Its only setup skills are `setup-matt-pocock-skills`, `setup-pre-commit` and `setup-ts-deep-modules`. Its worktree mentions are in `implement-spec`, where each subagent works in its own worktree. Its `implement` docs warn that `refs/stash` is shared across worktrees.

## 3. Git: submodules combined with worktrees

**From the official docs:**
- **git-worktree BUGS:** "Multiple checkout in general is still experimental, and the support for submodules is incomplete. It is NOT recommended to make multiple checkouts of a superproject." (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)
- **`remove`:** "Only clean worktrees ... can be removed. Unclean worktrees or ones with submodules can be removed with `--force`." A locked worktree needs `--force` twice.
- **`move`:** "linked worktrees containing submodules cannot be moved with this command."
- **`prune`:** cleans up `$GIT_DIR/worktrees` entries whose directories are gone. Use it "after manually removing a working tree ... (but use 'git worktree remove' next time)". Stale entries are also pruned automatically through `gc.worktreePruneExpire`.
- **Metadata and refs:** each worktree's metadata is in `$GIT_DIR/worktrees/<id>`, with a `.git` file pointing to it. "all refs starting with `refs/` are shared", except `refs/bisect`, `refs/worktree` and `refs/rewritten`. Config is shared unless `extensions.worktreeConfig` is on.
- **Where a submodule's git dir lives (gitsubmodules(7)):**
  - Usually "a Git directory located under the `$GIT_DIR/modules/` directory of its superproject" plus a `.git` file in the submodule.
  - "To completely remove a submodule, manually delete `$GIT_DIR/modules/<name>/`."
  - `absorbgitdirs` moves an embedded git dir there and sets `core.worktree`.

**Config keys** (gitmodules page at https://git-scm.com/docs/gitmodules; the rest from the local git 2.53 man pages, same text as git-scm):

| Key / command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `submodule.<name>.branch` | The remote branch tracked by `update --remote`. Defaults to remote `HEAD`. `.` means "same name as the current branch in the superproject". `.git/config` overrides `.gitmodules`. |
| `submodule.<name>.ignore` | `all`: never shown as modified (except when staged). `dirty`: ignores all work-tree changes, only the HEAD vs recorded commit counts. `untracked`: ignores only untracked files. `none`: the default, shows everything. Affects status and diff; `git submodule` commands are unaffected. |
| `submodule.<name>.update` | `checkout` (default, detached HEAD), `rebase`, `merge` or `none`. `!command` is allowed in `.git/config` only. Only `git submodule update` uses it, and `git submodule init` seeds it from `.gitmodules`. |
| `submodule.recurse` | Turns on `--recurse-submodules` by default for checkout, fetch, pull, push, reset, switch and similar. Default false. |
| `submodule.propagateBranches` | Experimental: makes branch operations recurse into submodules. |
| `status.submoduleSummary` | Shows a commit summary for modified submodules in status and commit. Suppressed where `ignore=all`. |
| `push.recurseSubmodules` | `check` aborts the push if changed submodule commits aren't on any submodule remote. `on-demand` pushes the changed submodules first and aborts if that fails. `only` pushes submodules but not the superproject. `no` is the default, unless `submodule.recurse` is set, in which case it means on-demand. |
| `git submodule update --remote --merge` | Fetches each submodule's remote and merges its tracking branch (from `submodule.<name>.branch`) into the submodule's current branch, without detaching HEAD. Plain `--merge` instead merges the superproject's recorded gitlink commit. |

**Running `git worktree add` from inside a submodule [inference]:** these are logical consequences of the docs above, not documented statements.
- **Metadata location:** the submodule's `$GIT_DIR` is `<super>/.git/modules/<name>`, so the worktree metadata lands in `<super>/.git/modules/<name>/worktrees/<id>`.
- **Branches:** they are ordinary `refs/heads` in `.git/modules/<name>`, shared across worktrees. They persist after the worktree is removed, and are lost only if that modules directory is deleted.
- **`remove` vs `rm -rf`:** `git worktree remove` cleans the metadata and refuses dirty trees. `rm -rf` leaves a stale entry, and the branch stays "checked out" there until `prune` or gc runs. That blocks re-checking out the same branch without `--force`.
- **Run prune from the submodule:** run `git worktree prune` from inside the submodule, not the superproject, because each repo has its own `worktrees/` directory.
- **Unknown:** the submodule's shared config sets `core.worktree`. The docs say that key "should never be shared", and that it applies only to the main worktree while `extensions.worktreeConfig` is off. I found no doc confirming that linked worktrees of a submodule behave correctly with it, so test it.

**For the skill design [inference]:** the BUGS note is a reason to prefer gitignored sibling or child clones, which is Pocock's approach, over making a submodule-bearing home repo the thing you open worktrees of.

## 1. Claude Code: Projects, multiple directories, worktrees

### What a "Claude project" is (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects)
- It is a cloud and web feature, not a CLI one. "A project is one ongoing conversation where Claude coordinates a stream of related work." Claude starts a thread for each task, usually as a cloud session. You can ask for a thread to run on your own machine through Remote Control.
- **Availability:** public beta on Pro, Max and Ultra only, not Team or Enterprise. It runs at claude.ai/code, in the desktop app and in the mobile app. The docs say it is "not in the terminal CLI, the VS Code extension, or the JetBrains plugin", and not on Bedrock, Google's platform or Foundry.
- **Configuration:** done in the UI under Project settings, "not in `settings.json`". Settings cover name and goal, coordinator and thread model/effort, project instructions, repositories, cloud environment, plugins and memory.
- **Multiple repos:** you add GitHub repos (github.com only, with the Claude GitHub App installed). Every cloud thread clones all of them.
  - The docs advise: "add the one or two repositories nearly every task touches and name the others in project instructions." A thread can add another repo to itself partway through a task.
  - Claude can only add repos from a GitHub owner the project already uses.
- **What is shared across threads:**
  - Project instructions, up to 16,000 characters.
  - Project memory: a `MEMORY.md` index plus files. This is separate from local auto memory.
  - Repositories and uploaded files, which appear under `/mnt/project-files`.
  - The cloud environment.
  - Plugins set in Project settings.
  - The connectors on your claude.ai account.
- **What cloud threads load from each repo:**
  - Loaded: root `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/`.
  - Not loaded: subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` files, path-specific rules, `.claude/skills/`, agents and commands, `.mcp.json`, and the plugins, permissions, hooks and env in `.claude/settings.json`.
  - Skills must be enabled on your claude.ai account instead.
  - A thread run on your own machine uses that machine's setup and gets the project instructions, but "not with its memory files loaded".
- **Limits:**
  - 500 new threads per day.
  - Uploads: 1,000 files or 2 GB at a time, 480 MB per file, at most 10 folders.
  - A project belongs to one user and can't be shared.
  - A sandbox that can't be resumed restarts from a fresh clone, so uncommitted work can be lost.
- **For your design [inference]:** Projects are a hosted alternative to a home repo, not a way to configure one. They don't read a repo's skills, so a home repo's `.claude/skills` would not reach cloud threads.

### CLAUDE.md discovery (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)
- **Ancestors:** CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files in directories above the working directory load at launch.
- **Subdirectories:** they load on demand, "once Claude reads, writes, or edits another file in that subdirectory".
- **`--add-dir`:** "By default, CLAUDE.md files from these directories are not loaded." Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1` loads the added directory's `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.claude/rules/*.md` (except rules with `paths`).
  - An added directory's **`AGENTS.md` does not load** even with that variable set.
- **AGENTS.md:** read only when there is no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or above it (needs v2.1.277 or later).
  - A subdirectory's AGENTS.md loads when Claude reads a file there, if that subdirectory has no CLAUDE.md of its own.
  - You can switch to `claude-md-and-agents-md` to load both.
- **`@imports`:** relative to the importing file, at most four hops deep. Imports pointing outside the working directory trigger a one-time approval dialog.
- **Auto memory:** "Per repository, shared across worktrees". The first 200 lines or 25KB load.
- **`claudeMdExcludes`:** skips ancestor CLAUDE.md files by glob pattern.

### Skills discovery (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)
- **Parents:** project skills load from `.claude/skills/` in the start directory and every parent directory up to the repo root.
- **Nested:** `&lt;subdir&gt;/.claude/skills/` loads "the first time Claude reads or edits a file in that subdirectory". `/add-dir &lt;subdir&gt;` loads it sooner (v2.1.257 or later).
  - If names clash, the nested skill is invoked as `/apps/web:deploy`.
- **`--add-dir` / `/add-dir` / SDK `additionalDirectories`:** loads `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/commands/` and `.claude/agents/`. Clashing names get a prefix such as `/cli:verify` (v2.1.309 or later).
  - Only `skills/` is watched for changes; restart after editing an added directory's commands or agents.
- **Settings `permissions.additionalDirectories`:** "grants file access only and loads none of these."
- **Worktrees:** the parent search stops at the worktree root. If the worktree has no `.claude/skills`, the main checkout's skills load instead (v2.1.277 or later).

### Worktrees (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows)
- **Creating one:**
  - `claude --worktree &lt;name&gt;` (or `-w`) creates `.claude/worktrees/&lt;name&gt;/` at the repo root on branch `worktree-&lt;name&gt;`. Without a name you get a generated one.
  - The docs recommend adding `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore`.
  - The base is `worktree.baseRef`: `"fresh"` (the remote default branch, the default) or `"head"`. You can't set it to a branch name.
  - `--worktree "#1234"` or a PR/MR URL starts from that pull request.
  - Interactive runs need workspace trust; `-p` skips the trust check.
- **EnterWorktree:** Claude creates or switches worktrees mid-session. Entering a path outside `.claude/worktrees/` always asks for approval, and only `bypassPermissions` skips that.
  - `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in hooks stays at the original root, while the hook's `cwd` field follows the worktree.
  - The EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree tools are removed when `permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories` is on.
- **Isolation:** Claude Code blocks edits, command working directories and git redirects (`-C`, `GIT_DIR` and similar) aimed at the main checkout.
- **Subagents with `isolation: worktree`:**
  - Each gets a temporary worktree, removed automatically when the subagent made no changes. Worktrees with changes wait for the periodic sweep.
  - It uses the same base branch as `--worktree`.
  - The subagent takes its instruction files from the main conversation, not from its worktree, and doesn't load the worktree root's CLAUDE.md or rules.
- **Cleanup when you exit an interactive session:**
  - Claude checks for changed or untracked files, "uncommitted work inside checked-out submodules", and new commits.
  - A clean, unnamed worktree is removed together with its branch. A named session prompts first.
  - Worktrees with work in them prompt you. If Claude can't inspect the submodule checkouts, it prompts rather than removing.
  - `-p` runs are never cleaned up and stay locked; remove them with `git worktree unlock` then `git worktree remove`.
- **Periodic sweep (`cleanupPeriodDays`):** applies to subagent and backgrounded-session worktrees. It keeps a worktree if:
  - it holds work;
  - "a checked-out submodule in the worktree holds changed or untracked files, or Claude Code can't inspect the worktree's submodules" (v2.1.274 or later);
  - it was created by hand with `git worktree add`;
  - it has no Claude marker in its git metadata.
  - Running agents hold a `git worktree lock`.
- **Shared with the main checkout:** the `.git` directory, project-scope plugins, "don't ask again" approvals (saved to the main checkout's `settings.local.json`), and untracked skills, agents and commands (the read-through described above).
- **`.worktreeinclude`:** copies gitignored files that match its patterns into new worktrees.
- **`WorktreeCreate` / `WorktreeRemove` hooks:** replace the git logic entirely, including where worktrees are placed.
- **Submodules:** the only documented behavior is the submodule-dirtiness checks in cleanup and the sweep. Nothing documents whether submodules get initialized in a new worktree.
  - **[inference]** The page lists everything that is copied (`.worktreeinclude`) and is silent on submodules, so expect submodules to be uninitialized in new worktrees. A setup step or a WorktreeCreate hook would need to run `git submodule update --init`.

## 2. Matt Pocock's Home Repo Pattern

- **Video:** the title is "The Home Repo Pattern: Run agents across ALL your repos" (YouTube oEmbed). I could not get the description or transcript.
- **Tweet (Nov 10, 2026), full text via https://api.fxtwitter.com/mattpocockuk/status/2120260969750540327:**
  - He keeps one repo "where all of my skills, steering files, wiki etc live", runs his agent there, and "inside AGENTS.md I have pointers to the other repos":
    ```
    For skills, clone mattpocock/skills to ~/repos/skills.
    For Sandcastle, clone mattpocock/sandcastle to ~/repos/sandcastle
    ```
  - Listed benefits: steering files and tooling in one place, a single spot to run agents, and sweeping changes across repos.
- **Most detailed primary source:** his dictionary entry at https://github.com/mattpocock/dictionary-of-ai-coding/blob/main/dictionary/Home%20Repo.md, added 2026-11-12.
  - **What lives in the home repo:** cross-repo skills, AGENTS.md with a pointer to each repo, shared docs (standards, glossary, system-wide decisions) and tooling such as a CLI.
  - **What stays in each repo:** its code, its own AGENTS.md with build and test commands, and docs about that repo alone.
  - **Pointers:** each is "one line naming the repo, where it lives on disk, and where to clone it from if it's missing". The agent "opens or clones the other repos as the task needs them". This is clone-if-missing, done by the agent following the instruction.
  - **Scale and progressive disclosure:** "About 20 repos works fine". At a few hundred, "point at one file per area of the business and list that area's repos in it". At thousands, use a skills marketplace.
  - **When it fits:** it replaces a monorepo when you can't have one, for example with mixed public and private repos or a team that won't adopt a monorepo. It also goes into a sandbox for a "software factory".
  - **Avoid** the older names "agent repo" and "meta-repo".
  - A related entry on context pointers says each pointer needs "a stable path, and enough description for the agent to know when following it is worth it".
- **Not in any source I could read:** submodules, gitignored clones, worktrees in the home-repo context, or an auto-clone script. His pointers use absolute paths outside the home repo (`~/repos/...`). **[inference]** That means sibling clones, not nested checkouts or submodules.
- **No published skill:** the mattpocock/skills file tree has no home-repo skill. Its only setup skills are `setup-matt-pocock-skills`, `setup-pre-commit` and `setup-ts-deep-modules`. Its worktree mentions are in `implement-spec`, where each subagent works in its own worktree. Its `implement` docs warn that `refs/stash` is shared across worktrees.

## 3. Git: submodules combined with worktrees

**From the official docs:**
- **git-worktree BUGS:** "Multiple checkout in general is still experimental, and the support for submodules is incomplete. It is NOT recommended to make multiple checkouts of a superproject." (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)
- **`remove`:** "Only clean worktrees ... can be removed. Unclean worktrees or ones with submodules can be removed with `--force`." A locked worktree needs `--force` twice.
- **`move`:** "linked worktrees containing submodules cannot be moved with this command."
- **`prune`:** cleans up `$GIT_DIR/worktrees` entries whose directories are gone. Use it "after manually removing a working tree ... (but use 'git worktree remove' next time)". Stale entries are also pruned automatically through `gc.worktreePruneExpire`.
- **Metadata and refs:** each worktree's metadata is in `$GIT_DIR/worktrees/&lt;id&gt;`, with a `.git` file pointing to it. "all refs starting with `refs/` are shared", except `refs/bisect`, `refs/worktree` and `refs/rewritten`. Config is shared unless `extensions.worktreeConfig` is on.
- **Where a submodule's git dir lives (gitsubmodules(7)):**
  - Usually "a Git directory located under the `$GIT_DIR/modules/` directory of its superproject" plus a `.git` file in the submodule.
  - "To completely remove a submodule, manually delete `$GIT_DIR/modules/&lt;name&gt;/`."
  - `absorbgitdirs` moves an embedded git dir there and sets `core.worktree`.

**Config keys** (gitmodules page at https://git-scm.com/docs/gitmodules; the rest from the local git 2.53 man pages, same text as git-scm):

| Key / command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `submodule.&lt;name&gt;.branch` | The remote branch tracked by `update --remote`. Defaults to remote `HEAD`. `.` means "same name as the current branch in the superproject". `.git/config` overrides `.gitmodules`. |
| `submodule.&lt;name&gt;.ignore` | `all`: never shown as modified (except when staged). `dirty`: ignores all work-tree changes, only the HEAD vs recorded commit counts. `untracked`: ignores only untracked files. `none`: the default, shows everything. Affects status and diff; `git submodule` commands are unaffected. |
| `submodule.&lt;name&gt;.update` | `checkout` (default, detached HEAD), `rebase`, `merge` or `none`. `!command` is allowed in `.git/config` only. Only `git submodule update` uses it, and `git submodule init` seeds it from `.gitmodules`. |
| `submodule.recurse` | Turns on `--recurse-submodules` by default for checkout, fetch, pull, push, reset, switch and similar. Default false. |
| `submodule.propagateBranches` | Experimental: makes branch operations recurse into submodules. |
| `status.submoduleSummary` | Shows a commit summary for modified submodules in status and commit. Suppressed where `ignore=all`. |
| `push.recurseSubmodules` | `check` aborts the push if changed submodule commits aren't on any submodule remote. `on-demand` pushes the changed submodules first and aborts if that fails. `only` pushes submodules but not the superproject. `no` is the default, unless `submodule.recurse` is set, in which case it means on-demand. |
| `git submodule update --remote --merge` | Fetches each submodule's remote and merges its tracking branch (from `submodule.&lt;name&gt;.branch`) into the submodule's current branch, without detaching HEAD. Plain `--merge` instead merges the superproject's recorded gitlink commit. |

**Running `git worktree add` from inside a submodule [inference]:** these are logical consequences of the docs above, not documented statements.
- **Metadata location:** the submodule's `$GIT_DIR` is `&lt;super&gt;/.git/modules/&lt;name&gt;`, so the worktree metadata lands in `&lt;super&gt;/.git/modules/&lt;name&gt;/worktrees/&lt;id&gt;`.
- **Branches:** they are ordinary `refs/heads` in `.git/modules/&lt;name&gt;`, shared across worktrees. They persist after the worktree is removed, and are lost only if that modules directory is deleted.
- **`remove` vs `rm -rf`:** `git worktree remove` cleans the metadata and refuses dirty trees. `rm -rf` leaves a stale entry, and the branch stays "checked out" there until `prune` or gc runs. That blocks re-checking out the same branch without `--force`.
- **Run prune from the submodule:** run `git worktree prune` from inside the submodule, not the superproject, because each repo has its own `worktrees/` directory.
- **Unknown:** the submodule's shared config sets `core.worktree`. The docs say that key "should never be shared", and that it applies only to the main worktree while `extensions.worktreeConfig` is off. I found no doc confirming that linked worktrees of a submodule behave correctly with it, so test it.

**For the skill design [inference]:** the BUGS note is a reason to prefer gitignored sibling or child clones, which is Pocock's approach, over making a submodule-bearing home repo the thing you open worktrees of.</result>

**Submodule state.** All 5 are on `main`, clean, with no extra worktrees. `.gitignore` excludes `.claude/worktrees/` ("Ephemeral EnterWorktree checkouts").

**Agent files.**

Key verbatim sections from `CLAUDE.md`:
> - **Commit from the inside out.** First commit and push every affected submodule to its own remote; only then commit the gitlink pointer bump in this superproject. `git submodule status` shows drift, and a superproject pointer to an unpushed commit dangles for every other clone.
> - **One cross-repo change gets one outer pointer commit.** … stage **all affected** gitlinks … and record them together in a single superproject commit. Do not make one outer commit per submodule or leave the second pointer as unrelated working-tree drift. … verify … with `git diff --cached --submodule=log -- …`
> - … Gitlinks record commit IDs, not branch names; make sure each selected commit is reachable from the intended upstream branch before the outer push.

> Do not create `TODO.md`/`ROADMAP.md`/`backlog/`/`pitfalls/` at this level — the submodules have independent upstreams and get cloned standalone, so a note that lives only here is invisible in the repo that has to act on it.
> **A cross-cutting item is split, not duplicated.** … **one** `backlog/<slug>.md` goes there, the other submodule gets a `TODO.md` line only, and the platform-agnostic *decision* goes in `docs/` here.

**Automation** (`justfile`, the most complete gitlink tooling of the four):
- `submodule-status` runs `git status --short --branch` on the outer repo, then `git submodule status --recursive`, then status on each child.
- `submodule-diff` runs `git diff [--cached] --submodule=log`.
- `submodule-fetch` runs `fetch --prune` in each child and does not move HEAD.
- `submodule-sync`; `submodule-bootstrap` runs `git submodule update --init --recursive`. The docs say it "may leave a submodule on detached HEAD. It is deliberately not part of any default recipe."
- `submodule-pull-main` requires every child to be clean, refuses a detached commit that origin/main can't reach, refuses a diverged main, then runs `switch main` + `merge --ff-only origin/main`.
- `gitlink-stage-{unix,windows,ish,openwrt,termux,all}` runs a preflight first (child initialized, clean including untracked files, `merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main`), then `git add`.
- `gitlink-review` checks the staged gitlink SHAs are reachable from origin/main.

- CI (`.github/workflows/check.yml`) runs `python -m unittest discover -s tests` on ubuntu and windows against disposable local fixture repos.

**README.** "Five independent repositories, checked out together for maintenance." It recommends `git clone --recurse-submodules`.

Key verbatim section from `AGENTS.md`:
> ## Submodule gitlinks and finishing work
> - Root gitlinks track each child's latest merged default branch (`origin/HEAD`), not a local or feature-branch commit. **Automation.**
- `scripts/repo_audit.py` (`just repo-audit`) runs over the root plus every submodule, recursively. It reports:

  - uncommitted changes and stashes;
  - extra worktrees, flagged "UNCOMMITTED CHANGES (back up before removing)" or "removable";

# Cross-repo synthesis

| Convention | dotfiles-all | Tadronaut | AlphaResearch | Tons |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name for itself | "umbrella superproject" | "Monorepo" / "coordination and investigation workspace" | "monorepo" (ADR 0001) | "thin coordination repository" / 整合 repo (integration repo) |
| Child location | root | `submodules/{,personal/,references/<owner>/}` | `libs/`, `knowledge/`, `references/<stage>/` | `submodules/` (enforced depth 2) |
| Count | 5 | 25 (+nested) | 37 (+nested) | 5 |
| Owners | single | mixed orgs + GitLab | mixed + 3rd-party | org + personal |
| `.gitmodules` options | none | 1 `branch=` | refs: `shallow/update=none/fetchRecurseSubmodules=false` | none |
| Gitlink policy | track child origin/main tip, pushed | track merged `origin/HEAD`; refs pinned | libs bumped after push/merge; refs pinned | "keep pinned" |
| Inside-out commit rule written? | yes, detailed | yes (PR/merge first) | yes (one line per lib) | no |
| One outer commit per change | explicit rule | de facto (bumps folded into feature commits) | per-bump commits | per-pin commits |
| Recursive init | `--recursive` bootstrap is opt-in | core only (scripted) | **forbidden** | none |
| Init tool | `just submodule-bootstrap` | `init_submodules.py` (preserve) | `just setup` / `just refs` | `workspace.py init` (preserve) |
| Status/audit sweep | `just submodule-status`, `gitlink-review` | `just repo-audit` (best) | `just refs-status` only | `just workspace-check` |
| Worktree convention | `.claude/worktrees/` ignored | external `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>`, `backup/*` branches | none written | `.claude/worktrees/` ignored |
| Child list with roles | CLAUDE.md table | delegated to `navigation` submodule | AGENTS.md Layout table | README table |
| CLAUDE.md | yes (AGENTS.md is a symlink to it) | **missing** | `@AGENTS.md` | **missing** |
| Project memory at root | forbidden (in children) | TODO/backlog/pitfalls + context/ + td | TODO/backlog/pitfalls + td | TODO/backlog/pitfalls + context/ |
| Root environment | none | none (PEP 723 scripts) | uv editable path sources | none |
| CI | yes (fixture tests) | no | no | no |
| Commit style | conventional | prose + "; bump X (#n)" | conventional + `(child#n)` | conventional |
| `.specstory` backup commits | yes | yes | yes | ignored |

**What all four share:**
1. Child repos are git submodules with independent upstreams. The root holds no product code (AlphaResearch is the partial exception).
2. "Read the child's own AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md before editing it" (dotfiles, Tadronaut, AlphaResearch).
3. Work is committed and pushed inside the child before the root pointer moves; the root never points at an unpushed commit. Three of four state this explicitly; Tons does it implicitly by pinning.
4. Initialization never disturbs existing child checkouts. Tadronaut and Tons check "HEAD ≠ gitlink → preserve and report"; dotfiles' pull-main refuses dirty, detached-unreachable or diverged children.
5. Blanket `--recurse-submodules` is not the default in 3 of 4 repos.
6. `just` is the entry point, and helpers are read-only or explicit: they never commit or push on their own.
7. The project-knowledge-harness layout (TODO.md / backlog / pitfalls), `.claude/plans` via `plansDirectory`, and `.specstory`.

**Where they diverge:**
- **Where project memory lives.** dotfiles forbids root TODO.md/backlog and puts memory in each child. The other three keep it at the root.
- **What a gitlink means.** Tadronaut says "latest merged main". Tons says "pinned". AlphaResearch says "pinned refs + bumped libs". dotfiles says "origin/main tip".
- **Child tiers.** Writable vs read-only reference children appear in Tadronaut and AlphaResearch, encoded differently: Tadronaut by path group plus a script, AlphaResearch by `.gitmodules` `update=none`.
- **Where child roles are listed.** CLAUDE.md vs README vs a navigation submodule.
- **CLAUDE.md presence.** Claude Code may not load the instructions in Tadronaut or Tons.
- **Worktree placement.** Only Tadronaut uses external `~/Worktrees`, which matches the `dev` CLI default. Two repos only gitignore `.claude/worktrees/`.

**Pain points visible today:**
- Orphan worktrees whose admin dir was deleted along with a root worktree: 5 under `~/Worktrees/OfflineAnalysis/*` and `~/Worktrees/feat-nas-feature-quality/feat-zr-paper-backtest`. `Tadronaut-Mono-Repo/backlog/worktree-consolidation.md` predicted exactly this: "Deleting that parent worktree/admin namespace could sever all five linked checkouts." The cause is a submodule's git store nested inside a *root linked worktree* (`.git/worktrees/<wt>/modules/...`). The lesson: create child worktrees from the canonical child store, not from inside a root worktree.
- `TODO.md` line 52 in Tadronaut: "**[M] 安全回收已整合 worktree** … 處理研究 worktree 內的共用子模組 Git store" (safely reclaim integrated worktrees … deal with the shared submodule Git stores inside research worktrees). Also `backlog/lazytarlin-v030-data-inventory.md`: a child commit "not pushed, so the root gitlink stays at `2bad12e`".
- `git submodule status` misreports initialized children as `-` in Tadronaut (24 of 25) and Tons (5 of 5) because `.git/config` lacks the entries. A skill should derive state from `submodule foreach` or `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, as `repo_audit.py` and `workspace.py` do.
- Stale `.git/config` and `.git/modules` entries for a removed or renamed submodule (`conbond-deep-model`, `jingle_ats`).
- Pointer drift: AlphaResearch `knowledge/` `+` (2 commits unstaged) and outer main 5 commits ahead and unpushed. Tadronaut children are detached (tarlin, OfflineAnalysis, infra) or dirty (tarlin, ConvertibleBond, trading-journal on a feature branch).
- Local branches with no upstream in dotfiles-all, plus a stash. `chore/single-conbond-model-checkout` in Tadronaut is not merged.
- The same repo appears in several home repos: `quant-data-kit` in Tadronaut `personal/` and AlphaResearch `libs/`; `2026-04-02-data-platform` in both; `nautilus_trader` as a fork in Tons and upstream in AlphaResearch. That makes worktree ownership ambiguous.

**Existing helpers that already solve part of this:**
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/Tadronaut-Mono-Repo/scripts/repo_audit.py`: recursive audit of branches, dirty state, stashes, worktrees and gitlink drift. It is the strongest base for a "status sweep / hand-off gate" step.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dotfiles-all/justfile` (`gitlink-stage-*`, `gitlink-review`, `submodule-pull-main`) and `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dotfiles-all/docs/superproject-justfile.md`: the inside-out bump workflow with preflight checks, plus fixture tests in `dotfiles-all/tests/test_gitlinks.py`.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/Tadronaut-Mono-Repo/scripts/init_submodules.py` and `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/Tons-Mono-Repo/scripts/workspace.py`: init that preserves existing checkouts, each with tests.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/AlphaResearch/justfile` `refs`/`refs-config`: the read-only reference tier through `.gitmodules` options.
- The **`dev` CLI** (`/opt/homebrew/bin/dev`, source at `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli`):
  - `dev git submodule status|init|develop|recover`; `develop` "Add[s] selected submodules to the current managed task branch" with `--submodule-base PATH=REF`.
  - `dev git worktree create|list|open|rm|provision`, with the documented placement `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>`.
  - `dev work start --submodule PATH`, and `--recursive` retire that checks child recovery before removal.
  - `dev help worktrees` and `dev help agents` ("Worktree per change stream").
  - Repo-local policy through `.dev-cli/config.toml` (`[submodules] init = "none"` in Tons).

  This overlaps heavily with the proposed skill. A new skill would likely work best as a thin agent playbook that calls `dev`, `repo_audit.py` and the gitlink-review checks, rather than reimplementing them.

- **Claude Code 的 `--worktree` 不保證初始化 submodule**：文件只提到清理時會檢查 submodule 是否有未提交修改，沒說新 worktree 會初始化 submodule。這是推論，不是文件明載。
