The biggest finding is the gap between the written rules and the actual state. Two repos have written rules, two have helper scripts, and there are live examples of the failures the skill should prevent.

# Per-repo findings

## 1. dotfiles-all (`/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dotfiles-all`)

**Layout.** There are 5 submodules, all directly at the root: `dotfiles-unix`, `dotfiles-windows`, `dotfiles-iSH`, `dotfiles-OpenWrt` and `dotfiles-Termux`. The root also has `docs/`, `scripts/native-guard.sh`, `tests/` (with `test_gitlinks.py` and `test_native_guard.py`), `.github/workflows/check.yml`, `.specstory/`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `justfile` and `skills-lock.json`.

**`.gitmodules`.**
- All 5 point to the same owner, `daviddwlee84`, with a mix of ssh and https URLs.
- No `branch=`, `ignore=` or `update=` is set.
- One rename: the submodule *name* is `dotfiles` but its path is `dotfiles-unix`. The README says "The Unix folder was renamed locally; its GitHub repository remains `dotfiles`."
- No nested submodules. One non-submodule sibling matters: the live chezmoi source `~/.local/share/chezmoi` is a separate clone.

**Outer repo.**
- On `main`. There are 2 local branches with no upstream (`chore/windows-bootstrap-sshd-gitlink`, `fix/copilot-auto-without-plan-floor`, both from September) and 1 stash.
- Commits use conventional-commit style. Pointer bumps are made by hand, e.g. `chore(submodule): bump dotfiles-iSH — Herdr/Rust compat …` and `chore(submodules): adopt cross-platform editor selection and Micro`.
- 12 of 66 commits are `chore: backup plan and chat history`.

**Submodule state.** All 5 are on `main`, clean, with no extra worktrees. `.gitignore` excludes `.claude/worktrees/` ("Ephemeral EnterWorktree checkouts").

**Agent files.**
- `CLAUDE.md` is the main file; `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to it.
- It has a table of the child repos with upstream, scope and package-layer roles.
- It calls itself an **"umbrella superproject"**.
- `.claude/settings.json` holds only `plansDirectory`. One skill is vendored: `.agents/skills/project-knowledge-harness`, with a symlink from `.claude/skills`.

Key verbatim sections from `CLAUDE.md`:
&gt; - **Commit from the inside out.** First commit and push every affected submodule to its own remote; only then commit the gitlink pointer bump in this superproject. `git submodule status` shows drift, and a superproject pointer to an unpushed commit dangles for every other clone.
&gt; - **One cross-repo change gets one outer pointer commit.** … stage **all affected** gitlinks … and record them together in a single superproject commit. Do not make one outer commit per submodule or leave the second pointer as unrelated working-tree drift. … verify … with `git diff --cached --submodule=log -- …`
&gt; - … Gitlinks record commit IDs, not branch names; make sure each selected commit is reachable from the intended upstream branch before the outer push.

&gt; Do not create `TODO.md`/`ROADMAP.md`/`backlog/`/`pitfalls/` at this level — the submodules have independent upstreams and get cloned standalone, so a note that lives only here is invisible in the repo that has to act on it.
&gt; **A cross-cutting item is split, not duplicated.** … **one** `backlog/&lt;slug&gt;.md` goes there, the other submodule gets a `TODO.md` line only, and the platform-agnostic *decision* goes in `docs/` here.

**Automation** (`justfile`, the most complete gitlink tooling of the four):
- `submodule-status` runs `git status --short --branch` on the outer repo, then `git submodule status --recursive`, then status on each child.
- `submodule-diff` runs `git diff [--cached] --submodule=log`.
- `submodule-fetch` runs `fetch --prune` in each child and does not move HEAD.
- `submodule-sync`; `submodule-bootstrap` runs `git submodule update --init --recursive`. The docs say it "may leave a submodule on detached HEAD. It is deliberately not part of any default recipe."
- `submodule-pull-main` requires every child to be clean, refuses a detached commit that origin/main can't reach, refuses a diverged main, then runs `switch main` + `merge --ff-only origin/main`.
- `gitlink-stage-{unix,windows,ish,openwrt,termux,all}` runs a preflight first (child initialized, clean including untracked files, `merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main`), then `git add`.
- `gitlink-review` checks the staged gitlink SHAs are reachable from origin/main.
- Every recipe exists in both bash and pwsh versions. The docs say: "These helpers never pull, commit, or push."
- CI (`.github/workflows/check.yml`) runs `python -m unittest discover -s tests` on ubuntu and windows against disposable local fixture repos.

- `scripts/repo_audit.py` (`just repo-audit`) runs over the root plus every submodule, recursively. It reports:

  - extra worktrees, flagged "UNCOMMITTED CHANGES (back up before removing)" or "removable";

# Cross-repo synthesis

| Convention | dotfiles-all | Tadronaut | AlphaResearch | Tons |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name for itself | "umbrella superproject" | "Monorepo" / "coordination and investigation workspace" | "monorepo" (ADR 0001) | "thin coordination repository" / 整合 repo (integration repo) |
| Child location | root | `submodules/{,personal/,references/&lt;owner&gt;/}` | `libs/`, `knowledge/`, `references/&lt;stage&gt;/` | `submodules/` (enforced depth 2) |
| Count | 5 | 25 (+nested) | 37 (+nested) | 5 |
| Owners | single | mixed orgs + GitLab | mixed + 3rd-party | org + personal |
| `.gitmodules` options | none | 1 `branch=` | refs: `shallow/update=none/fetchRecurseSubmodules=false` | none |
| Gitlink policy | track child origin/main tip, pushed | track merged `origin/HEAD`; refs pinned | libs bumped after push/merge; refs pinned | "keep pinned" |
| Inside-out commit rule written? | yes, detailed | yes (PR/merge first) | yes (one line per lib) | no |
| One outer commit per change | explicit rule | de facto (bumps folded into feature commits) | per-bump commits | per-pin commits |
| Recursive init | `--recursive` bootstrap is opt-in | core only (scripted) | **forbidden** | none |
| Init tool | `just submodule-bootstrap` | `init_submodules.py` (preserve) | `just setup` / `just refs` | `workspace.py init` (preserve) |
| Status/audit sweep | `just submodule-status`, `gitlink-review` | `just repo-audit` (best) | `just refs-status` only | `just workspace-check` |
| Worktree convention | `.claude/worktrees/` ignored | external `~/Worktrees/&lt;repo&gt;/&lt;slug&gt;`, `backup/*` branches | none written | `.claude/worktrees/` ignored |
| Child list with roles | CLAUDE.md table | delegated to `navigation` submodule | AGENTS.md Layout table | README table |
| CLAUDE.md | yes (AGENTS.md is a symlink to it) | **missing** | `@AGENTS.md` | **missing** |
| Project memory at root | forbidden (in children) | TODO/backlog/pitfalls + context/ + td | TODO/backlog/pitfalls + td | TODO/backlog/pitfalls + context/ |
| Root environment | none | none (PEP 723 scripts) | uv editable path sources | none |
| CI | yes (fixture tests) | no | no | no |
| Commit style | conventional | prose + "; bump X (#n)" | conventional + `(child#n)` | conventional |
| `.specstory` backup commits | yes | yes | yes | ignored |

**What all four share:**
1. Child repos are git submodules with independent upstreams. The root holds no product code (AlphaResearch is the partial exception).
2. "Read the child's own AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md before editing it" (dotfiles, Tadronaut, AlphaResearch).
3. Work is committed and pushed inside the child before the root pointer moves; the root never points at an unpushed commit. Three of four state this explicitly; Tons does it implicitly by pinning.
4. Initialization never disturbs existing child checkouts. Tadronaut and Tons check "HEAD ≠ gitlink → preserve and report"; dotfiles' pull-main refuses dirty, detached-unreachable or diverged children.
5. Blanket `--recurse-submodules` is not the default in 3 of 4 repos.
6. `just` is the entry point, and helpers are read-only or explicit: they never commit or push on their own.
7. The project-knowledge-harness layout (TODO.md / backlog / pitfalls), `.claude/plans` via `plansDirectory`, and `.specstory`.

**Where they diverge:**
- **Where project memory lives.** dotfiles forbids root TODO.md/backlog and puts memory in each child. The other three keep it at the root.
- **What a gitlink means.** Tadronaut says "latest merged main". Tons says "pinned". AlphaResearch says "pinned refs + bumped libs". dotfiles says "origin/main tip".
- **Child tiers.** Writable vs read-only reference children appear in Tadronaut and AlphaResearch, encoded differently: Tadronaut by path group plus a script, AlphaResearch by `.gitmodules` `update=none`.
- **Where child roles are listed.** CLAUDE.md vs README vs a navigation submodule.
- **CLAUDE.md presence.** Claude Code may not load the instructions in Tadronaut or Tons.
- **Worktree placement.** Only Tadronaut uses external `~/Worktrees`, which matches the `dev` CLI default. Two repos only gitignore `.claude/worktrees/`.

**Pain points visible today:**
- Orphan worktrees whose admin dir was deleted along with a root worktree: 5 under `~/Worktrees/OfflineAnalysis/*` and `~/Worktrees/feat-nas-feature-quality/feat-zr-paper-backtest`. `Tadronaut-Mono-Repo/backlog/worktree-consolidation.md` predicted exactly this: "Deleting that parent worktree/admin namespace could sever all five linked checkouts." The cause is a submodule's git store nested inside a *root linked worktree* (`.git/worktrees/&lt;wt&gt;/modules/...`). The lesson: create child worktrees from the canonical child store, not from inside a root worktree.
- `TODO.md` line 52 in Tadronaut: "**[M] 安全回收已整合 worktree** … 處理研究 worktree 內的共用子模組 Git store" (safely reclaim integrated worktrees … deal with the shared submodule Git stores inside research worktrees). Also `backlog/lazytarlin-v030-data-inventory.md`: a child commit "not pushed, so the root gitlink stays at `2bad12e`".
- `git submodule status` misreports initialized children as `-` in Tadronaut (24 of 25) and Tons (5 of 5) because `.git/config` lacks the entries. A skill should derive state from `submodule foreach` or `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, as `repo_audit.py` and `workspace.py` do.
- Stale `.git/config` and `.git/modules` entries for a removed or renamed submodule (`conbond-deep-model`, `jingle_ats`).
- Pointer drift: AlphaResearch `knowledge/` `+` (2 commits unstaged) and outer main 5 commits ahead and unpushed. Tadronaut children are detached (tarlin, OfflineAnalysis, infra) or dirty (tarlin, ConvertibleBond, trading-journal on a feature branch).
- Local branches with no upstream in dotfiles-all, plus a stash. `chore/single-conbond-model-checkout` in Tadronaut is not merged.
- The same repo appears in several home repos: `quant-data-kit` in Tadronaut `personal/` and AlphaResearch `libs/`; `2026-04-02-data-platform` in both; `nautilus_trader` as a fork in Tons and upstream in AlphaResearch. That makes worktree ownership ambiguous.

**Existing helpers that already solve part of this:**
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/Tadronaut-Mono-Repo/scripts/repo_audit.py`: recursive audit of branches, dirty state, stashes, worktrees and gitlink drift. It is the strongest base for a "status sweep / hand-off gate" step.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dotfiles-all/justfile` (`gitlink-stage-*`, `gitlink-review`, `submodule-pull-main`) and `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dotfiles-all/docs/superproject-justfile.md`: the inside-out bump workflow with preflight checks, plus fixture tests in `dotfiles-all/tests/test_gitlinks.py`.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/Tadronaut-Mono-Repo/scripts/init_submodules.py` and `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/Tons-Mono-Repo/scripts/workspace.py`: init that preserves existing checkouts, each with tests.
- `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/AlphaResearch/justfile` `refs`/`refs-config`: the read-only reference tier through `.gitmodules` options.
- The **`dev` CLI** (`/opt/homebrew/bin/dev`, source at `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli`):
  - `dev git submodule status|init|develop|recover`; `develop` "Add[s] selected submodules to the current managed task branch" with `--submodule-base PATH=REF`.
  - `dev git worktree create|list|open|rm|provision`, with the documented placement `~/Worktrees/&lt;repo&gt;/&lt;slug&gt;`.
  - `dev work start --submodule PATH`, and `--recursive` retire that checks child recovery before removal.

- **Policy per child** as extra keys in `.gitmodules`: `x-policy track|pin|lazy`, `x-bump pr|direct|manual`, `x-tier` (SKILL.md L35-64).
- **CLI subcommands:** `status | init | pull | bump | preflight | worktree add|list|remove | audit | adopt | ci-plan` (L160-165). Every command takes `--json`; mutating ones take `--dry-run`. Exit codes 0/1/2.
- **Bottom-up commits and pointer bumps:** `bump` refuses dirty or unpushed children and makes one outer commit with a `--submodule=log` body (L115-127). `preflight` also installs as a pre-commit hook.
- **Child worktrees:**
  - Location is `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch-with-/-replaced-by->` inside the superproject (`wt_path`, superproject.py L614-615). It adds `.worktrees/` to `.gitignore` (L618-627).
  - `track` children branch from `origin/<branch>`. `pin` and `lazy` children branch from the recorded gitlink (L660-670).
  - Cleanup is `worktree list` (flags merged ones) plus `worktree remove <child> <branch> --delete-branch` (L630-686).
  - `references/worktrees.md` says never to make worktrees of the superproject itself.
- **Bootstrap for an existing repo:** `adopt` (L843+) writes:
  - the policy keys
  - a marker-delimited AGENTS.md block (`assets/agents-block.md.template`)
  - `just sub-*` recipes (`assets/justfile.snippet`)
  - local git config (`diff.submodule=log`, `status.submoduleSummary`, `push.recurseSubmodules=check`)
  - optional CI (`assets/superproject-bump.yml`, `child-dispatch.yml`) and the hook
- **CLI is referenced, not copied:** resolution order is `$SUPERPROJECT_CLI` > vendored copy > `.agents/skills` > `~/.agents/skills` > GitHub raw at `$SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF`.
- **Agent entry point:** `references/agent-entry.md` covers AGENTS.md layering, root context, Claude/Codex Projects and add-dir. `references/decision-guide.md` compares monorepo, submodules, manifest plus gitignored clones, and add-dir.
- **Related files:** `backlog/superproject-workspace-adoption.md` (P2 adoption checklist) and the original design plan `.claude/plans/ai-repo-reference-monorepo-jaunty-scone.md`.

**What it does not cover (where your idea would add something):**
- **Gitignored-clones / "home repo" mode** is out of scope on purpose. SKILL.md L33 says "only the decision guide applies", and the plan made the same decision at L28.
- **No way to create a new superproject or add a child.** There is no `new` or `add` subcommand. `adopt` assumes `.gitmodules` already exists, and `find_root` (L139-157) fails without it.
- **No naming or branching conventions for the outer repo.**
- **No multi-child task worktrees.** There is nothing like the Gemini note's `start-task <task> <mod1> <mod2>` that gives several children the same branch, and no `cleanup <task>`. Worktrees are created and removed one child at a time.
- **No uv workspace or shared-venv guidance.**

### `forge-native-dev` (read fully)
- **Naming:**
  - Worktree dir: `$FORGE_WORKTREE_ROOT` (default `.worktrees`) + `/issue-<n>/` (`forge-worktree.sh` L19, L132).
  - Branch: `issue/<n>-<slug>`, or `agent/issue/<n>-<slug>` with `--agent` (L125-130).
  - Slug: `forge_slugify` (forge.sh L726-731) lowercases, turns non-alphanumerics into `-`, and cuts at 50 chars.
  - Base: `origin/<default>` from `forge_default_branch` (forge.sh L749-759).
  - `finish` pushes and opens a PR with "Closes #n".
- **Cleanup** (`forge-cleanup.sh`):
  - Scans `issue/*` and `agent/issue/*`. A branch is cleaned if its PR is merged, if it is closed and `--all` is set, or if there is no PR and the upstream is gone (L81-101).
  - Then `git worktree remove --force`, `git branch -D`, `git worktree prune`.
  - It shows an **interactive `[y/N]` prompt** unless `--force` (L137-144), which breaks the house no-prompt rule.
- **Status** (`forge-status.sh`): lists open issues against their branches and PRs, orphan branches, and only `.worktrees/issue-*`.
- **Single repo:** yes. Everything uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and the `origin` of the current directory.
- **Inside a submodule:** it resolves to the child repo and the child's forge, so the meaning is right. But it creates `.worktrees/issue-N` inside the submodule checkout. The child shows untracked content unless `forge-init.sh` L211-214 has added `.worktrees/` to its `.gitignore`, and the superproject then shows `modified: app (untracked content)`. That path also differs from superproject-workspace's `.worktrees/<child>/<branch>`. Run from the superproject root, it knows nothing about the children.
- **Coexistence rule** is already written down: `references/coexistence.md` L110-120 says forge-native-dev handles child issues and PRs plus outer-only `.worktrees/issue-<n>`, and superproject-workspace handles pointers and child worktrees.
- **Latent bug (verified):** `local` is used outside any function:
  - `forge-cleanup.sh` L94, 107, 156
  - `forge-status.sh` L104, 114, 115, 125, 127, 131, 157, 162, 169, 170, 174, 197, 202, 204, 208

  With `set -euo pipefail` this aborts: I ran `bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; while true; do local x=1; ...'` and it exited 1 with "local: can only be used in a function". `shellcheck -S error` reports SC2168. In practice, forge-cleanup dies on the first branch it can clean, and forge-status dies on the first open issue. No gate catches it (see section 2).

That gives **three conflicting worktree-location conventions**:

## 2. House conventions for a local skill

**Scaffolding:** `bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>`
- Scope flags: `--local`, `--project`, `--global`. Other flags: `--vendor`, `--root DIR`, `--no-symlinks`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
- It creates `SKILL.md` (from `assets/SKILL.md.template`) plus `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` with `.gitkeep`. It prints JSON `{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}`.
- `--local` without `--no-symlinks` adds `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` links. CLAUDE.md says to keep those only for skills useful while working on this repo. superproject-workspace used `--no-symlinks` (plan L101).
- The directory is called `assets/`, not `templates/`. Template files use a `.template` suffix.

**Frontmatter:**
- Only `name` and `description`. Name is hyphen-case, at most 64 chars, and should match the directory name.
- Description needs "Use when…" phrasing with concrete triggers. 120-500 chars preferred, 501-900 is context-heavy, over 1024 is invalid. It can include zh-TW trigger phrases; superproject-workspace L3 and forge-native-dev L3 do.
- **Quote the description if it contains `: ` or ` #`** (forge-native-dev uses single quotes). See `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md`.
- The skill body is English.

**Body (from the template):** When to use, When NOT to use, Workflow (numbered imperative steps), Available scripts, Bundled assets, Reference files (each with a "read when…" condition), and a required **Gotchas** section.
- `references/authoring-patterns.md` adds output templates, validation loops (plan, validate, execute), calibrated specificity, and defaults over menus.
- SKILL.md should stay under 500 lines: lint warns at 500 and fails above 700. Local skills run 38-629 lines, typically about 150-250 (superproject-workspace 200, project-knowledge-harness 225, skill-author 240).

**Scripts** (`references/script-design.md`, `this-repo-conventions.md` L137-154):
- No interactive prompts. `--help` is the main documentation.
- `--dry-run` for anything destructive.
- Data on stdout (JSON), prose on stderr. Errors say what was expected and what to try.
- Bash must be 3.2 compatible: no `mapfile`, `${var,,}`, or `[[ -v ]]`. Bash is preferred for orchestration; PEP 723 `uv run --script` Python is fine for heavier helpers. Pin `uvx`/`npx` versions.

**What the "lint sourced libraries" commit (d47cf9d) actually changed:**
- It is `skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh` check 2 (L253-302). Files in `scripts/*.sh` with `# skill-lint: sourced-only` in the leading comment header must be non-executable and pass `bash -n`. Other scripts need a shebang, `+x`, and a literal `--help`.
- Only `forge-native-dev/scripts/forge.sh` carries the marker. `project-knowledge-harness/scripts/_lib/*.sh` sit in a subdirectory, so the glob never sees them.
- Regression tests: `skills/local/skill-author/tests/test_lint_skill.py`, run with `uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/skill-author/tests/ -q`.
- **There is no make target for it, and shellcheck is not a gate anywhere.** `make validate` never runs lint-skill.sh, which is why the forge `local` bug slipped through. You run lint-skill.sh by hand. Both superproject-workspace and forge-native-dev pass it with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

**Best structural models for "bootstrap + ongoing maintenance, ships scripts + templates":**
1. **`superproject-workspace`**: one PEP 723 CLI with subcommands (bootstrap via `audit`/`adopt`, maintenance via `status`/`pull`/`bump`/`worktree`). `assets/` holds a marker-block AGENTS.md template, a managed justfile block, a CI workflow, and a hook. Seven focused `references/`. `tests/` uses stdlib unittest against local bare-repo fixtures.
2. **`project-knowledge-harness`**: Bash. `scripts/init.sh` is an idempotent bootstrap (`--target`, `--force`, sentinel-marker appends, agent-contract auto-detect). Maintenance scripts are `add-todo`, `promote-todo`, `sweep-inbox`, `todo-kanban`, `start-todo`, with shared libraries in `scripts/_lib/`. Eight `assets/*.template` files and four references.
3. Runner-up: `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` (`init-docs-site.sh` plus `add-*` maintenance scripts, and Bash tests wired into the Makefile and CI). forge-native-dev has a similar shape but carries the bug above.

  - `engineering-quality`, `quantitative-finance`, `go-cli`, `fullstack-nextjs`, `fastapi-ai`, `engineering-fundamentals`, `product-planning`, `github-workflow`
  - `version-control`, `web-quality`, `generative-ui`, `security`, `deep-research`
  - `browser-userscripts`, `desktop-extensions`, `music-notation`

  **Best fit: `version-control`** (L198-209: git-workflow, forge-native-dev, superproject-workspace; its tags already include submodules and superproject). The picker sorts alphabetically, and the `NN-` prefixes are deliberate. Path format is `./local/<name>`.
- **Docs:**
  - `docs/skills/<name>.md` and `docs/skills/<name>.zh-TW.md`. All 46 existing pages are paired. mkdocs i18n uses `docs_structure: suffix` with `fallback_to_default: true`.
  - A row in `docs/skills/index.md` and in `index.zh-TW.md`.
  - A nav entry in `mkdocs.yml` under Skills → Local (around L113-140; superproject-workspace is L131). The llmstxt sections pick up `skills/*.md` by glob.
  - Sources: `this-repo-conventions.md` L103-117 and `docs/workflows/creating-local-skills.md` L78-87.
- **README** "What's in here" list (L81-102). superproject-workspace and forge-native-dev are both missing from it today.
- **`make validate`** (Makefile L50-53, also the pre-push hook):
  - `lint-frontmatter.sh --quiet skills`: YAML-parses every frontmatter; the root must be a mapping with string `name` and `description`.
  - `validate-marketplace.sh`: valid JSON, name not reserved, every listed path has a SKILL.md, no duplicates, and a warning for unlisted skills.
  - `todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`: TODO.md format.
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/validate.yml`) also runs:
  - `test-source-sync`, `test-vectorbt-skill`, `test-nautilus-trader-skill`, `test-mkdocs-skill`, `test-zensical-skill`
  - the frontmatter lint with the node `yaml` parser
  - `native-marketplace-smoke`
- **Tests:** each skill has its own `tests/` (Python unittest/pytest or Bash scripts), plus a `test-<skill>-skill` Makefile target and a CI step, with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` for git fixtures. There is no bats harness. **superproject-workspace's tests are not wired into the Makefile or CI.**

- **Matt Pocock:** `docs/reference/mattpocock-skills.md` (+zh-TW), `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` L38 (marked "vendored (partial)", as the `engineering-fundamentals` series), and `backlog/evaluate-remaining-mattpocock-skills-for-engineering-fundamentals.md`. None of them mention a home repo.

- **TODO.md** has nothing planned on this. The only follow-up is `backlog/superproject-workspace-adoption.md`.

  - `chatgpt-跨机器使用方案-20261015-2132.md` (L261-292) is tangential: td shares its database across worktrees on one machine, and td-sync does not link clones by remote URL.
  - `chatgpt-列出Lazy工具…` only mentions lazygit worktrees.
  - `chatgpt-GitHub-Pages…` is unrelated.
- **The Gemini note** proposes a `workspace-assembler` skill with `scripts/sub-ops.sh` and `templates/CLAUDE.template.md`:
  - Mode A (submodules) vs Mode B (home repo: gitignored `modules/`)
  - `start-task` creating worktrees outside the repo at `../.worktrees/<task>/<repo>`
  - `.gitmodules` with `ignore = dirty`
  - a uv workspace with `PYTHONPATH` override for worktrees

  Mode B, multi-child tasks, and uv workspace are the real gaps. The outside-repo worktree location and `ignore = dirty` conflict with superproject-workspace's choices.

**Before designing:** the plan behind superproject-workspace already decided "no-submodule alternative = decision guide only" and "never superproject worktrees". A new skill will probably either extend superproject-workspace (v0.3: `add`/`new`, multi-child `task` worktrees, a manifest mode) or be a thin companion only for gitignored clones. Either way, pick one worktree-location convention across superproject-workspace, dev-cli, and the new skill.

## 2. House conventions for a local skill

**Scaffolding:** `bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks &lt;name&gt;`
- Scope flags: `--local`, `--project`, `--global`. Other flags: `--vendor`, `--root DIR`, `--no-symlinks`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
- It creates `SKILL.md` (from `assets/SKILL.md.template`) plus `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` with `.gitkeep`. It prints JSON `{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}`.
- `--local` without `--no-symlinks` adds `.agents/skills/&lt;name&gt;` and `.claude/skills/&lt;name&gt;` links. CLAUDE.md says to keep those only for skills useful while working on this repo. superproject-workspace used `--no-symlinks` (plan L101).
- The directory is called `assets/`, not `templates/`. Template files use a `.template` suffix.

**Frontmatter:**
- Only `name` and `description`. Name is hyphen-case, at most 64 chars, and should match the directory name.
- Description needs "Use when…" phrasing with concrete triggers. 120-500 chars preferred, 501-900 is context-heavy, over 1024 is invalid. It can include zh-TW trigger phrases; superproject-workspace L3 and forge-native-dev L3 do.
- **Quote the description if it contains `: ` or ` #`** (forge-native-dev uses single quotes). See `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md`.
- The skill body is English.

**Body (from the template):** When to use, When NOT to use, Workflow (numbered imperative steps), Available scripts, Bundled assets, Reference files (each with a "read when…" condition), and a required **Gotchas** section.
- `references/authoring-patterns.md` adds output templates, validation loops (plan, validate, execute), calibrated specificity, and defaults over menus.
- SKILL.md should stay under 500 lines: lint warns at 500 and fails above 700. Local skills run 38-629 lines, typically about 150-250 (superproject-workspace 200, project-knowledge-harness 225, skill-author 240).

**Scripts** (`references/script-design.md`, `this-repo-conventions.md` L137-154):
- No interactive prompts. `--help` is the main documentation.
- `--dry-run` for anything destructive.
- Data on stdout (JSON), prose on stderr. Errors say what was expected and what to try.
- Bash must be 3.2 compatible: no `mapfile`, `${var,,}`, or `[[ -v ]]`. Bash is preferred for orchestration; PEP 723 `uv run --script` Python is fine for heavier helpers. Pin `uvx`/`npx` versions.

**What the "lint sourced libraries" commit (d47cf9d) actually changed:**
- It is `skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh` check 2 (L253-302). Files in `scripts/*.sh` with `# skill-lint: sourced-only` in the leading comment header must be non-executable and pass `bash -n`. Other scripts need a shebang, `+x`, and a literal `--help`.
- Only `forge-native-dev/scripts/forge.sh` carries the marker. `project-knowledge-harness/scripts/_lib/*.sh` sit in a subdirectory, so the glob never sees them.
- Regression tests: `skills/local/skill-author/tests/test_lint_skill.py`, run with `uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/skill-author/tests/ -q`.
- **There is no make target for it, and shellcheck is not a gate anywhere.** `make validate` never runs lint-skill.sh, which is why the forge `local` bug slipped through. You run lint-skill.sh by hand. Both superproject-workspace and forge-native-dev pass it with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

**Best structural models for "bootstrap + ongoing maintenance, ships scripts + templates":**
1. **`superproject-workspace`**: one PEP 723 CLI with subcommands (bootstrap via `audit`/`adopt`, maintenance via `status`/`pull`/`bump`/`worktree`). `assets/` holds a marker-block AGENTS.md template, a managed justfile block, a CI workflow, and a hook. Seven focused `references/`. `tests/` uses stdlib unittest against local bare-repo fixtures.
2. **`project-knowledge-harness`**: Bash. `scripts/init.sh` is an idempotent bootstrap (`--target`, `--force`, sentinel-marker appends, agent-contract auto-detect). Maintenance scripts are `add-todo`, `promote-todo`, `sweep-inbox`, `todo-kanban`, `start-todo`, with shared libraries in `scripts/_lib/`. Eight `assets/*.template` files and four references.
3. Runner-up: `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` (`init-docs-site.sh` plus `add-*` maintenance scripts, and Bash tests wired into the Makefile and CI). forge-native-dev has a similar shape but carries the bug above.

# Adopt superproject-workspace in existing superprojects

**Status**: P2 (follow-up to #33)
**Effort**: M per superproject
**Related**: [`skills/local/superproject-workspace`](../skills/local/superproject-workspace/SKILL.md) · `references/case-patterns.md`

## Context

2026-10-28: `superproject-workspace` shipped with `audit` and `adopt`. A
read-only smoke run against the maintainer's two reference superprojects (an
umbrella and a workspace hub) found:

- no policy keys
- an umbrella child 9 commits ahead of its recorded pointer
- several hub gitlinks reachable from no `origin` branch in local refs (re-check with `audit --fetch`)
- checkouts sitting on feature branches with dirty trees
- child paths hard-coded into duplicated sh/pwsh recipes

The concrete per-repo checklists live in each superproject's own issue
tracker, because those repos are private.

## Generic adoption checklist

1. `audit --fetch` and save the report. Resolve every `gitlink-unreachable`
   error first by pushing the child commit or moving the pointer. A fresh
   clone fails on these.
2. Agree policies with the owner:
   - children the outer repo should follow → `track`
   - deployed or known-good baselines → `pin`, with `branch` set to the
     baseline line
   - references and rarely used children → `lazy`
3. `adopt --dry-run --policy-default pin --set <child>=track:pr ...`, review,
   then `adopt` (`--with-ci` once a `SUBMODULE_TOKEN` exists for private
   children). Install the skill globally first (`npx skills add ...`), because
   the recipes reference it instead of copying the CLI.
4. Replace hand-written submodule recipes with the `sub-*` block. Keep
   repo-specific recipes (deploy, build), but make them read paths from the CLI
   rather than hard-coding them.
5. Retire bespoke init scripts that the policy keys and `init --tier` now cover.
6. Move ongoing child feature work into `.worktrees/<child>/<branch>`, or

# CLAUDE.md

## Working with td

td keeps task context durable across sessions. In a new context, run `td usage --new-session -q` to see current work.

Use your judgment about how much tracking a task needs. For substantive work: `td start <id>`, record progress with `td log`, hand off with `td handoff <id>`, then `td review <id>`.

Closing needs a review. Say who did it (default trusted mode; delegated/strict allow only the first):

- independent session: `td approve <id> --reason "..."`
- a sub-agent: `td approve <id> --reviewed-by "<who>"`
- you: `td approve <id> --self-review --reason "..."`

Prefer a reviewer with its own `TD_CONTEXT_ID`; never name one who did not review.

Run `td usage` or `td <command> --help`.

<!-- td-agent-instructions:end -->

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. Contains local canonical skills (`skills/local/`), first-party project skills (`skills/owned/`), and cherry-picked third-party skills (`skills/vendor/`). Owned and vendor copies sync from their canonical upstream repos.

The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`owned/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).

## Commands

```bash
# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
make sync

# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
make sync-check

# Validate and render the repo backlog board
make kanban

# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
make marketplace

# Exercise native Claude Code + Codex marketplace add/list/install in isolated state.
make native-marketplace-smoke

# YAML-parse every skills/**/SKILL.md frontmatter. A file that fails to parse
# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
make lint-frontmatter

# All portable publish gates at once (frontmatter + marketplace + TODO format).
# CI additionally runs `make native-marketplace-smoke` with pinned CLIs.
make validate

# Install scripts/git-hooks/pre-push so `git push` runs `make validate` first.
make install-hooks

# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs

# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
  --title "Title" --description "Description"

# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines

# Start a TODO item as a td issue (td bridge; no-op without td, TODO.md unchanged)
./scripts/start-todo.sh --title "<substring>"

# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"

# Create a new local skill
cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]

# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
uv sync --extra docs
make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
make docs-build     # produces ./site/
```

## Source categories and upstream sync

- `skills/local/` — canonical skills authored in this repository.
- `skills/owned/` — first-party skills maintained in another repository owned by the maintainer. Edit the source project, then sync its distribution copy here.
- `skills/vendor/` — third-party upstream skills; preserve upstream content.

`vendor.yaml` remains the shared sync manifest. `collection: owned` selects
`skills/owned/`; an omitted collection defaults to `vendor`. Both support `series`,
`license_path`, `frozen`, and upstream commit tracking. Add published owned sources
with `scripts/add-vendor.sh --owned <owner/repo/path>`. A cross-repository symlink
cannot serve as a distributable copy.

An unpublished owned skill may use `pending_upstream: true`. Its bootstrap mirror
contains real files but claims no remote SHA; routine sync/check preserves it.
After publishing the canonical source, run `scripts/sync-vendor.sh --activate <name>`.
Only a successful sync clears pending. See [owned workflow](docs/workflows/adding-owned-skills.md).

## Vendor System (also used for owned sources)

- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir

Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.

`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.

Active series in this repo:
- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)

### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed

Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:

- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
  `skills@1.5.24` writes `skills-lock.json`, but a renamed skill is still a
  different install ID; review the lock and explicitly reinstall the new name.
- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.

Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.

## Marketplace Catalog

`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
for the full mechanism.

When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>`, `./owned/<name>`, or
`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).

**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
within-group caveat in
[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).

## SKILL.md Format

Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.

## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)

The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.

`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.

To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:

```bash
# Skip the symlinks at creation time
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>

# …or remove them afterward
rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
```

## Project Memory Workflow

<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance -->
### Issue-driven workflow (GitHub)

This project uses GitHub Issues as the canonical shared backlog, not as a
mandatory record of every change. The `forge-native-dev` skill provides the
scripts below; apply its scope gate before publishing any new record.

| Information | Lives in | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Bounded experiment, small fix, same-session evaluation | Conversation + diff; optional local note | Avoid unnecessary tracking overhead |
| Durable actionable backlog, blockers, shared ownership | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/issues) | Searchable, assignable, cross-linkable |
| Open questions needing ongoing asynchronous input | [Discussions](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/discussions) | Shared deliberation, not a research archive |
| Research docs, trade-off analysis | `backlog/` | Durable, diffable; no Discussion required |
| Past traps, debugging knowledge | `pitfalls/` | Grep-able by symptom, portable |
| Backlog visualization | [Project board](https://github.com/users/daviddwlee84/projects/11) | Built-in to the forge |
| Historical record | `TODO.md` `## Done` section | In git |

**Right-size tracking.** Default to local work for bounded experiments and
small changes. Create an external record only when explicitly requested or when
outstanding work needs durable backlog/ownership/dependency tracking or shared
input. Another session or a long research document alone does not require it;
use td/local notes for execution context where sufficient.

Reuse an existing relevant Issue/Discussion before creating one. "Research",
"maybe later", and "先記下來" do not automatically mean publish a Discussion or
Issue. Do not create both merely because a task includes research and code, or
retrospectively open tickets for completed small work. Local branches/worktrees
and directly requested PRs do not require a synthetic Issue number.

**Tracked work lifecycle (when an Issue is warranted):**
1. Start: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh start <issue-number>`
2. Work in the worktree, commit conventionally
3. Finish: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh finish <issue-number>`
4. After merge: `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-cleanup.sh`

**Check for work:** `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-issue.sh list --assignee @me`

**Dashboard:** `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-status.sh`

**PRs are review gates.** Link the existing Issue when there is one; a bounded
change may go directly to a requested PR without a prerequisite ticket. Keep
normal review/publication permissions. Default merge strategy: **squash and merge**.
<!-- forge-native-dev:guidance (end) -->

### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`

`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
own conventions). It has four subareas:

- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
  status / license / last_verified`).

Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |

Status changes trigger existing scripts:
`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).

Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.

### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`

When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:

1. The verbatim symptom or error text
2. The root cause
3. The workaround
4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it

Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
the explanation they do not know yet.

40	BUMP_MODES = ("pr", "direct", "manual")
41	WORKTREE_DIR = ".worktrees"
42	
43	AGENTS_BEGIN = "<!-- superproject-workspace:agent-guidance -->"
44	AGENTS_END = "<!-- superproject-workspace:agent-guidance --> (end)"
45	JUST_BEGIN = "# superproject-workspace:begin"
46	JUST_END = "# superproject-workspace:end"
47	VENDORED_CLI = "scripts/superproject.py"
48	
49	SKILL_ASSETS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "assets"
50	GIT_ENV = {**os.environ, "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0", "LC_ALL": "C"}
51	
52	
53	class Refused(Exception):
54	    """A safety rule declined the operation; the message says why."""
55	
56	
57	class UsageError(Exception):
58	    pass

61	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- git helpers
62	
63	def git(*args: str, cwd: Path, check: bool = True, input: str | None = None) -> str:
64	    p = subprocess.run(
65	        ["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=GIT_ENV, input=input
66	    )
67	    if check and p.returncode != 0:
68	        raise Refused(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed in {cwd}: {p.stderr.strip()}")
69	    return p.stdout.rstrip("\n")
70	
71	
72	def git_rc(*args: str, cwd: Path) -> int:
73	    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, env=GIT_ENV).returncode
74	
75	
76	def is_ancestor(repo: Path, a: str, b: str) -> bool | None:
77	    """True/False, or None when either object is unknown locally."""
78	    rc = git_rc("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", a, b, cwd=repo)
79	    return {0: True, 1: False}.get(rc)
80	
81	
82	def has_commit(repo: Path, sha: str) -> bool:
83	    return git_rc("cat-file", "-e", f"{sha}^{{commit}}", cwd=repo) == 0
84	
85	
86	def ref_exists(repo: Path, ref: str) -> bool:
87	    return git_rc("show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", ref, cwd=repo) == 0
88	
89	
90	def remote_refs_containing(repo: Path, sha: str) -> list[str]:
91	    out = git("for-each-ref", "--contains", sha, "--format=%(refname:short)", "refs/remotes/origin",
92	              cwd=repo, check=False)
93	    return [r for r in out.splitlines() if r and r != "origin/HEAD"]
94	
95	
96	def tracked_dirty(repo: Path) -> int:
97	    out = git("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no", cwd=repo, check=False)
98	    return len([line for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()])
99	
100	
101	def short(sha: str | None) -> str:
102	    return sha[:7] if sha else "-"
103	
104	
105	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- model
106	
107	@dataclass
108	class Sub:
109	    name: str
110	    path: str
111	    url: str | None
112	    branch: str | None
113	    policy: str | None
114	    bump: str | None
115	    tier: str | None
116	    update: str | None
117	
118	    @property
119	    def eff_policy(self) -> str:
120	        # An undeclared policy is treated as pin: never moved implicitly.
121	        return self.policy if self.policy in POLICIES else "pin"
122	
123	    @property
124	    def eff_bump(self) -> str:
125	        if self.eff_policy != "track":
126	            return "manual"
127	        return self.bump if self.bump in BUMP_MODES else "manual"
128	
129	    def eff_branch(self, root: Path) -> str:
130	        if self.branch == ".":
131	            return git("symbolic-ref", "-q", "--short", "HEAD", cwd=root, check=False) or "main"
132	        if self.branch:
133	            return self.branch
134	        # Undeclared: follow the child's remote default (main, master, ...).
135	        head = git("symbolic-ref", "-q", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD", cwd=root / self.path, check=False)
136	        return head.removeprefix("origin/") if head.startswith("origin/") else "main"
137	
138	
139	def find_root(explicit: str | None) -> Path:
140	    if explicit:
141	        root = Path(explicit).resolve()
142	        if not (root / ".gitmodules").exists():
143	            raise UsageError(f"{root} has no .gitmodules")
144	        return root
145	    cwd = Path.cwd()
146	    for cand in (
147	        git("rev-parse", "--show-superproject-working-tree", cwd=cwd, check=False),
148	        git("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel", cwd=cwd, check=False),
149	    ):
150	        if cand and (Path(cand) / ".gitmodules").exists():
151	            return Path(cand).resolve()
152	    # Inside a child worktree under .worktrees/: walk up to the superproject.
153	    for base in [cwd, *cwd.parents]:
154	        if (base / ".gitmodules").exists() and (base / ".git").exists():
155	            return base.resolve()
156	    raise UsageError("not inside a superproject (no .gitmodules found); pass --root")
157	
158	
159	def load_subs(root: Path) -> list[Sub]:
160	    if not (root / ".gitmodules").exists():
161	        return []
162	    out = subprocess.run(
163	        ["git", "config", "-z", "-f", ".gitmodules", "--get-regexp", r"^submodule\."],
164	        cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, env=GIT_ENV,
165	    ).stdout
166	    entries: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
167	    for rec in out.split("\0"):
168	        if not rec:
169	            continue
170	        key, _, value = rec.partition("\n")
171	        name, _, var = key[len("submodule."):].rpartition(".")
172	        entries.setdefault(name, {})[var.lower()] = value
173	    return [
174	        Sub(
175	            name=name, path=e["path"].rstrip("/"), url=e.get("url"), branch=e.get("branch"),
176	            policy=e.get("x-policy"), bump=e.get("x-bump"), tier=e.get("x-tier"),
177	            update=e.get("update"),
178	        )
179	        for name, e in entries.items()
180	        if "path" in e
181	    ]
182	
183	
184	def gitlink(root: Path, path: str, tree: str = "HEAD") -> str | None:
185	    out = git("ls-tree", tree, "--", path, cwd=root, check=False)
186	    m = re.match(r"160000 commit ([0-9a-f]+)\t", out)
187	    return m.group(1) if m else None
188	
189	
190	def index_gitlink(root: Path, path: str) -> str | None:
191	    out = git("ls-files", "-s", "--", path, cwd=root, check=False)
192	    m = re.match(r"160000 ([0-9a-f]+) 0\t", out)
193	    return m.group(1) if m else None
194	
195	
196	def is_initialized(root: Path, sub: Sub) -> bool:
197	    p = root / sub.path
198	    if not (p / ".git").exists():
199	        return False
200	    top = git("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel", cwd=p, check=False)
201	    return bool(top) and Path(top).resolve() == p.resolve()
202	
203	
204	def fetch(repo: Path) -> str | None:
205	    p = subprocess.run(
206	        ["git", "fetch", "--prune", "--quiet", "origin"],
207	        cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, env=GIT_ENV,
208	    )
209	    return None if p.returncode == 0 else p.stderr.strip() or "fetch failed"
210	
211	
212	def resolve(subs: list[Sub], ident: str) -> Sub:
213	    ident = ident.rstrip("/")
214	    hits = [s for s in subs if ident in (s.name, s.path)]
215	    if not hits:
216	        hits = [s for s in subs if Path(s.path).name == ident]
217	    if len(hits) != 1:
218	        known = ", ".join(s.name for s in subs)
219	        raise UsageError(f"{'ambiguous' if hits else 'unknown'} submodule {ident!r} (known: {known})")
220	    return hits[0]
221	
222	
223	def select(subs: list[Sub], args: argparse.Namespace, default) -> list[Sub]:
224	    names = getattr(args, "names", None) or []
225	    if names:
226	        chosen = [resolve(subs, n) for n in names]
227	    elif any(getattr(args, k, None) for k in ("tier", "policy")):
228	        chosen = list(subs)
229	    else:
230	        chosen = [s for s in subs if default(s)]
231	    if getattr(args, "tier", None):
232	        chosen = [s for s in chosen if s.tier == args.tier]
233	    if getattr(args, "policy", None):
234	        chosen = [s for s in chosen if s.eff_policy == args.policy]
235	    if getattr(args, "mode", None):
236	        chosen = [s for s in chosen if s.eff_bump == args.mode]
237	    return chosen
238	
239	
240	def sub_state(root: Path, sub: Sub, *, do_fetch: bool = False) -> dict:
241	    p = root / sub.path
242	    branch = sub.eff_branch(root)
243	    st: dict = {
244	        "name": sub.name, "path": sub.path, "policy": sub.policy, "bump": sub.eff_bump,
245	        "tier": sub.tier, "branch": branch, "recorded": gitlink(root, sub.path),
246	        "staged": None, "initialized": is_initialized(root, sub), "warnings": [],
247	    }
248	    staged = index_gitlink(root, sub.path)
249	    if staged and staged != st["recorded"]:
250	        st["staged"] = staged
251	    if not st["initialized"]:
252	        return st
253	    if do_fetch and (err := fetch(p)):
254	        st["warnings"].append(f"fetch failed: {err}")
255	    head = git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=p, check=False) or None
256	    upstream = f"refs/remotes/origin/{branch}"
257	    st.update(
258	        head=head,
259	        checkout_branch=git("symbolic-ref", "-q", "--short", "HEAD", cwd=p, check=False) or None,
260	        dirty=tracked_dirty(p),
261	        drift=bool(head and st["recorded"] and head != st["recorded"]),
262	        upstream_exists=ref_exists(p, upstream),
263	        lag=None, unpushed=None, recorded_reachable=None, recorded_on_remote=None, head_reachable=None,
264	        worktrees=list_child_worktrees(root, sub),
265	    )
266	    if not st["upstream_exists"]:
267	        st["warnings"].append(f"origin/{branch} missing locally (fetch, or fix `branch`)")
268	        return st
269	    rec = st["recorded"]
270	    if rec and has_commit(p, rec):
271	        left, right = git("rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", f"{rec}...{upstream}", cwd=p).split()
272	        st.update(unpushed=int(left), lag=int(right), recorded_reachable=int(left) == 0)
273	        st["recorded_on_remote"] = st["recorded_reachable"] or bool(remote_refs_containing(p, rec))
274	    elif rec:
275	        st["warnings"].append(f"recorded commit {short(rec)} not present locally (fetch?)")
276	    if head:
277	        st["head_reachable"] = is_ancestor(p, head, upstream)
278	    return st
279	
280	
281	def list_child_worktrees(root: Path, sub: Sub) -> list[dict]:
282	    p = root / sub.path
283	    base = (root / WORKTREE_DIR).resolve()
284	    out = git("worktree", "list", "--porcelain", cwd=p, check=False)
285	    found = []
286	    for block in out.split("\n\n"):
287	        info: dict = {}
288	        for line in block.splitlines():
289	            k, _, v = line.partition(" ")
290	            info[k] = v or True
291	        wt = info.get("worktree")
292	        if not isinstance(wt, str) or not Path(wt).resolve().is_relative_to(base):
293	            continue
294	        br = info.get("branch")
295	        found.append({
296	            "path": str(Path(wt).resolve().relative_to(root.resolve())),
297	            "branch": br.removeprefix("refs/heads/") if isinstance(br, str) else None,
298	            "head": info.get("HEAD"),
299	            "prunable": "prunable" in info,
300	        })
301	    branch = sub.eff_branch(root)
302	    for wt in found:
303	        wt["merged"] = bool(
304	            wt["head"] and wt["branch"] != branch
305	            and is_ancestor(p, wt["head"], f"refs/remotes/origin/{branch}")
306	        )
307	        if not wt["prunable"] and (root / wt["path"]).exists():
308	            wt["dirty"] = tracked_dirty(root / wt["path"])
309	    return found
310	
311	
312	def emit(args: argparse.Namespace, data, text: str) -> None:
313	    if args.json:
314	        print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
315	    else:
316	        print(text)
317	
318	
319	def table(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:
320	    if not rows:
321	        return ""
322	    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in rows) for i in range(len(rows[0]))]
323	    return "\n".join("  ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(r, widths)).rstrip() for r in rows)
324	
325	
326	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- status
327	
328	def describe(st: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
329	    if not st["initialized"]:
330	        return "uninit", ""
331	    bits = []
332	    if st["checkout_branch"]:
333	        bits.append(f"on {st['checkout_branch']}")
334	    else:
335	        bits.append("detached")
336	    if st["dirty"]:
337	        bits.append(f"dirty({st['dirty']})")
338	    if st["drift"]:
339	        bits.append(f"head {short(st['head'])} != gitlink")
340	    if st["staged"]:
341	        bits.append(f"staged {short(st['staged'])}")
342	    if st["recorded_on_remote"] is False:
343	        bits.append("gitlink NOT on any origin branch")
344	    elif st["recorded_reachable"] is False:
345	        bits.append(f"gitlink off origin/{st['branch']} (on another origin branch)")
346	    if st["worktrees"]:
347	        bits.append(f"{len(st['worktrees'])} worktree(s)")
348	    bits += st["warnings"]
349	    lag = "-" if st["lag"] is None else str(st["lag"])
350	    return lag, "; ".join(bits)
351	
352	
353	def cmd_status(root: Path, subs: list[Sub], args) -> int:
354	    chosen = select(subs, args, lambda s: True)
355	    states = [sub_state(root, s, do_fetch=args.fetch) for s in chosen]
356	    rows = [["NAME", "POLICY", "BUMP", "TIER", "GITLINK", "LAG", "STATE"]]
357	    for st in states:
358	        lag, note = describe(st)
359	        rows.append([
360	            st["name"] if st["name"] == st["path"] else f"{st['name']} ({st['path']})",
361	            st["policy"] or "(unset)", st["bump"], st["tier"] or "-",
362	            short(st["recorded"]), lag, note,
363	        ])
364	    hint = "" if args.fetch else "\n(lag uses local remote refs; add --fetch for current numbers)"
365	    emit(args, {"root": str(root), "cli_version": __version__, "submodules": states}, table(rows) + hint)
366	    return 0
367	
368	
369	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- init
370	
371	def cmd_init(root: Path, subs: list[Sub], args) -> int:
372	    chosen = select(subs, args, lambda s: args.all or s.eff_policy != "lazy")
373	    results = []
374	    for s in chosen:
375	        if is_initialized(root, s):
376	            results.append({"name": s.name, "action": "skipped",
377	                            "reason": "already initialized; init never moves a checkout (use pull/bump)"})
378	            continue
379	        cmd = ["submodule", "update", "--init"]
380	        if s.eff_policy == "lazy" or s.update == "none":
381	            cmd.append("--checkout")  # override update=none for an explicit request
382	        if args.recursive:
383	            cmd.append("--recursive")
384	        cmd += ["--", s.path]
385	        if not args.dry_run:
386	            git("submodule", "sync", "--", s.path, cwd=root)
387	            git(*cmd, cwd=root)
388	        results.append({"name": s.name, "action": "would-init" if args.dry_run else "initialized",
389	                        "command": "git " + " ".join(cmd)})
390	    text = "\n".join(f"{r['action']:12} {r['name']}" + (f"  ({r['reason']})" if "reason" in r else "")
391	                     for r in results) or "nothing selected"
392	    emit(args, {"results": results}, text)
393	    return 0
394	
395	
396	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- pull
397	
398	def pull_one(root: Path, s: Sub, args) -> dict:
399	    p = root / s.path
400	    branch = s.eff_branch(root)
401	    up = f"origin/{branch}"
402	    res = {"name": s.name, "branch": branch}
403	    if s.eff_policy != "track" and not args.force:
404	        raise Refused(f"policy is {s.policy or 'unset (treated as pin)'}; pass --force to move it")
405	    if not is_initialized(root, s):
406	        raise Refused("not initialized; run `init` first")
407	    if not args.no_fetch and (err := fetch(p)):
408	        raise Refused(f"fetch failed: {err}")
409	    if not ref_exists(p, f"refs/remotes/{up}"):
410	        raise Refused(f"{up} does not exist")
411	    if tracked_dirty(p):
412	        raise Refused("uncommitted changes in the checkout")
413	    cur = git("symbolic-ref", "-q", "--short", "HEAD", cwd=p, check=False)
414	    head = git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=p)
415	    if cur and cur != branch:
416	        raise Refused(f"checkout is on branch {cur!r}; develop in `worktree add`, keep the checkout on {branch}")
417	    if not cur and not is_ancestor(p, head, up):
418	        raise Refused(f"detached commit {short(head)} is not on {up}; save it on a branch first")
419	    if ref_exists(p, f"refs/heads/{branch}"):
420	        local = git("rev-parse", branch, cwd=p)
421	        behind, ahead = is_ancestor(p, local, up), is_ancestor(p, up, local)
422	        if not behind and not ahead:
423	            raise Refused(f"local {branch} has diverged from {up}; resolve manually")
424	        if not behind:
425	            res["warning"] = f"local {branch} has unpushed commits; bump will refuse until pushed"
426	    target = git("rev-parse", up, cwd=p)
427	    res.update({"from": head, "to": target})
428	    if head == target and cur == branch:
429	        res["action"] = "up-to-date"
430	        return res
431	    if args.dry_run:
432	        res["action"] = "would-update"
433	        return res
434	    if not cur:
435	        if ref_exists(p, f"refs/heads/{branch}"):
436	            git("switch", branch, cwd=p)
437	        else:
438	            git("switch", "--track", "-c", branch, up, cwd=p)
439	    git("merge", "--ff-only", up, cwd=p)
440	    res["to"] = git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=p)
441	    res["action"] = "updated"
442	    return res
443	
444	
445	def cmd_pull(root: Path, subs: list[Sub], args) -> int:
446	    chosen = select(subs, args, lambda s: s.eff_policy == "track" and is_initialized(root, s))
447	    results, failed = [], False
448	    for s in chosen:
449	        try:
450	            results.append(pull_one(root, s, args))
451	        except Refused as e:
452	            failed = True
453	            results.append({"name": s.name, "action": "refused", "reason": str(e)})
454	    lines = []
455	    for r in results:
456	        detail = r.get("reason") or f"{short(r.get('from'))} -> {short(r.get('to'))}"
457	        lines.append(f"{r['action']:12} {r['name']}  {detail}" + (f"  [{r['warning']}]" if r.get("warning") else ""))
458	    if any(r["action"] == "updated" for r in results):
459	        lines.append("checkouts moved; record them with `bump` (gitlinks are unchanged until then)")
460	    emit(args, {"results": results}, "\n".join(lines) or "nothing selected")
461	    return 1 if failed else 0
462	
463	
464	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- preflight / bump
465	
466	def check_commit(root: Path, s: Sub, sha: str, *, require_clean: bool) -> list[str]:
467	    """Problems that make `sha` unsafe to record as this submodule's gitlink."""
468	    p = root / s.path
469	    branch = s.eff_branch(root)
470	    if not is_initialized(root, s):
471	        return ["not initialized; cannot verify the commit"]
472	    problems = []
473	    if require_clean and tracked_dirty(p):
474	        problems.append("uncommitted changes in the checkout")
475	    if not has_commit(p, sha):
476	        return problems + [f"{short(sha)} does not exist in the child repo"]
477	    if s.eff_policy != "track":
478	        # A pin may sit on any pushed branch (e.g. a production baseline); it must only be recoverable.
479	        if not remote_refs_containing(p, sha):
480	            problems.append(f"{short(sha)} is not reachable from any origin branch; push the child commit (then fetch)")
481	        return problems
482	    if not ref_exists(p, f"refs/remotes/origin/{branch}"):
483	        return problems + [f"origin/{branch} missing; cannot prove {short(sha)} is pushed"]
484	    if not is_ancestor(p, sha, f"origin/{branch}"):
485	        problems.append(f"{short(sha)} is not reachable from origin/{branch}; push the child commit (then fetch)")
486	    return problems
487	
488	
489	def cmd_preflight(root: Path, subs: list[Sub], args) -> int:
490	    by_path = {s.path: s for s in subs}
491	    findings = []
492	    if git("ls-files", "-u", cwd=root):
493	        for line in git("ls-files", "-u", cwd=root).splitlines():
494	            if line.startswith("160000"):
495	                findings.append({"path": line.split("\t", 1)[1], "level": "error", "message": "unmerged gitlink"})
496	    raw = git("diff", "--cached", "--raw", "--no-abbrev", cwd=root)
497	    staged = []
498	    for line in raw.splitlines():
499	        m = re.match(r":\d+ (\d+) [0-9a-f]+ ([0-9a-f]+) \w+\t(.+)", line)
500	        if m and m.group(1) == "160000":
501	            staged.append((m.group(3), m.group(2)))
502	    for path, sha in staged:
503	        s = by_path.get(path)
504	        if not s:
505	            findings.append({"path": path, "level": "error", "message": "gitlink not declared in .gitmodules"})
506	            continue
507	        if args.fetch and is_initialized(root, s):
508	            fetch(root / s.path)
509	        for msg in check_commit(root, s, sha, require_clean=False):
510	            findings.append({"path": path, "level": "error", "message": msg})
511	        if is_initialized(root, s):
512	            p = root / s.path
513	            if tracked_dirty(p):
514	                findings.append({"path": path, "level": "warn", "message": "checkout has uncommitted changes"})
515	            if git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=p, check=False) != sha:
516	                findings.append({"path": path, "level": "warn", "message": "checkout HEAD differs from the staged gitlink"})
517	    errors = [f for f in findings if f["level"] == "error"]
518	    text = "\n".join(f"{f['level']:5} {f['path']}: {f['message']}" for f in findings)
519	    if not staged:
520	        text = text or "No staged gitlink changes."
521	    elif not findings:
522	        text = f"ok: {len(staged)} staged gitlink(s) are pushed and reachable"
523	    emit(args, {"staged": [{"path": p, "sha": s} for p, s in staged], "findings": findings, "ok": not errors}, text)
524	    return 1 if errors else 0
525	
526	
527	def cmd_bump(root: Path, subs: list[Sub], args) -> int:
528	    if not args.names and not args.all_track:
529	        raise UsageError("name submodules to bump, or pass --all-track")
530	    chosen = select(subs, args, lambda s: args.all_track and s.eff_policy == "track" and is_initialized(root, s))
531	    planned, refused, results = [], [], []
532	    for s in chosen:
533	        p = root / s.path
534	        res = {"name": s.name, "path": s.path, "policy": s.policy}
535	        try:
536	            if s.eff_policy != "track" and not args.reason:
537	                raise Refused(f"policy is {s.policy or 'unset (treated as pin)'}; pass --reason to move it")
538	            if not is_initialized(root, s):
539	                raise Refused("not initialized")
540	            if not args.no_fetch and (err := fetch(p)):
541	                raise Refused(f"fetch failed: {err}")
542	            head = git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=p)
543	            old = gitlink(root, s.path)
544	            res.update({"from": old, "to": head})
545	            if head == old and index_gitlink(root, s.path) == old:
546	                res["action"] = "up-to-date"
547	                results.append(res)
548	                continue
549	            if problems := check_commit(root, s, head, require_clean=True):
550	                raise Refused("; ".join(problems))
551	            if old and has_commit(p, old):
552	                res["commits"] = int(git("rev-list", "--count", f"{old}..{head}", cwd=p))
553	            res["action"] = "would-bump" if args.dry_run else "staged"
554	            planned.append((s, res))
555	        except Refused as e:
556	            res.update(action="refused", reason=str(e))
557	            refused.append(res)
558	        results.append(res)
559	
560	    commit_sha = None
561	    if refused and not args.partial:
562	        for _, res in planned:
563	            res["action"] = "aborted"
564	    elif planned and not args.dry_run:
565	        paths = [s.path for s, _ in planned]
566	        if args.commit:
567	            others = set(git("diff", "--cached", "--name-only", cwd=root).splitlines()) - set(paths)
568	            if others and not args.allow_other_staged:
569	                raise Refused(f"other staged changes would join the bump commit: {', '.join(sorted(others))}")
570	        git("add", "--", *paths, cwd=root)
571	        if args.commit:
572	            git("commit", "-F", "-", cwd=root, input=bump_message(root, planned, args))
573	            commit_sha = git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=root)
574	            for _, res in planned:
575	                res["action"] = "committed"
576	
577	    lines = []
578	    for r in results:
579	        if r["action"] == "refused":
580	            lines.append(f"refused      {r['name']}  {r['reason']}")
581	        else:
582	            n = f" (+{r['commits']})" if r.get("commits") is not None else ""
583	            lines.append(f"{r['action']:12} {r['name']}  {short(r.get('from'))} -> {short(r.get('to'))}{n}")
584	    if refused and not args.partial:
585	        lines.append("aborted: one cross-repo change gets one outer commit; fix the refusals or pass --partial")
586	    if commit_sha:
587	        lines.append(f"committed {short(commit_sha)}")
588	    elif planned and not args.dry_run and not (refused and not args.partial):
589	        lines.append("gitlinks staged; review with `git diff --cached --submodule=log`, then commit (or rerun with --commit)")
590	    emit(args, {"results": results, "commit": commit_sha}, "\n".join(lines) or "nothing selected")
591	    return 1 if refused else 0
592	
593	
594	def bump_message(root: Path, planned: list[tuple[Sub, dict]], args) -> str:
595	    names = [s.name for s, _ in planned]
596	    subject = args.subject or (
597	        f"chore(submodules): bump {', '.join(names)}" if len(names) <= 3
598	        else f"chore(submodules): bump {len(names)} submodules"
599	    )
600	    body = []
601	    for s, r in planned:
602	        n = f" (+{r['commits']})" if r.get("commits") is not None else ""
603	        body.append(f"- {s.name}: {short(r['from'])}..{short(r['to'])}{n} [{s.policy or 'unset'}]")
604	    if args.reason:
605	        body += ["", f"Reason: {args.reason}"]
606	    log = git("diff", "--cached", "--submodule=log", "--", *[s.path for s, _ in planned], cwd=root)
607	    if log:
608	        body += ["", log]
609	    return subject + "\n\n" + "\n".join(body) + "\n"
610

612	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- worktrees
613	
614	def wt_path(root: Path, s: Sub, branch: str) -> Path:
615	    return root / WORKTREE_DIR / s.path / branch.replace("/", "-")
616	
617	
618	def ensure_gitignore(root: Path, dry_run: bool) -> bool:
619	    """Return True when .gitignore needs (or got) the .worktrees/ entry."""
620	    if git_rc("check-ignore", "-q", "--no-index", f"{WORKTREE_DIR}/probe", cwd=root) == 0:
621	        return False
622	    if not dry_run:
623	        gi = root / ".gitignore"
624	        text = gi.read_text() if gi.exists() else ""
625	        sep = "" if not text or text.endswith("\n") else "\n"
626	        gi.write_text(f"{text}{sep}# superproject-workspace: child worktrees\n{WORKTREE_DIR}/\n")
627	    return True
628	
629	
630	def cmd_worktree(root: Path, subs: list[Sub], args) -> int:
631	    if args.wt_cmd == "list":
632	        chosen = [s for s in subs if is_initialized(root, s)]
633	        items = [dict(wt, submodule=s.name) for s in chosen for wt in list_child_worktrees(root, s)]
634	        rows = [["SUBMODULE", "BRANCH", "PATH", "STATE"]]
635	        for wt in items:
636	            state = ["prunable"] if wt["prunable"] else []
637	            if wt.get("dirty"):
638	                state.append(f"dirty({wt['dirty']})")
639	            if wt["merged"]:
640	                state.append("merged: safe to remove")
641	            rows.append([wt["submodule"], wt["branch"] or "(detached)", wt["path"], ", ".join(state)])
642	        emit(args, {"worktrees": items}, table(rows) if items else "no child worktrees")
643	        return 0
644	
645	    s = resolve(subs, args.submodule)
646	    p = root / s.path
647	    if not is_initialized(root, s):
648	        raise Refused(f"{s.name} is not initialized; run `init {s.name}` first")
649	    target = wt_path(root, s, args.branch)
650	    rel = str(target.relative_to(root))
651	
652	    if args.wt_cmd == "remove":
653	        cmd = ["worktree", "remove", *(["--force"] if args.force else []), str(target)]
654	        if not args.dry_run:
655	            git(*cmd, cwd=p)
656	            git("worktree", "prune", cwd=p)
657	            if args.delete_branch:
658	                git("branch", "-D" if args.force else "-d", args.branch, cwd=p)
659	        emit(args, {"removed": rel, "dry_run": args.dry_run}, f"{'would remove' if args.dry_run else 'removed'} {rel}")
660	        return 0
661	
662	    # add
663	    if target.exists():
664	        raise Refused(f"{rel} already exists")
665	    if not args.no_fetch:
666	        fetch(p)
667	    branch = s.eff_branch(root)
668	    if ref_exists(p, f"refs/heads/{args.branch}"):
669	        cmd, base = ["worktree", "add", str(target), args.branch], args.branch
670	    elif ref_exists(p, f"refs/remotes/origin/{args.branch}"):
671	        base = f"origin/{args.branch}"
672	        cmd = ["worktree", "add", "--track", "-b", args.branch, str(target), base]
673	    else:
674	        # Pinned children branch from the recorded baseline, not from upstream tip.
675	        base = args.base or (f"origin/{branch}" if s.eff_policy == "track" else gitlink(root, s.path))
676	        cmd = ["worktree", "add", "-b", args.branch, str(target), base]
677	    gi = ensure_gitignore(root, args.dry_run)
678	    if not args.dry_run:
679	        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
680	        git(*cmd, cwd=p)
681	    data = {"path": rel, "branch": args.branch, "base": base, "gitignore_updated": gi, "dry_run": args.dry_run}
682	    emit(args, data, f"{'would create' if args.dry_run else 'created'} {rel} on {args.branch} from {base}"
683	         + ("\nadded .worktrees/ to .gitignore" if gi else ""))
684	    return 0
685

689	def find_agents_file(root: Path) -> Path | None:
690	    for name in ("AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md"):
691	        if (root / name).exists():
692	            return root / name
693	    return None
694	
695	
696	def find_justfile(root: Path) -> Path | None:
697	    for name in ("justfile", "Justfile", ".justfile"):
698	        if (root / name).exists():
699	            return root / name
700	    return None
