702	
703	def cmd_audit(root: Path, subs: list[Sub], args) -> int:
704	    f: list[dict] = []
705	
706	    def add(level: str, code: str, subject: str, message: str, fix: str = "") -> None:
707	        f.append({"level": level, "code": code, "subject": subject, "message": message, "fix": fix})
708	
709	    if not subs:
710	        add("error", "no-submodules", ".gitmodules", "no submodules declared")
711	    for s in subs:
712	        if s.policy is None:
713	            add("warn", "policy-missing", s.name, "no x-policy; treated as pin",
714	                f"git config -f .gitmodules submodule.{s.name}.x-policy track|pin|lazy")
715	        elif s.policy not in POLICIES:
716	            add("error", "policy-invalid", s.name, f"x-policy={s.policy!r} (expected {'|'.join(POLICIES)})")
717	        if s.bump and s.bump not in BUMP_MODES:
718	            add("error", "bump-invalid", s.name, f"x-bump={s.bump!r} (expected {'|'.join(BUMP_MODES)})")
719	        if s.bump in ("pr", "direct") and s.eff_policy != "track":
720	            add("warn", "bump-ignored", s.name, f"x-bump={s.bump} has no effect on a {s.eff_policy} submodule")
721	        if s.eff_policy == "track" and not s.branch:
722	            add("warn", "branch-missing", s.name, "track without `branch`; assuming main",
723	                f"git config -f .gitmodules submodule.{s.name}.branch main")
724	        if s.policy == "lazy" and s.update != "none":
725	            add("warn", "lazy-update", s.name, "lazy without `update = none`; plain `git submodule update --init` will fetch it",
726	                f"git config -f .gitmodules submodule.{s.name}.update none")
727	        if s.policy in ("track", "pin") and s.update == "none":
728	            add("warn", "update-none", s.name, f"{s.policy} child has update=none; plain git will never check it out")
729	        st = sub_state(root, s, do_fetch=args.fetch)
730	        if not st["initialized"]:
731	            if s.eff_policy != "lazy":
732	                add("warn", "uninitialized", s.name, f"{s.eff_policy} child is not initialized", f"init {s.name}")
733	            continue
734	        configured = git("config", "--get", f"submodule.{s.name}.url", cwd=root, check=False)
735	        if s.url and configured and configured != s.url and not s.url.startswith("."):
736	            add("warn", "url-unsynced", s.name, f".git/config url differs from .gitmodules ({configured})",
737	                f"git submodule sync -- {s.path}")
738	        if st["recorded_on_remote"] is False:
739	            add("error", "gitlink-unreachable", s.name,
740	                f"recorded {short(st['recorded'])} is on no origin branch; a fresh clone cannot check it out",
741	                "push the child commit, or move the pointer to a pushed commit")
742	        elif st["recorded_reachable"] is False:
743	            add("warn" if s.eff_policy == "track" else "info", "gitlink-off-branch", s.name,
744	                f"recorded {short(st['recorded'])} is pushed but not on origin/{st['branch']}",
745	                "merge the child branch, or set `branch` to the baseline it follows")
746	        if st["drift"]:
747	            add("info", "checkout-drift", s.name, f"checkout at {short(st['head'])}, gitlink at {short(st['recorded'])}",
748	                f"bump {s.name} to record it, or `git submodule update -- {s.path}` to discard")
749	        if st["dirty"]:
750	            add("info", "dirty", s.name, f"{st['dirty']} uncommitted change(s) in the checkout")
751	        if s.eff_policy == "track" and st["lag"]:
752	            add("warn", "behind", s.name, f"gitlink is {st['lag']} commit(s) behind origin/{st['branch']}",
753	                f"pull {s.name} && bump {s.name}")
754	        if s.eff_policy == "pin" and st["lag"]:
755	            add("info", "pin-behind", s.name, f"pinned {st['lag']} commit(s) behind origin/{st['branch']}")
756	        for w in st["worktrees"]:
757	            if w["prunable"]:
758	                add("info", "worktree-prunable", s.name, f"{w['path']} is gone", f"git -C {s.path} worktree prune")
759	            elif w["merged"]:
760	                add("info", "worktree-merged", s.name, f"{w['path']} ({w['branch']}) is merged",
761	                    f"worktree remove {s.name} {w['branch']} --delete-branch")
762	        for w in st["warnings"]:
763	            add("warn", "state", s.name, w)
764	
765	    agents = find_agents_file(root)
766	    if not agents or AGENTS_BEGIN not in agents.read_text():
767	        add("warn", "agents-block", agents.name if agents else "AGENTS.md",
768	            "no superproject-workspace guidance block for agents", "adopt")
769	    if git_rc("check-ignore", "-q", "--no-index", f"{WORKTREE_DIR}/probe", cwd=root) != 0:
770	        add("warn", "worktrees-not-ignored", ".gitignore", f"{WORKTREE_DIR}/ is not ignored", "adopt")
771	    jf = find_justfile(root)
772	    if jf:
773	        text = jf.read_text()
774	        hard = [s.path for s in subs if s.path in text]
775	        if JUST_BEGIN not in text and len(hard) >= 2:
776	            add("info", "justfile-hardcoded", jf.name,
777	                f"recipes hard-code {len(hard)} submodule paths; policy-driven recipes avoid per-child edits", "adopt")
778	    # The tool itself drifts too: compare managed blocks and any vendored copy to this CLI.
779	    if SKILL_ASSETS.exists():
780	        for target, begin, end, asset in (
781	            (agents, AGENTS_BEGIN, AGENTS_END, "agents-block.md.template"),
782	            (jf, JUST_BEGIN, JUST_END, "justfile.snippet"),
783	        ):
784	            block = extract_block(target.read_text(), begin, end) if target else None
785	            want = extract_block(render_asset(asset), begin, end)
786	            if block and want and block != want:
787	                add("warn", "managed-block-stale", target.name,
788	                    f"managed block differs from superproject-workspace {__version__}", "adopt")
789	    vendored = root / VENDORED_CLI
790	    if vendored.exists() and vendored.resolve() != Path(__file__).resolve() \
791	            and vendored.read_bytes() != Path(__file__).read_bytes():
792	        add("warn", "vendored-cli-stale", VENDORED_CLI,
793	            f"vendored CLI {cli_version(vendored)} differs from running CLI {__version__}",
794	            "adopt --vendor-cli to refresh, or delete it to use the installed skill")
795	    automated = [s for s in subs if s.eff_bump in ("pr", "direct")]
796	    wf_dir = root / ".github" / "workflows"
797	    has_ci = wf_dir.is_dir() and any("ci-plan" in w.read_text() or "superproject.py" in w.read_text()
798	                                      for w in wf_dir.glob("*.y*ml"))
799	    if automated and not has_ci:
800	        add("warn", "ci-missing", ".github/workflows",
801	            f"{len(automated)} child(ren) want automated bumps but no bump workflow exists", "adopt --with-ci")
802	    if git("config", "--get", "push.recurseSubmodules", cwd=root, check=False) not in ("check", "on-demand"):
803	        add("info", "push-check", "git config", "push.recurseSubmodules is not set; outer pushes can reference unpushed children",
804	            "git config push.recurseSubmodules check")
805	
806	    counts = {lvl: sum(1 for x in f if x["level"] == lvl) for lvl in ("error", "warn", "info")}
807	    order = {"error": 0, "warn": 1, "info": 2}
808	    lines = [f"{x['level']:5} {x['code']:22} {x['subject']}: {x['message']}" + (f"\n      fix: {x['fix']}" if x["fix"] else "")
809	             for x in sorted(f, key=lambda x: order[x["level"]])]
810	    lines.append(f"\n{counts['error']} error(s), {counts['warn']} warning(s), {counts['info']} info")
811	    emit(args, {"findings": f, "counts": counts}, "\n".join(lines))
812	    failed = counts["error"] or (args.strict and counts["warn"])
813	    return 1 if failed else 0
814

816	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- adopt
817	
818	def render_asset(name: str) -> str:
819	    path = SKILL_ASSETS / name
820	    if not path.exists():
821	        raise UsageError(f"asset {name} not found; run adopt from the installed skill, not a vendored copy")
822	    return path.read_text()
823	
824	
825	def extract_block(text: str, begin: str, end: str) -> str | None:
826	    m = re.search(re.escape(begin) + r".*?" + re.escape(end), text, re.S)
827	    return m.group(0) if m else None
828	
829	
830	def cli_version(path: Path) -> str:
831	    m = re.search(r'^__version__ = "([^"]+)"', path.read_text(), re.M)
832	    return m.group(1) if m else "?"
833	
834	
835	def upsert_block(text: str, begin: str, end: str, block: str) -> str:
836	    pattern = re.compile(re.escape(begin) + r".*?" + re.escape(end), re.S)
837	    if pattern.search(text):
838	        return pattern.sub(lambda _: block.strip("\n"), text, count=1)
839	    sep = "" if not text else ("\n" if text.endswith("\n") else "\n\n")
840	    return f"{text}{sep}\n{block.strip(chr(10))}\n" if text else block.strip("\n") + "\n"
841	
842	
843	def cmd_adopt(root: Path, subs: list[Sub], args) -> int:
844	    actions: list[dict] = []
845	    overrides: dict[str, tuple[str, str | None]] = {}
846	    for spec in args.set or []:
847	        ident, _, val = spec.partition("=")
848	        pol, _, bump = val.partition(":")
849	        if pol not in POLICIES or (bump and bump not in BUMP_MODES):
850	            raise UsageError(f"--set {spec!r}: expected NAME=track|pin|lazy[:pr|direct|manual]")
851	        overrides[resolve(subs, ident).name] = (pol, bump or None)
852	
853	    def set_key(s: Sub, key: str, value: str) -> None:
854	        actions.append({"kind": "gitmodules", "target": f"submodule.{s.name}.{key}", "detail": value})
855	        if not args.dry_run:
856	            git("config", "-f", ".gitmodules", f"submodule.{s.name}.{key}", value, cwd=root)
857	
858	    for s in subs:
859	        forced = overrides.get(s.name)
860	        policy = forced[0] if forced else (s.policy or args.policy_default)
861	        if policy != s.policy:
862	            set_key(s, "x-policy", policy)
863	        if policy == "track":
864	            bump = (forced and forced[1]) or s.bump or args.bump_default
865	            if bump != s.bump:
866	                set_key(s, "x-bump", bump)
867	        if not s.branch and policy != "lazy":
868	            remote_head = ""
869	            if is_initialized(root, s):
870	                remote_head = git("symbolic-ref", "-q", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD",
871	                                  cwd=root / s.path, check=False).removeprefix("origin/")
872	            set_key(s, "branch", remote_head or "main")
873	        if policy == "lazy" and s.update != "none":
874	            set_key(s, "update", "none")
875	
876	    if args.vendor_cli:
877	        # Opt-in only (offline / air-gapped): a copy stops receiving skill updates.
878	        dest = root / VENDORED_CLI
879	        src = Path(__file__).resolve()
880	        if dest.resolve() != src and (not dest.exists() or dest.read_bytes() != src.read_bytes()):
881	            actions.append({"kind": "file", "target": VENDORED_CLI,
882	                            "detail": f"{'refresh' if dest.exists() else 'vendor'} CLI {__version__}"})
883	            if not args.dry_run:
884	                dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
885	                shutil.copy2(src, dest)
886	
887	    if not args.no_agents:
888	        agents = find_agents_file(root) or root / "AGENTS.md"
889	        old = agents.read_text() if agents.exists() else ""
890	        new = upsert_block(old, AGENTS_BEGIN, AGENTS_END, render_asset("agents-block.md.template"))
891	        if new != old:
892	            actions.append({"kind": "file", "target": agents.name, "detail": "upsert agent guidance block"})
893	            if not args.dry_run:
894	                agents.write_text(new)
895	
896	    if not args.no_justfile:
897	        jf = find_justfile(root) or root / "justfile"
898	        old = jf.read_text() if jf.exists() else ""
899	        new = upsert_block(old, JUST_BEGIN, JUST_END, render_asset("justfile.snippet"))
900	        if new != old:
901	            actions.append({"kind": "file", "target": jf.name, "detail": "upsert sub-* recipes"})
902	            if not args.dry_run:
903	                jf.write_text(new)
904	
905	    if not args.no_gitignore and ensure_gitignore(root, args.dry_run):
906	        actions.append({"kind": "file", "target": ".gitignore", "detail": f"ignore {WORKTREE_DIR}/"})
907	
908	    if args.with_ci:
909	        wf = root / ".github" / "workflows" / "superproject-bump.yml"
910	        content = render_asset("superproject-bump.yml")
911	        if not wf.exists() or wf.read_text() != content:
912	            actions.append({"kind": "file", "target": str(wf.relative_to(root)), "detail": "scheduled bump workflow"})
913	            if not args.dry_run:
914	                wf.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
915	                wf.write_text(content)
916	
917	    if args.with_hook:
918	        hook = root / git("rev-parse", "--git-path", "hooks/pre-commit", cwd=root)
919	        if hook.exists():
920	            if render_asset("pre-commit-hook.sh") != hook.read_text():
921	                actions.append({"kind": "skipped", "target": "pre-commit hook",
922	                                "detail": "a different hook exists; chain `preflight` into it by hand"})
923	        else:
924	            actions.append({"kind": "file", "target": "pre-commit hook", "detail": "run preflight before commits"})
925	            if not args.dry_run:
926	                hook.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
927	                hook.write_text(render_asset("pre-commit-hook.sh"))
928	                hook.chmod(0o755)
929	
930	    if not args.no_git_config:
931	        for key, value in (("diff.submodule", "log"), ("status.submoduleSummary", "true"),
932	                           ("push.recurseSubmodules", "check")):
933	            if not git("config", "--local", "--get", key, cwd=root, check=False):
934	                actions.append({"kind": "git-config", "target": key, "detail": value})
935	                if not args.dry_run:
936	                    git("config", "--local", key, value, cwd=root)
937	
938	    verb = "would" if args.dry_run else "did"
939	    text = "\n".join(f"{verb}: {a['kind']:10} {a['target']} = {a['detail']}" for a in actions) or "already adopted; nothing to do"
940	    if actions and not args.dry_run:
941	        text += "\nreview with `git diff`, then run `audit`"
942	    emit(args, {"actions": actions, "dry_run": args.dry_run}, text)
943	    return 0

````text
1	---
2	name: superproject-workspace
3	description: Keep a git-submodule superproject (umbrella repo / multi-repo workspace used as one agent entry point) from drifting — per-submodule policy in .gitmodules (track / pin / lazy), lag and drift status, safe fast-forward, preflighted gitlink bumps in one outer commit, scheduled bump PRs, child worktrees, and audit/adopt for existing superprojects. Use when a repo has .gitmodules and the user asks to update/sync submodules, bump pointers, work on a branch inside a submodule, add a repo to the workspace, or asks "monorepo vs submodules", incl. "submodule 落後 / 更新 submodule / 拉到 latest main".
4	---
5	
6	# superproject-workspace
7	
8	A superproject is a repo whose job is to hold other repos as git submodules,
9	so that one agent session gets every repo's context and edit access while each
10	repo keeps its own remote, PRs, and release cycle. The cost: **a gitlink
11	records a commit, not a branch.** Children merge PRs and the superproject
12	silently falls behind; checkouts end up detached, dirty, or on stray branches;
13	pointers reference commits nobody pushed. Drift is the default, not a bug.
14	
15	This skill makes drift **visible** and moves pointers **by policy**, with one
16	CLI (`scripts/superproject.py`, stdlib Python ≥3.10, PEP 723). Every
17	superproject **references** the installed skill's CLI instead of copying it,
18	so `npx skills update` upgrades all of them at once. Otherwise the tool itself
19	would drift the same way the gitlinks do.
20	
21	## When to use
22	
23	- The repo has `.gitmodules` and the user wants to update, sync, or "pull latest" children.
24	- After a child PR merges, to move the superproject pointer.
25	- Starting feature work inside a child repo from the superproject.
26	- Adding a repo to a workspace, or deciding *how* to bring repos together (see `references/decision-guide.md`).
27	- Auditing or upgrading an older superproject that has ad-hoc recipes.
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- Ordinary single-repo git work: use `git-workflow`.
32	- Issue/PR lifecycle inside one child: use that child's own workflow (`forge-native-dev`, etc.).
33	- The repos are not submodules (manifest + gitignored clones, or Project add-dir): only the decision guide applies.
34	
35	## The policy model
36	
37	Each child declares its policy as extra keys in `.gitmodules`. Git ignores keys
38	it does not know, so these keys live next to `path` and `url` and cannot fall
39	out of sync with them.
40	
41	```ini
42	[submodule "app"]
43	    path = app
44	    url = git@github.com:me/app.git
45	    branch = main        # tracking branch (native key; unset -> child's origin/HEAD)
46	    x-policy = track     # track | pin | lazy
47	    x-bump = pr          # pr | direct | manual   (only for track)
48	    x-tier = core        # free-form grouping for --tier selection
49	    update = none        # lazy only: plain `git submodule update --init` skips it
50	```
51	
52	| Policy | Means | Pointer moves | Initialized |
53	|---|---|---|---|
54	| `track` | "Be at the latest `origin/<branch>`" | `pull` (ff-only), then `bump`; may be automated (`x-bump`) | by default |
55	| `pin` | "Be at a known baseline" (production, a release, a reproduction) | only `bump --reason "..."` | by default |
56	| `lazy` | "Reference material; fetch only when a task needs it" | only `bump --reason` | only when named |
57	| unset | treated as `pin`; `audit` warns | | |
58	
59	Bump modes for `track`: `pr` means scheduled CI opens one PR on
60	`chore/submodule-bump`. `direct` means CI commits to the default branch after
61	preflight. `manual` means a human or agent runs `bump`. An umbrella where every
62	child follows main is simply "everything `track`". A workspace hub mixes core
63	`pin`s with `lazy` references. Details and example configs are in
64	`references/policies.md`.
65	
66	## Workflow
67	
68	Below, `sp` means `uv run --script <skill-dir>/scripts/superproject.py`. For a
69	global install, `<skill-dir>` is `~/.agents/skills/superproject-workspace`.
70	After `adopt`, the same commands are available as `just sub-*` recipes. They
71	resolve the CLI in this order, first match wins:
72	
73	1. `$SUPERPROJECT_CLI`
74	2. a vendored `scripts/superproject.py` (opt-in)
75	3. the project skill install `.agents/skills/...`
76	4. the global install `~/.agents/skills/...`
77	5. GitHub raw at `$SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF` (default `main`)
78	
79	`just sub-which` prints which one won. Every command takes `--json`. Mutating
80	commands take `--dry-run`.
81	
82	### 1. Look first
83	
84	```bash
85	sp status --fetch   # policy, lag, drift, dirty, worktrees
86	sp audit            # findings + exact fix commands
87	```
88	
89	Without `--fetch`, lag is computed against stale remote refs. Never report
90	"up to date" without fetching.
91	
92	### 2. Get a child you need
93	
94	```bash
95	sp init                 # all non-lazy, uninitialized children
96	sp init some-reference  # a lazy child, by name/path/basename
97	```
98	
99	`init` never touches an already-initialized checkout and does not recurse
100	unless you pass `--recursive`. Initialization is not a way to update.
101	
102	### 3. Develop inside a child: use a child worktree
103	
104	```bash
105	sp worktree add app feat/login
106	# -> .worktrees/app/feat-login  (gitignored; branch from origin/main for track,
107	#    from the recorded gitlink for pin, so fixes start from the baseline)
108	```
109	
110	Work, commit, push, and open the PR **in the child's own repo and workflow**.
111	The submodule checkout itself stays on its branch or pin. Clean up with
112	`worktree list` (shows merged ones) and `worktree remove app feat/login --delete-branch`.
113	Do not create worktrees of the superproject for this; see `references/worktrees.md`.
114	
115	### 4. Move pointers: inside-out, one outer commit
116	
117	```bash
118	sp pull                 # ff track children (checkout only)
119	sp bump --all-track --commit
120	sp bump lib --reason "prod baseline v2.3" --commit   # pin/lazy
121	```
122	
123	`bump` refuses the whole set if any child is dirty or its commit is not
124	pushed. For a `track` child, "pushed" means on `origin/<branch>`; for a pin, it
125	means on any origin branch. One cross-repo change gets one outer commit. The
126	commit body contains each range and the `--submodule=log` summary. Pass
127	`--partial` only when the user explicitly accepts splitting.
128	
129	### 5. Guard every outer commit
130	
131	```bash
132	sp preflight   # also installed as a pre-commit hook by adopt --with-hook
133	```
134	
135	### 6. Adopt an existing superproject
136	
137	```bash
138	uv run --script <skill>/scripts/superproject.py audit --root ../old-super
139	uv run --script <skill>/scripts/superproject.py adopt --root ../old-super --dry-run \
140	    --policy-default pin --set app=track:pr --set docs-ref=lazy
141	```
142	
143	`adopt` writes policy keys, but only where they are missing or named by
144	`--set`. It also upserts a marker-delimited AGENTS.md block and `sub-*`
145	justfile recipes, adds `.worktrees/` to `.gitignore`, and sets local git
146	config:
147	- `diff.submodule=log`
148	- `status.submoduleSummary=true`
149	- `push.recurseSubmodules=check`
150	
151	Opt in to `--with-ci` and `--with-hook`. It does **not** copy the CLI. Pass
152	`--vendor-cli` only for offline or air-gapped superprojects, and accept that
153	the copy stops receiving fixes. It is idempotent: rerun it (`just sub-adopt`)
154	after a skill update to refresh the managed blocks. `audit` reports
155	`managed-block-stale` and `vendored-cli-stale` when the tool itself has
156	drifted. Review `git diff`
157	before committing, and pick policies with the user. The default
158	`--policy-default pin` is deliberately conservative.
159	
160	## Available scripts
161	
162	- **`scripts/superproject.py`**: `status | init | pull | bump | preflight | worktree add|list|remove | audit | adopt | ci-plan`.
163	  - Common flags: `--root`, `--json`, `--dry-run` (mutating commands).
164	  - Selection: positional names (name, path, or basename), `--tier`, `--policy`, `--mode`.
165	  - Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 refused or check failed, 2 usage error. Diagnostics go to stderr.
166	
167	## Bundled assets
168	
169	- `assets/justfile.snippet`: thin `sub-*` recipes (marker block; `adopt` upserts it).
170	- `assets/agents-block.md.template`: the cross-repo contract for agents (marker block).
171	- `assets/superproject-bump.yml`: scheduled, `workflow_dispatch`, and `repository_dispatch` bump workflow (`pr` and `direct`).
172	- `assets/child-dispatch.yml`: optional; goes in a child repo to request an immediate bump on push to main.
173	- `assets/pre-commit-hook.sh`: runs `preflight`.
174	
175	The recipes, hook, and workflow all use the same CLI resolution. CI pins
176	the version with the `SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF` repository variable (a tag or
177	SHA).
178	
179	## Reference files
180	
181	- `references/decision-guide.md`: read when choosing between a real monorepo, a submodule superproject, a manifest with clones, or Project add-dir.
182	- `references/policies.md`: read when assigning policies, or for umbrella vs hub examples.
183	- `references/worktrees.md`: read before any branch work inside a child.
184	- `references/ci-bump.md`: read when enabling `pr`/`direct` automation, private or GitLab children, or dispatch.
185	- `references/agent-entry.md`: read when setting up the superproject as an agent entry point (AGENTS.md layering, Claude/Codex Projects, root context).
186	- `references/gotchas.md`: read when git prints something surprising about a submodule.
187	- `references/case-patterns.md`: read when adopting; lists lessons from real umbrella and hub superprojects.
188	
189	## Gotchas
190	
191	- **Don't copy the CLI into each superproject.** Copies freeze at adoption
192	  time and silently diverge across repos. Reference the installed skill; vendor
193	  only for offline use, and let `audit` flag stale copies.
194	- **`git pull` in the superproject does not update children.** It moves gitlinks and leaves checkouts behind, which then shows as `modified: app (new commits)`. Run `status`, then decide whether to `bump` (keep the checkout) or `git submodule update -- app` (discard and go back to the gitlink).
195	- **`git submodule update` detaches HEAD** and can strand local commits that are not on a branch. `pull` refuses "detached commit not on origin/<branch>" for this reason; save the commit to a branch first.
196	- **"Latest" never means resetting pins.** A pinned child may legitimately be behind or sit on a release branch. `audit` reports this as info, not an error.
197	- **Never bump to an unpushed child commit.** A fresh clone would then fail with `fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref`. `bump` and `preflight` block this, and `push.recurseSubmodules=check` blocks the outer push.
198	- **A submodule name is not its path.** One example is `[submodule "dotfiles"] path = dotfiles-unix`. Policy keys use the *name*. The CLI accepts either.
199	- **CI PRs opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other workflows.** Run the gates inside the bump job, or use a PAT or GitHub App token (`references/ci-bump.md`).
200	- **After a child's URL changes in `.gitmodules`**, existing clones keep the old URL until `git submodule sync`. `init` syncs, and `audit` flags `url-unsynced`.
201
````

=================== references/agent-entry.md
# The superproject as an agent entry point

## Instruction layering

- **Outer `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`** governs *cross-repo* work only. Keep the
  `adopt` block in it (commit inside-out, one outer commit, worktrees, pins).
  Add a short map of which child owns what.
- **Each child's `AGENTS.md`** stays authoritative inside that child. Agents
  must read it before editing there; say so explicitly in the outer file.
  Claude Code loads nested `CLAUDE.md` files on demand when it touches files
  in that directory; Codex reads `AGENTS.md` along the path. Neither harness
  guarantees this for files the agent only greps.
- Do not copy child instructions upward; link to them. Copies drift exactly
  like gitlinks do.

## Root context that earns its place

What makes a superproject better than "a folder of clones" is content that
belongs to *no single child*:

- a cross-repo context graph (entities, relations, dated observations)
- `pitfalls/` for traps that span repos (version skew, protocol mismatches)
- runbooks that orchestrate several children (deploy, parity checks)
- agent session history (SpecStory), since cross-repo sessions have no other home

Record facts with the gitlink SHA or date they were observed against. A note
like "service X does Y" goes stale when the pointer moves.

## Claude / Codex Projects and add-dir

A Project or `--add-dir` gives similar context breadth without submodules,
but provides no versioned snapshot and no home for root content. Use them for
one-off reads; use the superproject when the combination itself, or the root
knowledge, matters.

## Session start checklist (put in AGENTS.md)

1. `sp status --fetch`
2. Read the target child's AGENTS.md.
3. Branch work goes in `worktree add`, never in the submodule checkout.
=================== references/case-patterns.md
# Case patterns from real superprojects

Two production superprojects informed this skill. Their lessons, with private
details removed:

## Umbrella: parallel platform repos, all following main

Five equally owned repos (one per OS or platform), unified by an outer repo
whose purpose is UX parity across them. No product is built in the outer repo.

What worked:
- **Inside-out commits** with a preflight that the inner HEAD is reachable
  from `origin/main` before the gitlink is staged. This is the origin of
  `bump`/`preflight`.
- **ff-only "pull main"** that refuses diverged branches and detached commits
  not on main. This is the origin of `pull`'s refusal list.
- **"One cross-repo change gets one outer commit"**, reviewed with
  `git diff --cached --submodule=log`.
- Deploy recipes pin the tool to a specific child checkout, never to an
  implicit default.

What drifted:
- No scheduled bump, so children ran 9+ commits ahead of the recorded pointer
  between maintenance sessions. Fix: `x-bump = pr`.
- Every child path was hard-coded into a dozen recipes, written twice (POSIX
  sh and PowerShell). Adding a sixth child meant editing all of them, and one
  pathspec still named a path that no longer existed. Fix: policy-driven
  recipes and one cross-platform CLI.

## Workspace hub: tiered children, pins, and root knowledge

About 20 children across GitHub and GitLab, org and personal, grouped
`core / personal / references`. The outer repo holds a structured context
graph (entities, relations, dated observations), runbooks, and agent history.

What worked:
- **Tiers with on-demand init**: references are fetched only when a task
  needs them, and never recursively. This is the origin of `lazy` + `update = none`.
- **"Latest is not reset-to-main"**: production diagnosis reads the deployed
  revision rather than upstream tip. This is the origin of `pin`.
- **Root context** that cites the revisions it observed.

What drifted:
- No rule for when a core pin moves forward, and no lag report. Some
  checkouts sat on feature branches, dirty, while their gitlinks pointed at
  commits on no origin branch at all. Fix: `status`, `audit`, explicit
  `pin`/`track`.
- External worktrees outside the entry point. Fix: `.worktrees/<child>/<branch>`.
- A bespoke init script (tiers and selection) that the policy keys plus `init --tier` now replace.

## Older, less agentic superprojects

These typically have `.gitmodules` and nothing else: no policy, no AGENTS.md,
and READMEs telling humans to run `git submodule update --remote`. Run `audit`,
then `adopt --dry-run --policy-default pin`, agree the policies with the
owner, then `adopt` and commit.
=================== references/ci-bump.md
# Automated bumps in CI

`adopt --with-ci` installs `.github/workflows/superproject-bump.yml`:

1. `ci-plan --json` lists `track` children with `x-bump` `pr` or `direct`.
   Use `--only` to select one child, as `workflow_dispatch` and
   `repository_dispatch` do.
2. `init` checks out just those children.
3. **direct:** `pull` → `bump --commit` → push to the default branch.
4. **pr:** switch to the fixed branch `chore/submodule-bump` → `pull` →
   `bump --commit` → force-push → open the PR once (later runs update it).

The job fails, with a red run, when `pull` or `bump` refuses. Typical causes:
a child's history was rewritten (diverged), or the gitlink points at a
deleted commit. Fix those by hand.

## Which CLI version CI runs

The workflow uses `scripts/superproject.py` if the repo vendored one
(`adopt --vendor-cli`). Otherwise it runs the skill's CLI straight from GitHub
raw at the `SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF` repository variable, defaulting to `main`:

- **`main`**: every superproject picks up fixes automatically. You trust the
  skill repo's main branch with a job that has `contents: write`.
- **tag or SHA**: reproducible and reviewed. Moving it is one variable change
  per repo. Use this for superprojects that guard production.

## Credentials

| Children | Secret | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Public | none | `GITHUB_TOKEN` can push the outer repo |
| Private on GitHub | `SUBMODULE_TOKEN` | Fine-grained PAT (or GitHub App token) with *Contents: read* on each child. The workflow rewrites `git@github.com:` and `https://github.com/` to use it. |
| GitLab | `GITLAB_TOKEN` | Project or group access token with `read_repository`; rewritten the same way |
| Other forges | add another `insteadOf` line | |

SSH URLs in `.gitmodules` are fine for humans. The `insteadOf` rewrite maps
them to HTTPS in CI.

## Gotchas

- **PRs created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `pull_request` workflows.**
  Either run validation in the bump job itself, or create the PR with a PAT or
  App token.
- **`direct` with branch protection** needs a token that may bypass it, or
  else use `pr`.
- **Schedule vs dispatch:** a schedule is simple and needs no child changes.
  For near-immediate bumps, add `assets/child-dispatch.yml` to each child.
  This needs a PAT with *Contents: write* on the superproject, because
  `repository_dispatch` requires it.
- **GitLab-hosted superprojects:** port the same steps to `.gitlab-ci.yml`
  with a scheduled pipeline and `glab mr create`. The CLI is forge-agnostic.
=================== references/decision-guide.md
# Decision guide: how to bring repos together for an agent

Goal: one agent entry point with context (and usually edit access) across
several repos, without coupling their histories, CI, or release cycles more
than necessary.

| Option | What it is | Version snapshot of the set? | Drift problem | Best when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Real monorepo** | One repo, one history | Yes (every commit) | None | Repos ship together, share CI and owners, and change atomically |
| **Submodule superproject** (this skill) | Outer repo pins each child by gitlink | Yes (outer commit = exact set) | Yes, so manage it by policy | Repos are independent but you need reproducible "this set worked together" points, or the outer repo carries shared knowledge (agent history, context, runbooks) |
| **Manifest + gitignored clones** | `repos.yaml` + a clone/update script (`mani`, `gita`, `repo`, `meta`, or 20 lines of shell) | No (unless you record SHAs yourself) | None: each clone is just "whatever is checked out" | You only need co-location for context; no one asks "which versions went together?" |
| **Project / add-dir** (Claude Code `--add-dir`, Codex or Claude Projects) | Agent session spans several existing checkouts | No | None | Ad-hoc, personal, short-lived cross-repo tasks |

## Questions that decide it

1. **Do you need to reproduce a combination later?** Examples: "what did prod
   run", "the umbrella state that passed parity checks". If yes, choose
   submodules, or a monorepo if the repos are tightly coupled.
2. **Does the outer repo have content of its own?** Examples: AGENTS.md, a
   cross-repo `context/` graph, `pitfalls/`, SpecStory history, deployment
   runbooks. If yes, a superproject gives that content a versioned home, and
   the gitlinks date each note against concrete child versions.
3. **Do children have different owners, visibility, or forges** (GitHub +
   GitLab, personal + org)? Then rule out a monorepo; submodules or a manifest
   both work.
4. **Will you remember to bump?** If not, either automate it (`x-bump = pr` or
   `direct`) or choose a manifest. A superproject with no bumping is the worst
   option: it pins by accident.

## Hybrid that works well

Use a superproject for the **core** set (`track` or `pin`), and mark
reference material `lazy` so a fresh clone stays small. Truly throwaway reads
don't need a submodule at all: use add-dir for those.
=================== references/gotchas.md
# Submodule gotchas, by symptom

### `modified: app (new commits)` after `git pull`
The outer pull moved the gitlink; the child checkout stayed where it was (or
the reverse: you moved the child). Inspect with `status`. To keep the
checkout, run `bump app`. To discard it, run `git submodule update -- app`.
Setting `git config submodule.recurse true` makes `pull`/`checkout` update
children automatically. That is convenient for consumers, but surprising
while you develop in children, so leave it off in maintainer checkouts.

### `HEAD detached at 1a2b3c4` inside a child
This is normal after `git submodule update`. Commits made in this state belong
to no branch and are easily lost. Save them first:
`git switch -c rescue/<topic>`. `pull` refuses to move a detached commit that
is not on `origin/<branch>`.

### `fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref <sha>` / `Fetched in submodule path 'x', but it did not contain <sha>`
Someone recorded a gitlink to a commit that was never pushed, or was
force-pushed away. Push it if it still exists locally. Otherwise move the
pointer to a pushed commit. Prevent it with `preflight` (pre-commit) and
`push.recurseSubmodules=check`.

### `Submodule 'x' could not be updated` / `update = none` surprises
`update = none` in `.gitmodules` makes plain `git submodule update --init`
skip the child. That is intended for `lazy` children. `init <name>` passes
`--checkout` to override it for that one call.

### Clone still uses the old URL after `.gitmodules` changed
`.git/config` caches submodule URLs at init time. Run
`git submodule sync -- <path>`; `audit` reports `url-unsynced`.

### Nested submodules fail to clone (private descendants)
`--recursive` pulls in every descendant, including private or unrecoverable
ones. The CLI never recurses unless asked. Initialize nested children
explicitly, only when the task needs them.

### Branch named in `.gitmodules` doesn't exist (`origin/main missing`)
The child uses `master`, or a release branch. Set `branch` explicitly. If
`branch` is unset, the CLI uses the child's `origin/HEAD`.

### `git status` shows `.worktrees/` as untracked
Add `.worktrees/` to `.gitignore`. `worktree add` and `adopt` do this
automatically.
=================== references/policies.md
# Policies

Keys live in `.gitmodules` under the submodule's **name** (not path):

```bash
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.x-policy track   # track | pin | lazy
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.x-bump pr        # pr | direct | manual
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.x-tier core
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.branch main      # native git key
git config -f .gitmodules submodule.<name>.update none      # lazy children
```

## Choosing a policy

| Question about the child | Policy |
|---|---|
| You own it and the superproject should follow its main line | `track` |
| A specific version matters (deployed, released, a known-good reproduction) | `pin` |
| It's reference reading, a third-party upstream, or rarely used | `lazy` |
| You don't know yet | leave unset (treated as `pin`; `audit` reminds you) |

## Choosing a bump mode (`track` only)

| Mode | Use when | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `manual` | Default. Bumps happen deliberately, alongside cross-repo work | Falls behind if nobody looks; `audit` shows `behind` |
| `pr` | You want a reviewable stream of updates (umbrellas, docs hubs) | PR noise; needs CI token for private children |
| `direct` | The pointer carries no review value (pure aggregation, notes repos) | A broken child lands in the outer default branch without review |

`direct` still runs preflight: a commit that is not reachable from
`origin/<branch>` is never recorded.

## Example: umbrella (every child follows main)

Parallel, equally owned repos, such as per-platform dotfiles:

```ini
[submodule "dotfiles-unix"]
    path = dotfiles-unix
    url = git@github.com:me/dotfiles.git
    branch = main
    x-policy = track
    x-bump = pr
[submodule "dotfiles-windows"]
    path = dotfiles-windows
    url = git@github.com:me/dotfiles-windows.git
    branch = main
    x-policy = track
    x-bump = pr
```

## Example: workspace hub (tiers)

```ini
[submodule "submodules/engine"]
    path = submodules/engine
    url = https://github.com/org/engine.git
    branch = release/2.x       # the baseline the pin follows
    x-policy = pin
    x-tier = core
[submodule "submodules/dashboard"]
    path = submodules/dashboard
    url = https://github.com/org/dashboard.git
    branch = main
    x-policy = track
    x-bump = manual
    x-tier = core
[submodule "submodules/references/someone/paper-code"]
    path = submodules/references/someone/paper-code
    url = https://github.com/someone/paper-code.git
    x-policy = lazy
    x-tier = reference
    update = none
```

`init --tier reference` fetches all references at once. `status --tier core`
narrows the report.

## Pins and branches

For a pin, `branch` names the line the pin follows, such as a release branch.
That is what `status` measures lag against. The safety rule for pins is
weaker than for track: the recorded commit must be on **some** origin branch,
so a fresh clone can check it out. It does not have to be on `branch`.
=================== references/worktrees.md
# Worktrees in a superproject

## Rule

Feature work in a child happens in a **worktree of the child**, placed inside
the superproject at `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch-slug>` (gitignored):

```bash
sp worktree add <child> <branch> [--base REV]
sp worktree list
sp worktree remove <child> <branch> --delete-branch
```

The submodule checkout itself stays on its tracked branch, or at its pin.

## Why not the alternatives

| Approach | Problem |
|---|---|
| Switch branches in the submodule checkout | Only one branch at a time. The gitlink shows dirty while you work. `pull` and `bump` then operate on your feature branch. Parallel agents collide. |
| `git worktree add` of the **superproject** | Submodules in a new superproject worktree start **uninitialized**: each worktree needs a full `submodule update --init`, which is slow and multiplies clones. Git's support for submodules inside multiple superproject worktrees is still marked experimental. |
| Worktree outside the superproject (`~/worktrees/...`) | Works, but leaves the agent's entry point. Context such as AGENTS.md, `context/`, and sibling repos is not under the session root, and the agent needs add-dir. Use it only when a task must be isolated from the superproject. |

## Base revision

- `track` children branch from `origin/<branch>`.
- `pin` and `lazy` children branch from the **recorded gitlink**: a fix to a
  pinned production baseline should start from that baseline, not from
  upstream main.
- An existing local or remote branch of the same name is checked out instead
  of a new one being created.
- Override with `--base`.

## Coexistence with superproject issue worktrees

`forge-native-dev` places superproject issue worktrees at `.worktrees/issue-<n>`.
Child worktrees are nested under the child's path (`.worktrees/app/...`), so
the two never collide. Superproject issue worktrees remain fine for changes
that touch **only** outer content (docs, context, CI).
=================== assets/agents-block.md.template
<!-- superproject-workspace:agent-guidance -->
## Working across submodules

This repository is a superproject: each child under a submodule path is its
own repository with its own remote, history, and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. Read
the child's own instructions before editing inside it; they are authoritative
there. This file only governs cross-repo work.

- **Gitlinks record commits, not branches.** Each child declares a policy in
  `.gitmodules` (`x-policy`): `track` follows `origin/<branch>` by
  fast-forward, `pin` moves only for a stated reason, `lazy` is not
  initialized until a task needs it. "Latest" never means resetting pins.
- The `just sub-*` recipes run the shared skill CLI (`just sub-which` shows
  which file). Without just: `uv run --script
  ~/.agents/skills/superproject-workspace/scripts/superproject.py <cmd>`.
- **Look before acting:** `just sub-status --fetch` shows
  policy, lag, drift, and dirty checkouts. `audit` gives fixes.
- **Need an absent child?** `just sub-init <name>`. Never
  recurse into nested submodules unless the task needs them.
- **Develop in a child worktree, not the child checkout:**
  `just sub-wt add <child> <branch>` creates
  `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch>`. Keep the checkout at its tracked branch
  or pinned commit. Do not create worktrees of this superproject for child
  work; their submodules start uninitialized.
- **Commit inside-out.** Commit and push the child first, through the child's
  own PR flow. Then move the pointer here with
  `just sub-bump <child> --commit` (add `--reason` for pin/lazy).
  The bump refuses unpushed or unreachable commits.
- **One cross-repo change gets one outer commit.** Bump every affected child
  together, and leave no unrelated gitlink drift behind.
- **Before any outer commit that stages gitlinks**, run
  `just sub-preflight`.
- Preserve existing child branches, local commits, and dirty work. `pull`
  refuses diverged or dirty checkouts; resolve those by hand, don't force.
<!-- superproject-workspace:agent-guidance --> (end)
=================== assets/child-dispatch.yml
# superproject-workspace: place in a CHILD repo to request an immediate
# pointer bump in its superproject after every push to main.
# Replace OWNER/SUPERPROJECT and CHILD_NAME (the submodule name in the
# superproject's .gitmodules). SUPERPROJECT_DISPATCH_TOKEN is a fine-grained
# PAT with contents:write on the superproject (needed for repository_dispatch).
name: notify-superproject

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  dispatch:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Request a submodule bump
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPERPROJECT_DISPATCH_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh api repos/OWNER/SUPERPROJECT/dispatches \
            -f event_type=submodule-bump \
            -f "client_payload[submodule]=CHILD_NAME"
=================== assets/justfile.snippet
# superproject-workspace:begin (managed by `superproject.py adopt`; edits inside this block are overwritten)
# The CLI is NOT copied into this repo. It resolves, first match wins:
#   $SUPERPROJECT_CLI > scripts/superproject.py (adopt --vendor-cli)
#   > project skill install (.agents/skills) > global skill install (~/.agents/skills)
#   > GitHub raw at $SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF (default: main).
# Update every superproject at once with `npx skills update`.
_sp_vendored := justfile_directory() / "scripts" / "superproject.py"
_sp_project := justfile_directory() / ".agents" / "skills" / "superproject-workspace" / "scripts" / "superproject.py"
_sp_global := home_directory() / ".agents" / "skills" / "superproject-workspace" / "scripts" / "superproject.py"
_sp_remote := "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/" + env("SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF", "main") + "/skills/local/superproject-workspace/scripts/superproject.py"
_sp := env("SUPERPROJECT_CLI", if path_exists(_sp_vendored) == "true" { _sp_vendored } else if path_exists(_sp_project) == "true" { _sp_project } else if path_exists(_sp_global) == "true" { _sp_global } else { _sp_remote })

# Policy, lag and drift for every submodule (add --fetch for current numbers).
sub-status *args:
    uv run --script "{{_sp}}" status {{args}}

# Initialize children; lazy ones only when named, by --tier, or with --all.
sub-init *args:
    uv run --script "{{_sp}}" init {{args}}

# Fast-forward track children to origin/<branch> (checkouts only).
sub-pull *args:
    uv run --script "{{_sp}}" pull {{args}}

# Record children's HEADs as gitlinks after preflight (add --commit).
sub-bump *args:
    uv run --script "{{_sp}}" bump {{args}}

# Verify staged gitlinks are pushed and reachable.
sub-preflight *args:
    uv run --script "{{_sp}}" preflight {{args}}

# Child worktrees: sub-wt add <child> <branch> | list | remove <child> <branch>
sub-wt *args:
    uv run --script "{{_sp}}" worktree {{args}}

# Read-only health report (also flags stale managed blocks).
sub-audit *args:
    uv run --script "{{_sp}}" audit {{args}}

# Re-apply managed blocks from the current CLI version (idempotent).
sub-adopt *args:
    uv run --script "{{_sp}}" adopt {{args}}

# Which CLI file the recipes resolve to.
sub-which:
    @echo "{{_sp}}"

# superproject-workspace:end
=================== assets/pre-commit-hook.sh
#!/bin/sh
# superproject-workspace: refuse outer commits whose staged gitlinks point at
# commits that are not pushed. Resolves the CLI like the justfile recipes do.
root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) || exit 1
rel=skills/superproject-workspace/scripts/superproject.py
cli=${SUPERPROJECT_CLI:-}
for cand in "$root/scripts/superproject.py" "$root/.agents/$rel" "$HOME/.agents/$rel"; do
  [ -n "$cli" ] && break
  [ -f "$cand" ] && cli=$cand
done
cli=${cli:-https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/${SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF:-main}/skills/local/superproject-workspace/scripts/superproject.py}
exec uv run --quiet --script "$cli" preflight
=================== assets/superproject-bump.yml
# superproject-workspace: move gitlinks of `x-policy = track` children.
#   x-bump = direct -> committed straight to the default branch after preflight
#   x-bump = pr     -> one PR on the fixed branch chore/submodule-bump
#   x-bump = manual -> never touched here
# Private children need a SUBMODULE_TOKEN secret (fine-grained PAT with
# contents:read on each child). See references/ci-bump.md.
# The CLI is fetched from the skill repo at SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF (repository
# variable; default main). Pin it to a tag or SHA for fully reproducible runs.
name: superproject-bump

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 3 * * 1" # weekly, Mon 03:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      only:
        description: "Bump only this submodule (name or path); empty = all"
        required: false
        default: ""
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [submodule-bump] # sent by a child's notify workflow

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: superproject-bump
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CLI_REF: ${{ vars.SUPERPROJECT_CLI_REF || 'main' }}
  ONLY: ${{ github.event.inputs.only || github.event.client_payload.submodule || '' }}
  BUMP_BRANCH: chore/submodule-bump
  DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}

jobs:
  bump:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          submodules: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6

      - name: Resolve the CLI (vendored copy if present, else the skill repo)
        run: |
          if [ -f scripts/superproject.py ]; then
            echo "CLI=$PWD/scripts/superproject.py" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo "CLI=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/${CLI_REF}/skills/local/superproject-workspace/scripts/superproject.py" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      - name: Configure git identity and child credentials
        env:
          SUBMODULE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUBMODULE_TOKEN }}
          GITLAB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITLAB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config --global user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          if [ -n "$SUBMODULE_TOKEN" ]; then
            git config --global url."https://x-access-token:${SUBMODULE_TOKEN}@github.com/".insteadOf "git@github.com:"
            git config --global --add url."https://x-access-token:${SUBMODULE_TOKEN}@github.com/".insteadOf "https://github.com/"
          fi
          if [ -n "$GITLAB_TOKEN" ]; then
            git config --global url."https://oauth2:${GITLAB_TOKEN}@gitlab.com/".insteadOf "git@gitlab.com:"
            git config --global --add url."https://oauth2:${GITLAB_TOKEN}@gitlab.com/".insteadOf "https://gitlab.com/"
          fi

      - name: Plan and initialize the automated children
        run: |
          uv run --script "$CLI" ci-plan --json ${ONLY:+--only "$ONLY"} > "$RUNNER_TEMP/plan.json"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/plan.json"
          mapfile -t paths < <(jq -r '.init_paths[]' "$RUNNER_TEMP/plan.json")
          if [ "${#paths[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            uv run --script "$CLI" init "${paths[@]}"
          fi

      - name: Direct bumps (commit to the default branch)
        run: |
          mapfile -t names < <(jq -r '.direct[].name' "$RUNNER_TEMP/plan.json")
          [ "${#names[@]}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "no direct children"; exit 0; }
          before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          uv run --script "$CLI" pull "${names[@]}"
          uv run --script "$CLI" bump "${names[@]}" --commit --subject "chore(submodules): auto-bump ${names[*]}"
          if [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" != "$before" ]; then
            git push origin "HEAD:$DEFAULT_BRANCH"
          fi

      - name: PR bumps (fixed branch)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          mapfile -t names < <(jq -r '.pr[].name' "$RUNNER_TEMP/plan.json")
          [ "${#names[@]}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "no pr children"; exit 0; }
          before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          git switch -C "$BUMP_BRANCH"
          uv run --script "$CLI" pull "${names[@]}"
          uv run --script "$CLI" bump "${names[@]}" --commit
          if [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$before" ]; then
            echo "pr children already up to date"
            exit 0
          fi
          git push --force origin "$BUMP_BRANCH"
          state=$(gh pr view "$BUMP_BRANCH" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            gh pr create --base "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" --head "$BUMP_BRANCH" \
              --title "chore(submodules): bump tracked children" \
              --body "Automated by superproject-bump. The commit body lists each child's range and \`--submodule=log\`. PRs opened with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger other workflows; run checks manually if needed."
          fi

# Plan: `superproject-workspace` skill

## Context

In AI-assisted development an agent often needs one entry point with context and edit access across many repos. A real monorepo couples the repos too tightly. A **superproject of git submodules** keeps them decoupled, but it drifts over time:

- child PRs merge and the gitlink silently falls behind
- children sit detached or dirty
- a pointer can reference an unpushed commit
- worktrees get messy
- each superproject grows its own ad-hoc justfile

The user has two working examples, which follow two different patterns:

- **dotfiles-all** is an *umbrella*. All 5 children are owned by the user and track `main`. Strong points: the `gitlink-preflight` check that a commit is reachable from `origin/main`, the ff-only `submodule-pull-main`, and inside-out commits. Weak points: no scheduled bump, 5 hard-coded paths, and every recipe duplicated for sh and pwsh.
- **Tadronaut-Mono-Repo** is a *workspace hub*. Children are tiered core/personal/references. Lazy init happens through `scripts/init_submodules.py`, and gitlinks are reproducible pins ("latest ≠ reset to main"). Experiments run in external worktrees, and a `context/` knowledge graph lives at the root. Weak points: no rule for when a pin moves forward, and no report of how far behind each child is.

The user has more, older and less agentic superprojects. The goal is one skill that encodes best practice for both patterns, and that can audit and upgrade the existing repos.

## Decisions (agreed with the user)

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Scope | Cover both patterns with one **per-submodule policy**. An umbrella is the special case where every child is `track`. |
| Policy storage | Custom keys in `.gitmodules`, read and written with `git config -f .gitmodules` |
| Bump mode | Each submodule chooses: `pr` (scheduled CI opens a PR), `direct` (CI commits to main after preflight), or `manual` |
| Worktrees | Child feature branches go in `.worktrees/<sub>/<branch>`, created from the child's own gitdir and gitignored. They stay inside the agent's entry point. Never use superproject worktrees. |
| No-submodule alternative | Covered by the decision guide only: manifest + gitignored clones, or Claude/Codex Project add-dir |
| Tooling | One PEP 723 Python CLI run via `uv run`. It works cross-platform, which removes the duplicate sh/pwsh recipes. Thin justfile wrapper, `--json` and `--dry-run` on every subcommand. |
| Adoption | `audit` (read-only) plus `adopt` (writes policy keys, AGENTS.md block, recipes, optional CI) |
| Deliverable | The skill, plus a list of improvements for the two example repos. Those repos are not modified in this task. |

### `.gitmodules` schema

```ini
[submodule "tarlin"]
    path = submodules/tarlin
    url = https://github.com/tadronaut/tarlin.git
    branch = main          # native git key; the tracking branch
    x-policy = track       # track | pin | lazy
    x-bump = pr            # pr | direct | manual   (pin/lazy => manual enforced)
    x-tier = core          # free-form grouping: core | personal | reference | ...
    update = none          # set for lazy: native git skip on plain `submodule update`
```

Semantics:

- `track`: may follow `origin/<branch>` by fast-forward only.
- `pin`: moves only on an explicit `bump --reason`. The reason goes into the commit body.
- `lazy`: not initialized by default and never bumped automatically. It is initialized on demand without recursion.

## Skill layout: `skills/local/superproject-workspace/`

- `SKILL.md`
  - when to use it
  - the core invariant: a gitlink is a commit, not a branch, so drift is expected and must be made visible and machine-bumped
  - policy table, daily workflows (start / develop in a child / bump / review)
  - gotchas
  - CLI quick reference
- `scripts/superproject.py` (PEP 723, stdlib only, Python ≥3.10). The subcommands:
  - `status [--fetch] [--json]`: for each submodule, shows policy and tier, whether it is initialized, gitlink vs HEAD, branch or detached, dirty, ahead/behind `origin/<branch>`, whether the gitlink is reachable from origin, and its worktrees.
  - `init [--tier T] [names…] [--recursive]`: policy-aware init. Lazy submodules are initialized only by name or tier, using `--checkout` to override `update=none`.
  - `pull [names…]`: fast-forwards `track` submodules. It reuses the dotfiles-all safety rules: refuse on diverged branch, unreachable detached commit, or dirty tree. It refuses `pin` unless `--force`.
  - `bump [names…|--all-track] [--reason] [--commit] [--dry-run]`: runs preflight, stages the affected gitlinks together, and creates **one outer commit** whose message includes the `--submodule=log` summary.
  - `preflight`: checks that staged gitlinks are clean, pushed, and reachable from `origin/<branch>`. It also serves as the pre-commit hook.
  - `worktree add|list|remove <sub> <branch> [--base REV]`: manages `.worktrees/<sub>/<branch>` and ensures the `.gitignore` entry exists.
  - `audit [--json]`: reports
    - missing policy keys
    - drift and lag
    - unreachable pointers
    - stale worktrees
    - missing AGENTS.md block
    - hard-coded submodule paths in the justfile
    - missing CI for `pr`/`direct` submodules
  - `adopt [--dry-run] [--policy-default …] [--with-ci]`: writes policy keys, inserts the marker-delimited AGENTS.md block, adds the justfile snippet and `.gitignore` entry, and optionally the workflow.
  - `ci-plan --json`: emits the `pr` and `direct` bump sets for the workflow.
- `assets/`
  - `justfile.snippet`: thin recipes that call the CLI
  - `agents-block.md.template`: the cross-repo contract. It covers reading the child's AGENTS.md first, committing inside-out, one outer pointer commit per cross-repo change, and "latest ≠ reset pins". Marker-delimited, like project-knowledge-harness.
  - `superproject-bump.yml`: scheduled plus `workflow_dispatch`. It runs `ci-plan`. `pr` submodules go to a fixed branch `chore/submodule-bump`, using the same pattern as this repo's `.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml`. `direct` submodules push to main after preflight.
  - `child-dispatch.yml`: optional, for an immediate bump through `repository_dispatch`
  - `pre-commit-hook.sh`
- `references/`
  - `decision-guide.md`: when to choose a real monorepo, a submodule superproject, a manifest with gitignored clones, or Project add-dir
  - `policies.md`: the policy model with examples of umbrella vs hub configurations
  - `worktrees.md`: explains why superproject worktrees fail (each needs every submodule re-initialized) and gives the child-worktree recipe
  - `ci-bump.md`: tokens and deploy keys for private and GitLab children, and the `GITHUB_TOKEN` → no-validate pitfall already documented in CLAUDE.md
  - `agent-entry.md`: AGENTS.md layering, Claude/Codex Projects, and a root `context/` directory
  - `gotchas.md`, grep-able by symptom. Covers:
    - "modified: sub (new commits)"
    - detached HEAD after update
    - `git pull` not updating submodules / `submodule.recurse`
    - nested private submodules
    - a URL changed without running `submodule sync`
  - `case-patterns.md`: anonymized umbrella and hub patterns. No private repo names, customers, or hosts, because this repo is public.
- `tests/test_superproject.py`: unittest against temporary local bare-repo fixtures. Covers status, pull refusal cases, bump/preflight unreachable detection, lazy init, worktree add/remove, and audit/adopt idempotency.

## Repo integration (per CLAUDE.md)

- Open a GitHub issue first, then `bash skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh start <n>`.
- Scaffold with `bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks superproject-workspace`. It is downstream-only, so it gets no `.claude/skills` link.
- Add `./local/superproject-workspace` to the `version-control` plugin in `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
- Add bilingual docs pages `docs/skills/superproject-workspace.md` and `.zh-TW.md`, following existing pages such as `docs/skills/agent-history-hygiene.md`. Add a nav entry if mkdocs.yml lists the pages explicitly.
- Cross-link from `skills/local/git-workflow/references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md` and from forge-native-dev's `coexistence.md`.
- Finish with `forge-worktree.sh finish <n>` and squash-merge the PR.

## Improvement checklists (delivered as a report, not applied)

Write `backlog/superproject-workspace-adoption.md`. It holds generic checklists only; private details stay out.

- **dotfiles-all**:
  - add `x-policy=track` and `x-bump` keys
  - replace the 5 hard-coded paths and the duplicated sh/pwsh recipes with CLI calls
  - add a scheduled bump workflow
  - remove the stale `dotfiles` path in the `submodule-diff` pathspecs
- **Tadronaut**:
  - map core → `pin`/`track` and personal/references → `lazy`, so that `update=none` replaces most of `init_submodules.py`
  - add `status` lag reporting
  - move external worktrees to `.worktrees/`, or keep them and document why
  - keep `context/` as is
- **Older superprojects**: run `audit`, then `adopt --dry-run`.

## Verification

1. `uv run skills/local/superproject-workspace/scripts/superproject.py --help`, plus each subcommand's `--help`.
2. `uv run python -m unittest skills/local/superproject-workspace/tests/test_superproject.py -v`. This covers the fixture superproject with track, pin, and lazy children.
3. Read-only smoke test on local clones of dotfiles-all and Tadronaut: `status --json` and `audit` must report sensible results, and `adopt --dry-run` must show a plausible diff without writing anything.
4. `make validate`, which covers frontmatter, marketplace, and TODO format. Also `make docs-build`.
5. Lint the CI template with `actionlint` if it is installed.

# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
```

Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):

| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
|---|---|---|
| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
> out without further prompting.

After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
follow-up actions deterministically.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent fre

... [19824 characters truncated] ...

ipts/new-skill.sh` supports three placement scopes that mirror the
behavior of `npx skills add` (`vercel-labs/skills`). Auto-detection
precedence (when no flag given):

1. **LOCAL** — publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml`, `skills/local/`, or
   `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) found walking up. This is the
   default *inside this very repo*. Canonical content lives in
   `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with
   `--vendor`); the script adds the `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`
   discovery symlinks for you.
2. **PROJECT** — a git root found walking up. Canonical content goes to
   `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents like Cursor / Codex /
   OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot read this directly); a relative
   symlink `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>` is
   added for Claude Code, plus links for any other non-universal agent dir
   (e.g. `.windsurf/`, `.continue/`) that already exists at the repo root.
3. **GLOBAL** — neither anchor found, or `--global` forced. Same shape as
   PROJECT but rooted at `$HOME`: canonical at `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`,
   plus `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and any other already-present
   `~/.<agent>/skills/` link.

The fan-out rule is "claude-code always, others only if their config root
already exists at the base dir" — this mirrors `npx skills add`'s
"don't create `.windsurf/` unless the project already uses Windsurf"
behavior. The script never creates a new top-level agent home dir.

Symlinks are always *relative* with a fixed `../../` prefix because both
the link's parent (`.../skills/`) and the canonical dir
(`.../.agents/skills/` or `.../skills/local/`) are exactly two levels under
the base dir. See [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md)
for the historical bug this convention prevents.

## Skill discovery

The `skills` CLI looks for `SKILL.md` files like this:

1. **First pass:** one level deep — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
2. **Fallback:** recursive up to **5 levels** if first pass found nothing
   useful.

That's why `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md`
both work — they're 2 levels deep, well within the recursive fallback. **Don't
nest a skill more than 5 levels deep** or it becomes invisible.

## Scripts naming and mirroring

Some scripts are bundled into a skill **and** mirrored to `scripts/` at repo
root. The pattern:

| Canonical location | Mirror |
|---|---|
| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/add-todo.sh` | `scripts/add-todo.sh` |
| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` | `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` |
| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/promote-todo.sh` | `scripts/promote-todo.sh` |
| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/todo-kanban.sh` | `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` |

Reason: the canonical copy travels with the skill (downstream consumers get it
via `init.sh`). The root-level mirror is for *this* repo's own use so `make`
targets and CI don't have to know the skill's path.

**Mirrors must stay byte-identical.** If you edit one, run the equivalent
`cp` to update the other and verify with `diff`. There is currently no
automated check for this — be careful.

## Documentation

- `README.md` — short repo entrypoint with install snippet.
- `docs/` — built into a MkDocs Material site at
  `https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/`.
- `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` — user-facing docs for each local skill. Link
  back to the canonical SKILL.md on GitHub via absolute URL (see linking rules
  in `docs/reference/docs-stack-recipe.md`).

When you add a new local skill, also add:

1. A row to `docs/skills/index.md`.
2. A `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` page (can be short; cross-link to SKILL.md).
3. A nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`.
4. A row to the README's "What's in here" table.

## Project memory

This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` skill on itself. That means:

- `TODO.md` is structured (P1/P2/P3/P?/Done sections, validated by
  `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`).
- `backlog/inbox.md` is the loose-capture inbox.
- `backlog/<slug>.md` holds research notes for non-trivial items.
- `pitfalls/<slug>.md` holds debugging traps with symptom-first titles.

When authoring a skill, if you discover a non-obvious trap, write it to
`pitfalls/`. Don't bury it in commit messages or chat history.

## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md

`AGENTS.md` is a **symlink** to `CLAUDE.md`. Edit either one. Don't replace
the symlink with a real file or they'll drift.

## Bash compatibility

All bundled scripts must be **bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). See
`script-design.md` § "Bash 3.2 compatibility" for the safe subset and
escape hatches.

## When this repo's conventions conflict with agentskills.io

The agentskills.io best practices are upstream / generic; this file is local /
specific. When they conflict, this file wins **for skills authored

# Coexistence with Other Skills

## Decision tree

```
Is there a GitHub/GitLab remote?
├── No  → use git-workflow (+ optionally project-knowledge-harness)
└── Yes → is gh/glab installed and authenticated?
    ├── No  → use git-workflow (recommend installing the CLI)
    └── Yes → does the user prefer local-first or hosted-first?
        ├── Local-first  → project-knowledge-harness + git-workflow
        └── Hosted-first → forge-native-dev (this skill)
```

## forge-native-dev vs git-workflow

| Aspect | git-workflow | forge-native-dev |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Git mechanics (commits, branches, merges) | Forge lifecycle (issues, PRs, cleanup) |
| Requires | git | git + gh/glab |
| Branching | `feat/`, `fix/`, `agent/` | `issue/<N>-*`, `agent/issue/<N>-*` |
| Worktrees | Generic parallel isolation | Issue-linked, auto-created/destroyed |
| PR creation | Delegate to `create-pull-request` skill | Built-in via `forge-worktree.sh finish` |
| Branch cleanup | `branch-status.sh` (diagnosis) | `forge-cleanup.sh` (diagnosis + action) |
| Backlog | Not covered (defer to PKH) | Issues on the forge |

### If both are installed

On first ambiguous operation, the agent asks the user's preference.
Default: `forge-native-dev` for anything involving the remote.

`git-workflow` is still useful for:
- Commit message conventions (Conventional Commits)
- AI provenance trailers (`AI-Assisted-By`, etc.)
- SemVer release tagging
- The lazygit cheatsheet

These don't conflict with `forge-native-dev`. The overlap is specifically
in branching, PR creation, and cleanup.

**Recommendation**: install both, let `forge-native-dev` handle the forge
layer, and `git-workflow` handle the commit/release layer.

## forge-native-dev vs project-knowledge-harness

| Aspect | project-knowledge-harness | forge-native-dev |
|---|---|---|
| Backlog | `TODO.md` (file-based, portable) | Issues (hosted, collaborative) |
| Research | `backlog/*.md` (in-repo) | Local research docs; Discussions only for ongoing shared input |
| Pitfalls | `pitfalls/*.md` (in-repo) | `pitfalls/*.md` (in-repo — same) |
| Visualization | `todo-kanban.sh` | GitHub Projects / GitLab Boards |
| Cross-referencing | Manual links | Auto-linked |
| Offline access | Full | Limited to cached data |
| td integration | Yes (optional) | Optional local execution/handoff state, not a duplicate shared backlog |

### One shared backlog, not two competing indexes

Mirroring the same actionable backlog into both `TODO.md` and Issues creates
drift. Local research notes and task execution state are different: they can
support a hosted backlog without creating duplicate external records. Check the
repository's declared policy before proposing a migration merely because local
files or multiple skills are present.

### Migration: PKH -> forge-native-dev

1. **Run `forge-init.sh`** to set up the forge-native workflow.

2. **For each active `TODO.md` item**, create an Issue:

   ```bash
   # Example: migrate a P2 item
   bash scripts/forge-issue.sh create \
     --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
     --body "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative.

   Migrated from TODO.md P? lane." \
     --label "backlog" --label "priority/P3"
   ```

3. **For `backlog/*.md` research docs**:
   - Keep the files; link relevant evidence from an existing Issue/PR if useful.
   - Create a Discussion only for a still-open question needing asynchronous
     input. Document length alone is not a publication criterion.

4. **Keep `pitfalls/`** in-repo — they need grep-ability.

5. **Remove PKH guidance** from `AGENTS.md`:
   Delete the block between `<!-- project-knowledge-harness:... -->` markers.

6. **Optionally remove `TODO.md`** once all items are migrated.
   Keep `backlog/` and `pitfalls/` directories.

### Migration: forge-native-dev -> PKH

If you decide to go back to local-first:

1. Export open issues to `TODO.md` entries
2. Run PKH's `init.sh`
3. Remove forge-native-dev guidance from `AGENTS.md`

## forge-native-dev vs create-pull-request (vendored)

The vendored `create-pull-request` skill is a standalone PR creation guide.
`forge-native-dev` includes PR creation as part of its lifecycle
(`forge-worktree.sh finish` and `forge-pr.sh create`).

If both are installed, prefer `forge-native-dev`'s PR flow because it
automatically links the PR to the originating issue.

## forge-native-dev in a submodule superproject

If the repo is a superproject (`.gitmodules` present), use the two skills at
different levels:

- **forge-native-dev** handles issues and PRs in each child, in that child's
  own forge. Superproject issue worktrees (`.worktrees/issue-<n>`) are only for
  changes to outer content.
- **superproject-workspace** handles pointer policy, child worktrees under
  `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch>`, and the preflighted bump commit that
  records merged child work in the superproject.

## Role model

The skill distinguishes two roles based on actual repository permissions,
not repo ownership:

| Role | Who | Detection |
|---|---|---|
| **Maintainer** | Repo owner, org member with write access, collaborator with push | GitHub: `repo.permissions.push == true`; GitLab: `access_level >= 30` (Developer+) |
| **Contributor** | Fork-based contributor, read-only org member, guest | Everything else |

This means a core developer in an organization who has write access is
correctly detected as `maintainer` — they can create labels, assign issues,
and merge PRs, even though they didn't create the repo.

### Override

If auto-detection gives the wrong answer (e.g., API rate-limited, SSO
not configured):

```bash
# At init time
forge-init.sh --role maintainer

# At runtime (env var)
export FORGE_ROLE_OVERRIDE=maintainer
```

### What changes by role

| Action | Maintainer | Contributor |
|---|---|---|
| `forge-init.sh` creates labels | Yes | Skipped |
| `forge-issue.sh backlog` applies priority labels | Yes | Priority noted in body text |
| `forge-worktree.sh start` assigns issue + adds label | Yes | May fail silently (no write access) |
| `forge-pr.sh merge` | Yes | Cannot merge (expected — maintainer merges) |
| Issue templates scaffolded | Yes | Yes (they're just repo files) |
| Git config set | Yes | Yes (local config only) |

## Detecting which workflow is active

Agents can detect the active workflow by checking for sentinel markers:

```bash
# PKH is active if TODO.md has lane headers
grep -q '^## P[123?]' TODO.md 2>/dev/null && echo "PKH active"

# forge-native-dev is active if AGENTS.md has its sentinel
grep -q 'forge-native-dev:guidance' AGENTS.md 2>/dev/null && echo "forge-native-dev active"

# git-workflow is active if its commit template is configured
git config commit.template 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'git-workflow' && echo "git-workflow active"
```
